story.skycraft.q.lw_t_falls_a.find: A pilgrim's notebook left on a flat rock: eight falls named, six crossed out with the date and a single word, 'hushed'. 'Tonight: the pool at Mist Mirror. Do not be near the water when it stops.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_falls_a.o0.text: Stand at the base of Waterdancer Falls when the water falls silent.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_falls_a.o1.text: Wait at the waterfall court of Tor Hame Khard for the hush.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_falls_a.o2.text: Sit beneath the aqueduct's arches on the night the channel stops.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_falls_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The hush has moved from falls and aqueducts to a lava-cascade, a weeping inn, an ice seam and finally to the Black Marsh falls.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_falls_a.pitch: A pilgrim says the waterfalls are falling silent in order, one a night, and nobody can stop it.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_falls_a.title: The Silent Falls
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_falls_b.desc: The hush has moved from falls and aqueducts to a lava-cascade, a weeping inn, an ice seam and finally to the Black Marsh falls.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_falls_b.o0.text: Visit the lava-cascade's grotto at Molag Mar the night it falls silent.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_falls_b.o1.text: Sit beside the weeping giant's cheek and listen as the tears slow.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_falls_b.o2.text: Visit the stalhrim basin at the hush and note the hum's pitch.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_falls_b.o3.text: Climb to the weeping falls and face the coven before the last verse.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_falls_b.outro: I stood in the spray of the last falls as the water dropped to a whisper and the wamasu in the rock began to weep. The coven's eighth verse was unfinished. I sang the other eight from memory, in the old tongue. The water remembered its voice.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_falls_b.pitch: A pilgrim says the waterfalls are falling silent in order, one a night, and nobody can stop it.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_falls_b.title: The Silent Falls (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_a.desc: A debt-slip in a sugar-urn with a crescent-and-ledger watermark: 'Do not pay the farmer. Pay the Counting-House.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_a.find: A sugar-urn at the meadow's edge holds a debt-slip folded around a coin. The slip bears a watermark: a crescent moon and a ledger. 'Purchased. Do not pay the farmer. Pay the Counting-House.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_a.o0.text: Trace the farm's purchased debt to the sugar-port's counting-room.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_a.o1.text: Open the Counting-House's branch behind a Senchal sugar warehouse.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_a.o2.text: Take the caravan-mother's debt-slips to the next town on the trade-road.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_a.o3.text: Follow the debt-slips from Rawlkha's lantern market north into Cyrodiil.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The slips' trail runs from sugar farms and Khajiit caravans through river and lake towns to a stilt-market in the Bitter Coast.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_a.pitch: A farmer says her debts were bought by a house she has never met, and that its slips bear a moon.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_a.title: The Sugar Road
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_b.desc: The slips' trail runs from sugar farms and Khajiit caravans through river and lake towns to a stilt-market in the Bitter Coast.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_b.o0.text: Trace the Crescent Ledger's river-agents in Bravil's flooded cellars.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_b.o1.text: Take the ledger's night-boats from the Lunar Fang Docks toward Morrowind.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_b.o2.text: Break the Counting-House's silt-strider ledger-room in Balmora.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_b.o3.text: Open the strongbox beneath the Gnaar Mok stilts and face the Pale Lender.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_b.outro: The strongbox rose out of the mud on its chain, heavy with years instead of gold. I opened it, and I read the names, and I burned the slips one by one. I do not know how many were freed. I know I burned them all.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_b.pitch: A farmer says her debts were bought by a house she has never met, and that its slips bear a moon.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_sugar_b.title: The Sugar Road (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_a.desc: A scale-mosaic tile bears a navigator's tide-glyph: 'One of nine. Read at low tide only.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_a.find: A scale-mosaic tile at the temple's threshold bears an unfamiliar tide-glyph and a navigator's mark. Scratched into its edge: 'One of nine. Seek the other eight. Read at low tide only.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_a.o0.text: Find the harbour's hidden ledger-page behind its sealed manifest.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_a.o1.text: Read the lighthouse's treaty plate for a tide-glyph and carry it north.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_a.o2.text: Pry open the wreck's bow-chest for a ledger page among the barnacles.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_a.o3.text: Search Firsthold's lighthouse for the fourth page, hidden in its lens-case.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The ledger's nine pieces lie in ports from Hammerfell and Solstheim to the Maormer isles and Yokuda.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_a.pitch: A serpent-priest says the tile came from a ledger torn in nine, each piece hidden in a different sea.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_a.title: The Tide-Ledger
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_b.desc: The ledger's nine pieces lie in ports from Hammerfell and Solstheim to the Maormer isles and Yokuda.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_b.o0.text: Take the fifth page from the keeper's totem and look for the Maormer's copy.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_b.o1.text: Consult the sea-king's window for the sixth page and the Maormer's secret.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_b.o2.text: Bring the gathered pages to the Ra Gada drill-master and ask his counsel.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_b.o3.text: Lay the nine pages on the funeral barge and read the ledger's tide.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_b.outro: In the sunken temple's hall I laid the ninth page against the other eight and a chart of tides unfolded across the water. The road home was shorter than I had feared, and stranger. I set the pages back, one in each of nine ports, so no one people would own the road.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_b.pitch: A serpent-priest says the tile came from a ledger torn in nine, each piece hidden in a different sea.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_tide_b.title: The Tide-Ledger (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_a.desc: A census slate at an Alessian gate lists eight light-stones, five of them struck through in a fresh hand.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_a.find: A scholar's census slate leans against the gate-arch: eight stone-names in a column, five struck through in a fresh hand. The last line reads, in Aldmeri: 'Then the Tower.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_a.o0.text: Find the first relit lamp in the Shardiuss pit and follow the cabal's route west.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_a.o1.text: Relight the Miscarcand name-lamp and carry its flame to the Valenwood towers.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_a.o2.text: Relight the Ne Salas pillar and take the cabal's tally on to the star-vault.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The lamps are being relit across the Cyrodiil ruins, the Valenwood vaults and the Tower of the Summerset Isles.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_a.pitch: A scholar at an old gate says someone is taking a census of the Ayleid lamps, and crossing them off.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_a.title: The Welkynd Census
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_b.desc: The lamps are being relit across the Cyrodiil ruins, the Valenwood vaults and the Tower of the Summerset Isles.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_b.o0.text: Relight the star-vault's ceiling and follow the white flame to the burned city.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_b.o1.text: Relight the burned city's cistern lamp and sail for the Crystal Tower.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_b.o2.text: Climb the Crystal Tower to the lens-room where the last stone waits.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_b.o3.text: Face the Lampwright Magister in the vaults beneath the Tower.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_b.outro: I lit the eighth stone with my own hand. The Tower's lens turned slowly and, for the span of a breath, the sky above Summerset showed every star a thousand years gone. The Lampwrights bowed. I did not know what I had begun.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_b.pitch: A scholar at an old gate says someone is taking a census of the Ayleid lamps, and crossing them off.
story.skycraft.q.lw_t_welkynd_b.title: The Welkynd Census (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_1_a.desc: A root-totem studded with glass splinters at the base of the great tree says the crown is thirsty and must be fed names.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_1_a.find: A root-totem at the trunk's base has been drilled with a dozen small holes. In each a pale glass splinter glows faintly. A tag in Bosmer script: 'The crown is thirsty. Feed it names.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_1_a.o0.text: Copy a ring of name-plates from Ne Salas and take it to the star-vault.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_1_a.o1.text: Re-light the dark stars in the Reliquary and take the scroll to Elden Root.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_1_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The lamp's trail dips into an underground tower-city and a star-vault, climbs the tree's capital, and ends in a bone-walled ossuary.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_1_a.pitch: The totem-carvers say the great tree's glow has dimmed one shade each season.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_1_a.title: The Crown Lamp
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_1_b.desc: The lamp's trail dips into an underground tower-city and a star-vault, climbs the tree's capital, and ends in a bone-walled ossuary.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_1_b.o0.text: Open the keepers' hall and read the debate's ballot.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_1_b.o1.text: Read the lamp-warden's name at the lowest tier and relight the crown.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_1_b.outro: I laid the last name in the ossuary's tier and the glow in the crown flickered up like a lit wick. The Pact's keepers will be less grateful than I hoped. The lamp, though, burned bright.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_1_b.pitch: The totem-carvers say the great tree's glow has dimmed one shade each season.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_1_b.title: The Crown Lamp (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_2_a.desc: A charcoal line on an inn's route-board shows the walking city heading in a straight line for a hollow tree.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_2_a.find: An inn's travel-board lists the walking city's seasons, in one column the old route and in another, a new straight line drawn in charcoal, heading for a hollow tree.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_2_a.o0.text: Take the chant tablet from the hermit to the Orc outposts that will help cut.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_2_a.o1.text: Take the Drabul chief's tally to the next outpost at Jathsogur.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_2_a.o2.text: Take the guide-line bearing from Jathsogur to the hidden court at Silvenar.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_2_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The cutters' trail runs through Orc outposts and a hidden court to the walking city and the tree-tomb itself.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_2_a.pitch: The innkeeper says the walking city has stopped wandering and started to march.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_2_a.title: Where the City Walks
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_2_b.desc: The cutters' trail runs through Orc outposts and a hidden court to the walking city and the tree-tomb itself.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_2_b.o0.text: Secure the court seal at Silvenar and join the walking city.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_2_b.o1.text: Sever the walking city's final guide-root at the base of Falinesti.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_2_b.o2.text: Descend the hollow tree and silence the apostates' chant.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_2_b.outro: At the tomb I silenced the chant and the city, far behind me, slowed and began, at long last, to turn. A Pact-warden saw me cut the last guide-tree and said nothing. Some silences are a kind of thanks.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_2_b.pitch: The innkeeper says the walking city has stopped wandering and started to march.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_2_b.title: Where the City Walks (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_3_a.desc: A thorn-wall plaque lists forty Ayleid names with a Bosmer warning never to cut the trees.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_3_a.find: A thorn-wall plaque at the glade's rim lists forty names in a looping Ayleid script, each pricked out with a thorn. Below it, in Bosmer: 'The Mercy. Never be cut. Never be moved.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_3_a.o0.text: Take a leaf from the Woodhearth ring and follow where the trees lean.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_3_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The orchard's roots lean through a hedge-maze toward a burned city.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_3_a.pitch: The thorn-wardens say the trees of Woodhearth are leaning, a finger a year, to the south.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_3_a.title: The Citizens' Orchard
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_3_b.desc: The orchard's roots lean through a hedge-maze toward a burned city.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_3_b.o0.text: Climb the ridge, read the maze as a map and walk it to the burned city's gate.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_3_b.o1.text: Carry the orchard leaf to the cistern lamp and let the citizens go home.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_3_b.outro: I walked the last road with the orchard's leaf in my hand and set it on a melted lamp in the burned city. For an hour the ash-grey terraces were green. The trees will not lean further. They are home.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_3_b.pitch: The thorn-wardens say the trees of Woodhearth are leaning, a finger a year, to the south.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_3_b.title: The Citizens' Orchard (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_4_a.desc: A prayer-stone at the falls has eight notches for the Truce's bones, and the eighth is wet red clay.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_4_a.find: A prayer-stone beside the falls is cut with eight notches for the Truce's bones. Seven are filled in white. The eighth is red clay, still wet, with a thumb-print.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_4_a.o0.text: Learn the seven verses at Sren Ja and take them to the monastery of Dokrin.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_4_a.o1.text: Recover the pressed leaf from the Dokrin library and trace the hand.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_4_a.o2.text: Trace the stolen verse through the Rawlkha market's eleven buyers.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_4_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. Each stop on the trail holds a part of the rite, from a tree village and a monastery to an arena and the bone-white henge.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_4_a.pitch: A priest at Waterdancer Falls says the Truce's eighth bone has not been laid and the two peoples are not speaking of it.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_4_a.title: The Truce of Bones
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_4_b.desc: Each stop on the trail holds a part of the rite, from a tree village and a monastery to an arena and the bone-white henge.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_4_b.o0.text: Convince the Arenthia scholar to return the Truce's eighth verse.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_4_b.o1.text: Dance the eighth step on the Thizzrini sand and carry the full rite to the henge.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_4_b.o2.text: Lay the eighth bone on the altar and renew the Truce.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_4_b.outro: At the henge I laid the eighth bone on the altar, white as the other seven, and the circle's wind dropped. Bosmer and Khajiit stood on opposite sides and, for the first time in a generation, looked at one another.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_4_b.pitch: A priest at Waterdancer Falls says the Truce's eighth bone has not been laid and the two peoples are not speaking of it.
story.skycraft.q.lw_val_4_b.title: The Truce of Bones (II)
story.skycraft.q.main_alduins_bane.desc: With the Elder Scroll I return to the summit of the Throat of the World. At the time-wound, where Alduin was cast out long ago, the Scroll will show me the Shout I need.
story.skycraft.q.main_alduins_bane.o0.te: Return to the summit of the Throat of the World
story.skycraft.q.main_alduins_bane.o1.te: Read the Elder Scroll at the time-wound
story.skycraft.q.main_alduins_bane.o3.jo: Grounded by Dragonrend, Alduin fought like a cornered wolf, and when he was beaten he fled into the sky. He is not dead. Not yet.
story.skycraft.q.main_alduins_bane.title: Alduin's Bane
story.skycraft.q.main_alduins_wall.desc: Esbern believes Alduin's Wall, carved in the lost Sky Haven Temple, shows how the ancient Nords defeated the World-Eater. The temple lies hidden inside Karthspire, in the Reach, where the Forsworn now camp.
story.skycraft.q.main_alduins_wall.o0.te: Meet Delphine and Esbern at Karthspire
story.skycraft.q.main_alduins_wall.o1.te: Clear the Forsworn camp at Karthspire
story.skycraft.q.main_alduins_wall.o3.re: Look, look! The heroes didn't kill him. They cast him out of time, with a Shout made for the purpose.
story.skycraft.q.main_alduins_wall.o4.re: Then go. Take this blade from the old Blades' armory: it was forged for exactly this kind of work. You're one of us now, whatever the Greybeards say.
story.skycraft.q.main_alduins_wall.o4.to: We have to ask the Greybeards about Dragonrend.
story.skycraft.q.main_alduins_wall.title: Alduin's Wall
story.skycraft.q.main_before_the_storm.d: The dragon flew north toward Whiterun. Riverwood asked me to carry word to Jarl Balgruuf and beg him for soldiers; the village has no walls and no garrison.
story.skycraft.q.main_before_the_storm.o: The Jarl sent soldiers to Riverwood. He has another task for me, something about his court wizard and dragons.

A dragon? So the rumors are true. Irileth, send a detachment to Riverwood at once. You've done Whiterun a service, friend. Stay a moment. My court wizard has a task that wants someone with your nerve.
Speak to Jarl Balgruuf in Dragonsreach
Riverwood needs protection. A dragon destroyed Helgen.
Delphine is one of the last Blades, the order that once guarded the Dragonborn emperors. She thinks the dragons are not returning on their own: something is raising them from their mounds. Kynesgrove is next on her map.
That map Farengar copied for me marks every burial mound in Skyrim. If I'm right, a dragon will rise from the one at Kynesgrove. Meet me there. Bring your Voice.
What do you know about the dragons?
By Alduin himself. The World-Eater, out of the old prophecies. I hoped it was a story. The Thalmor will know something; they always do. I have a way into their embassy.
So the dragons are being raised.
story.skycraft.q.main_bleak_falls_barrow: Farengar Secret-Fire, the Jarl's court wizard, believes there is a record of the dragons' resting places carved on a tablet in Bleak Falls Barrow, the old tomb on the mountain above Riverwood.
Help is a strong word. I need legs. In Bleak Falls Barrow lies a carved tablet: the Dragonstone. It maps their burial mounds, I'm sure of it. Bring it to me and the Jarl will pay you.
Speak to Farengar about the Dragonstone
The Jarl says you need help with dragons.
The dead don't stay down in Bleak Falls Barrow. I put four of them back in their alcoves.
Behind the overlord's sarcophagus stood a curved wall carved in claw-marks. One of the marks burned and I knew it: FUS. Force. I can't make it mean anything yet.
Defeat the Draugr Overlord guarding the inner chamber
Take the Dragonstone from the overlord's tomb
Remarkable. A map of mounds, every one marked. My colleague will be delighted. And you should go to the Jarl; a guard just came in shouting about the western watchtower.
story.skycraft.q.main_cornered_rat.desc: Esbern, an archivist of the Blades, is hiding somewhere in the Ratway beneath Riften. The Thalmor are looking for him too.
story.skycraft.q.main_cornered_rat.o1.re: An old man jumping at shadows? Lad, half the Ratway fits that. But there's one locked in the Warrens like he owes the world money. Watch yourself down there; you're not the only one asking.
story.skycraft.q.main_cornered_rat.o1.te: Ask around Riften about the old man in the Ratway
story.skycraft.q.main_cornered_rat.o1.to: I'm looking for an old man hiding in the Ratway.
story.skycraft.q.main_cornered_rat.o3.te: Deal with the Thalmor hunting Esbern
story.skycraft.q.main_cornered_rat.o4.re: Delphine? Alive? Then the world isn't entirely lost. Alduin has come back, and nothing can stop him but a Dragonborn. Take me to her. I know where the Blades hid their secrets.
story.skycraft.q.main_cornered_rat.o4.te: Find Esbern in the Ratway Warrens
story.skycraft.q.main_cornered_rat.o5.te: Bring Esbern to Delphine in Riverwood
story.skycraft.q.main_cornered_rat.o6.re: Old fool, I thought you dead. Esbern says the lost Sky Haven Temple holds Alduin's Wall, the Blades' record of how he was beaten. It's in Karthspire, in the Reach. We go now.
story.skycraft.q.main_cornered_rat.title: A Cornered Rat
story.skycraft.q.main_diplomatic_immunit: Delphine is sure the Thalmor know who is raising the dragons. Their embassy outside Solitude holds a reception tonight, and a friend of the Blades works in the kitchen.
Keep your voice down. I'll smuggle your gear into the embassy kitchen. Get in, find their files, get out. If anyone asks, you've never met me.
The Thalmor don't know who raises the dragons either. But they are hunting an old Blade named Esbern, and their file says he hides in the Ratway beneath Riften.
Search the embassy for the Thalmor's files
But they're hunting Esbern. If that old man is still alive, he knows more about Alduin than anyone living. Find him in the Ratway before they do.
The Thalmor are as lost as we are.
story.skycraft.q.main_dragon_rising.desc: A dragon attacked the western watchtower. The Jarl sent his housecarl Irileth with a band of guards, and asked me to go with them. If a dragon can die, we will learn it today.
story.skycraft.q.main_dragon_rising.o0.t: Join Irileth at the western watchtower
story.skycraft.q.main_dragon_rising.o2.j: When the dragon died, its soul poured into me. The guards say only the Dragonborn of legend could do that.
story.skycraft.q.main_dragon_rising.o3.r: Then the old tales are true. And did you hear the mountain? The Greybeards called a name from High Hrothgar, and I believe it was yours. By my right as Jarl, I name you Thane of Whiterun. Take this axe from my armory. And go to them: one does not keep the Greybeards waiting.
story.skycraft.q.main_dragon_rising.o3.t: The dragon is dead, and I took its soul.
story.skycraft.q.main_dragonslayer.desc: The World-Eater is no more. Paarthurnax will want to hear it from me, on the mountain where it began.
story.skycraft.q.main_dragonslayer.o0.te: Return to the Throat of the World
story.skycraft.q.main_dragonslayer.title: Dragonslayer
story.skycraft.q.main_elder_knowledge.de: I need an Elder Scroll. The only person in Skyrim who might know where one lies is Septimus Signus, a scholar of the Scrolls who lives alone in the ice north of Winterhold.
story.skycraft.q.main_elder_knowledge.o0: Find Septimus Signus north of Winterhold
story.skycraft.q.main_elder_knowledge.o1: The Scroll! Under the earth, in the Dwemer's hidden city, it waits inside the Tower of Mzark. Go down through Alftand into Blackreach. Take this sphere; the tower will listen to it.
Ask Septimus about the Elder Scroll
I'm looking for an Elder Scroll.
story.skycraft.q.main_elder_knowledge.o3: Survive the Falmer and the machines of Alftand
story.skycraft.q.main_elder_knowledge.o6: The tower's lenses focused a beam of starlight, and a cylinder rose from the floor. Inside lay an Elder Scroll.
Take the Elder Scroll from the tower's lens
story.skycraft.q.main_horn_of_jurgen.des: The Greybeards' final trial: recover the horn of their founder from his tomb in Ustengrav, deep in the bogs of Hjaalmarch.
Fight through the depths of Ustengrav
The horn was gone. Someone had beaten me to it and left a note: 'If you want the horn, rent the attic room at the Sleeping Giant Inn in Riverwood. Your friend.'
Go to the Sleeping Giant Inn in Riverwood
The attic? We don't have... Close the door. So you're the one the Greybeards were shouting for. Here's your horn. I needed to see who'd come for it before I trusted them with anything.
Ask the innkeeper about the attic room
I'd like to rent the attic room.
You have passed the trials. Stand with us, and receive the last word of Force: DAH. Push. Let your Voice break what stands before it.
Return the horn to the Greybeards
Here is the Horn of Jurgen Windcaller.
story.skycraft.q.main_paarthurnax.desc: Delphine and Esbern have learned what Paarthurnax is. They demand his death as the price of the Blades' help.
I won't kill him. He taught me, and he's earned his peace.
Then the Blades have nothing more to say to you. I hope you're right about him.
Good. Esbern will see to it that the Blades remember this.
story.skycraft.q.main_paarthurnax.offer: You look like you want to say something, Delphine.
story.skycraft.q.main_paarthurnax.pitch: I'll say it plainly. Paarthurnax is a dragon. He was Alduin's lieutenant once, and he did unspeakable things. The Blades will not help you again until he's dead.
story.skycraft.q.main_paarthurnax.title: Paarthurnax
I agreed to kill Paarthurnax at the Blades' demand. He waits on the summit, as he always has.
Then the Blades stand with you again, Dragonborn. Some debts take a thousand years to collect.
story.skycraft.q.main_season_unending.de: The civil war gets in the way of the fight against Alduin. Arngeir agreed to host a council at High Hrothgar, if both sides come.
story.skycraft.q.main_season_unending.o0: A truce with that rebel? ...If it frees my soldiers to fight dragons, I'll listen. I promise nothing.
Persuade General Tullius to attend the council
The Greybeards are holding a council. You should be there.
story.skycraft.q.main_season_unending.o1: I'd sooner not sit at a table with the Empire's dog. But I owe the Greybeards that much. I'll come.
Persuade Jarl Ulfric to attend the council
The Greybeards want both sides at High Hrothgar.
story.skycraft.q.main_season_unending.o2: Return to High Hrothgar for the council
story.skycraft.q.main_season_unending.of: Could the Greybeards host a truce between Ulfric and Tullius?
story.skycraft.q.main_season_unending.pi: This is a strange request to bring to High Hrothgar. But if the war hinders the fight against Alduin, we will open our doors. Bring them here. Let them talk.
story.skycraft.q.main_sovngarde.desc: Sovngarde. The mist here is Alduin's: he hunts the souls of the dead as they arrive. The heroes who first cast him out wait in the Hall of Valor.
story.skycraft.q.main_sovngarde.o1.text: Follow the old road through the mist and find the heroes of old
story.skycraft.q.main_sovngarde.o2.journ: Alduin is gone. His soul broke apart over Sovngarde like sparks on the wind.
story.skycraft.q.main_sovngarde.o3.text: Ask Tsun at the Whalebone Bridge to send you home (or take the golden way at the misty vale)
story.skycraft.q.main_sovngarde.title: Sovngarde
story.skycraft.q.main_the_fallen.desc: Alduin fled to Sovngarde, through a portal no mortal can reach on foot. Paarthurnax says one of Alduin's own dragons could carry me, if I could trap one. Dragonsreach was built to hold a dragon once. Jarl Balgruuf will need persuading.
story.skycraft.q.main_the_fallen.o0.repl: You want me to invite a dragon into my palace? ...You've never asked me for anything, and you saved this city once already. Very well. The great porch, and the old yoke. Gods help us.
story.skycraft.q.main_the_fallen.o0.text: Ask Jarl Balgruuf to let you trap a dragon in Dragonsreach
story.skycraft.q.main_the_fallen.o0.topi: I need Dragonsreach to trap a dragon.
story.skycraft.q.main_the_fallen.o1.text: Learn from Paarthurnax which dragon to call
story.skycraft.q.main_the_fallen.o2.text: Go to the great porch of Dragonsreach and call the dragon's name
story.skycraft.q.main_the_fallen.o3.jour: Odahviing came, and when he was spent the yoke slammed shut over his neck. Trapped, he offered a bargain.
story.skycraft.q.main_the_fallen.o3.text: Wear Odahviing down until he can be caught in the yoke
story.skycraft.q.main_the_fallen.title: The Fallen
story.skycraft.q.main_throat_of_the_worl: Arngeir must tell me about Dragonrend, though the Greybeards will not thank me for keeping company with the Blades.

That Shout was made from hatred, and we will not teach it. Our master may answer you. Paarthurnax dwells on the summit. Take this Shout to part the winds that guard the path: LOK VAH KOOR. Clear Skies.
Use Clear Skies to part the storm on the path to the summit
Climb to the summit of the Throat of the World
Paarthurnax, master of the Greybeards, is a dragon. He says Dragonrend can only be learned by seeing it, through an Elder Scroll read at the time-wound on this summit.
story.skycraft.q.main_unbound.desc: I woke on the road with smoke on the northern horizon and a black dragon crossing the mountains. Riverwood is the nearest village; they need to be warned.
story.skycraft.q.main_unbound.o0.journal: No one was chasing me. I followed the road toward the nearest village, the dragon's roar fading behind me.
story.skycraft.q.main_unbound.o1.c0.labe: A dragon is burning the north. Riverwood needs to know.
story.skycraft.q.main_unbound.o1.c0.repl: A dragon? Shor's bones. Then Riverwood is next and we have no walls. Take what you need from the mill. And go to Whiterun, tell the Jarl we need soldiers.
story.skycraft.q.main_unbound.o1.c1.labe: I saw a dragon in the north. Riverwood needs to know.
story.skycraft.q.main_unbound.o1.c1.repl: A dragon! The Nine preserve us. Here, take some iron from the forge and something to eat. Someone has to warn Jarl Balgruuf. Will you go?
story.skycraft.q.main_unbound.o1.text: Find help in Riverwood: Gerdur at the mill, or Alvor the smith
story.skycraft.q.main_unbound.title: Unbound
story.skycraft.q.main_way_of_the_voice.d: The Greybeards have summoned me to High Hrothgar, their monastery high on the Throat of the World. The pilgrims' road starts at Ivarstead: seven thousand steps cut into the mountain.
story.skycraft.q.main_way_of_the_voice.o: Begin the climb of the Seven Thousand Steps
So. A Dragonborn appears in our time. Let us see whether the blood speaks true. Show us your Voice.
Use Unrelenting Force before the Greybeards
Use Whirlwind Sprint to pass the gate in the courtyard
Then hear it. In the barrow of Ustengrav lies the Horn of Jurgen Windcaller, founder of our order. Bring it to us. The way is long and the dead do not sleep there.
Ask Arngeir about the final trial
I'm ready for the last trial.
Odahviing agreed to carry me to Skuldafn, a temple in the eastern mountains where Alduin's portal to Sovngarde stands. In return, I set him free.
Fight through the temple of Skuldafn
Open the portal with the dragon priest's staff and step through
story.skycraft.q.mg_arcane_university.de: With a chapter's recommendation in hand, I can present myself at the Arcane University in the Imperial City and ask to be admitted as an apprentice.
story.skycraft.q.mg_arcane_university.o0: Travel to the Arcane University in the Imperial City
story.skycraft.q.mg_arcane_university.o1: He did, in four pages, with diagrams. Before I admit you, tell me what you want from the University. People who don't know tend not to last.
Teekeeus of Chorrol sent a recommendation for me.
story.skycraft.q.mg_arcane_university.o2: Knowledge. Everything the old masters wrote down.
A reader. Good. The Mystic Archives will eat your evenings. Don't let them eat your sleep.
Power. Enough that nothing can threaten me.
Honest, at least. Most who say that end up in a necromancer's cellar or a Guild report. Learn restraint along with the spells.
To protect people. Magic is a tool like any other.
Traven will like you. Try not to let him lecture you about it for more than an hour.
Tell Raminus Polus what you seek at the University
story.skycraft.q.mg_arcane_university.o3: Then welcome. The University is the heart of the Guild, and the Guild is the conscience of Tamriel's magic, or it tries to be. Raminus will keep you busy.
story.skycraft.q.mg_arcane_university.ou: I was admitted to the Arcane University as an apprentice. Raminus Polus warned me that the work would start immediately. He was not exaggerating.
story.skycraft.q.mg_king_of_worms.desc: Mannimarco, the King of Worms, waits in Echo Cave, east of the Imperial City. Traven has charged me with ending him before his Order can strike the University itself.
story.skycraft.q.mg_king_of_worms.o1.tex: Fight through the Order of the Black Worm
story.skycraft.q.mg_king_of_worms.o2.jou: Mannimarco was older than anything I had fought, and the dead rose for him without being asked. He came apart at last into dust and the smell of old paper.
story.skycraft.q.mg_king_of_worms.o3.rep: Then sit. No, sit, before you fall down. There is something the Council and I must say to you.
story.skycraft.q.mg_king_of_worms.o3.tex: Report to Hannibal Traven at the Arcane University
story.skycraft.q.mg_king_of_worms.outro: I destroyed Mannimarco, the King of Worms, in Echo Cave. Hannibal Traven stepped aside and the Council of Mages named me his successor.
story.skycraft.q.mg_king_of_worms.title: The King of Worms
story.skycraft.q.mg_light_of_vahtacen.de: Raminus Polus sent me to Vahtacen, an Ayleid ruin near Lake Rumare, to recover a Welkynd stone from a sealed chamber.
story.skycraft.q.mg_light_of_vahtacen.o0: Travel to the Ayleid ruin of Vahtacen
story.skycraft.q.mg_light_of_vahtacen.o2: The sealed chamber was open when I reached it. Someone had come before me, cut a black worm into the wall, and left the stone where it lay.
Take the Welkynd stone from the sealed chamber
story.skycraft.q.mg_light_of_vahtacen.o3: A black worm carved on the wall? I was afraid of that. The stone is yours to keep for your trouble. The mark you saw is mine to worry about. For now.
Bring the Welkynd stone to Raminus Polus
The stone, intact. But someone had opened the chamber before me.
story.skycraft.q.mg_light_of_vahtacen.of: Do you have work for an apprentice?
story.skycraft.q.mg_light_of_vahtacen.ou: I brought a Welkynd stone back from Vahtacen, but the Order of the Black Worm had been there first. Raminus did not look surprised.
story.skycraft.q.mg_light_of_vahtacen.pi: The Ayleid ruin of Vahtacen, west of the lake, has a chamber our scholars could never open. A colleague swears it holds a working Welkynd stone. Bring one back intact and I will see you advanced. And watch for the dead. Ayleids rarely sleep alone.
story.skycraft.q.mg_necromancers_moon.de: Hannibal Traven believes the Order of the Black Worm makes black soul gems at an altar in Fort Linchal, near Bravil. He wants me to break the ritual on a moonlit night and bring him one of the gems.
story.skycraft.q.mg_necromancers_moon.o1: Wait for nightfall at Fort Linchal
story.skycraft.q.mg_necromancers_moon.o3: Take the black soul gem from the altar
story.skycraft.q.mg_necromancers_moon.o4: Let me see. Yes. I could fill this, you know. With my own soul, poured into a spell no necromancer could withstand. Or we break it here, and fight him as the Guild has always fought. Your counsel?
Bring the black soul gem to Hannibal Traven
The ritual is broken. I have one of their gems.
story.skycraft.q.mg_necromancers_moon.o5: Break it. We won't become what we're fighting.
Spoken like a true member of this Guild. There. Gone. We'll find another way to his door.
Keep it, but only as a last resort.
A last resort it is. I'll lock it in my study and pray I never need it.
Advise Traven on the black soul gem
story.skycraft.q.mg_necromancers_moon.ou: I broke the Black Worm's ritual at Fort Linchal and brought back one of their black soul gems. Among the necromancers' papers was the name of the place where their master waits: Echo Cave.
story.skycraft.q.mg_necromancers_moon.pi: Black soul gems. On certain nights the necromancers' altars catch the moonlight and turn an ordinary gem into a vessel for a mortal soul. They make them at Fort Linchal, near Bravil. Go when the moon is up, scatter them, and bring me one of those gems.
story.skycraft.q.mg_recommendation.desc: Teekeeus, head of the Mages Guild chapter in Chorrol, will recommend me to the Arcane University if I deal with the scamps loose in his library and recover his Concordance.
story.skycraft.q.mg_recommendation.o0.jo: Three scamps, a great deal of smoke, and one very unhappy apprentice. The library will need a new rug.
story.skycraft.q.mg_recommendation.o0.te: Banish the scamps loose in the Chorrol guild hall
story.skycraft.q.mg_recommendation.o2.re: Mostly is more than I hoped for. Welcome to the Guild. My letter will be at the Arcane University before you are. Ask for Raminus Polus, and try not to set anything on fire.
story.skycraft.q.mg_recommendation.o2.to: The scamps are gone. Here is your Concordance, mostly.
story.skycraft.q.mg_recommendation.offer: I'd like to join the Mages Guild.
story.skycraft.q.mg_recommendation.outro: I joined the Mages Guild in Chorrol. Teekeeus has written to the Arcane University on my behalf.
story.skycraft.q.mg_recommendation.pitch: The University only admits those a chapter will vouch for. I will vouch for you, once you help me. An apprentice's summoning went astray and there are scamps loose in the stacks, eating my books. Get rid of them and find my Concordance before they finish it.
story.skycraft.q.mg_recommendation.title: A Matter of Recommendation
Guild mages travelling between chapters have been disappearing on the roads. Teekeeus's own journeyman has not reached Chorrol, and the University suspects the Order of the Black Worm.
Three days late. She was carrying letters for the Arch-Mage. The road east of town runs past an old shepherd's track. Look there, and be ready for company.
The University says your journeyman never arrived.
The journeyman was beyond help. The acolytes had been waiting for the next Guild mage to come along the same road.
Break the necromancers' ambush on the Chorrol road
Search the acolytes for their orders
So is yours, I see. Stay a moment. Raminus should hear this.
Bring the orders to Hannibal Traven
The necromancers have a list of Guild mages. Your name is on it.
The Order of the Black Worm is hunting the Mages Guild, and it answers to Mannimarco, the King of Worms. Traven means to strike first.
story.skycraft.q.mp_dro_mathra.desc: Moongrave Fane, an old temple west of Torval, has fallen silent. Azadhi believes the Dro-m'Athra, Khajiit spirits lost to the darkness between the moons, have claimed it.
story.skycraft.q.mp_dro_mathra.o0.reply: Moongrave Fane has gone dark. Its keeper's censer burned for three hundred years and now it does not. Only the Dro-m'Athra put out a light like that. Go, and if the censer can be lit again, bring it to me.
story.skycraft.q.mp_dro_mathra.o2.text: Send the Dro-m'Athra back into the dark
story.skycraft.q.mp_dro_mathra.o3.journa: Ash-Whisker had been the Fane's keeper once. I could see the old priest's cord still around its neck, gone black as the rest of it.
story.skycraft.q.mp_dro_mathra.o3.text: Destroy the Dro-m'Athra who snuffed the censer
story.skycraft.q.mp_dro_mathra.o5.reply: Then he is home now, or closer to it. Look, the censer remembers.
story.skycraft.q.mp_dro_mathra.o5.text: Bring the censer to Azadhi in Torval
story.skycraft.q.mp_dro_mathra.o5.topic: The Fane is cleansed. Its keeper was among them.
story.skycraft.q.mp_dro_mathra.outro: I cleansed Moongrave Fane of the Dro-m'Athra, including the lost spirit of its own keeper, and brought the temple's censer back to Azadhi, who lit it again.
story.skycraft.q.mp_dro_mathra.title: Children of the Dark Moon
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.desc: Jo'vassa, an old Khajiit pilgrim, asked me to walk with him from Torval to the Moon Temple in the hills, where he means to give thanks for his grandson's birth.
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.o0.tex: Escort Jo'vassa to the Moon Temple
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.o1.jou: The bandits had a senche-tiger on a chain. When its keeper fell, it simply lay down and purred. Jo'vassa fed it a sugar cake.
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.o1.tex: Drive off the bandits waylaying pilgrims
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.o2.rep: Terrible, and full of gratitude. This one will pray for his grandson, and then for you. Tell Hadoba that Jo'vassa says you walk well.
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.o2.tex: See Jo'vassa to the temple steps
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.o2.top: You made it. How are the knees?
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.offer: You look like you could use company on the road.
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.outro: I escorted the pilgrim Jo'vassa safely to the Moon Temple, clearing the bandits who prey on the faithful along the way.
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.pitch: Company, and a sword to go with it. This one is walking to the Moon Temple in the hills to give thanks for a grandson. The road is full of bandits who think pilgrims carry gold. This one carries only sugar cakes, but bandits do not ask first.
story.skycraft.q.mp_pilgrims_path.title: The Pilgrim's Path
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_lunar_lattice.de: Skooma-cooks raided the temple's moon sugar fields outside Torval. Hadoba sent me to recover the consecrated sugar before it was boiled into skooma.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_lunar_lattice.o0: Find the skooma-cooks' camp south of Torval
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_lunar_lattice.o1: Two of them were too far gone on their own product to feel the blows. I felt sorry for them, a little, afterwards.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_lunar_lattice.o3: The moons thank you, and so does Hadoba's sweet tooth. Remember: sugar is holy. Skooma is sugar that has forgotten what it is for. So are some Khajiit.
Return the sugar to Moon-Bishop Hadoba
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_lunar_lattice.of: What would you have an Initiate do?
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_lunar_lattice.ou: I broke up a skooma camp outside Torval and returned the temple's consecrated moon sugar to Hadoba.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_lunar_lattice.pi: Moon sugar is the Lattice made solid, the light of the moons caught in a grain. Skooma-cooks have raided the temple fields and carried our sugar to a camp south of the city, to boil it into poison. Bring it home before it is ruined.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.desc: Moon-Bishop Hadoba of Torval agreed to teach me the faith of the Khajiit, beginning with the Riddle'Thar, the divine order of the moons.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.o0.r: Good. Hadoba only sends those who might listen. We will wait for the moons together. They are always late, and always exactly on time.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.o0.t: The Moon-Bishop sent me to walk with you.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.o2.r: Jone and Jode. Masser and Secunda. They move in a pattern, the Lattice, and a Khajiit's shape depends on how they stood at birth. All of us, cathay and senche and the little alfiq, are one people dancing under two lights. That is the first riddle.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.o2.t: The moons are up. What am I looking for?
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.o3.c: That every shape of Khajiit is one people.
Yes. The Riddle'Thar ended our clan wars by reminding us whose children we are. Welcome, Initiate.
That the moons move in a pattern nobody can change.
Hm. Nobody should change. Some try. That is a story for later. Still: welcome, Initiate.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.offe: I'd like to learn the ways of the Moon-Priests.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.outr: I watched the moons rise with Moon-Priest Azadhi and learned the first lesson of the Riddle'Thar. Moon-Bishop Hadoba accepted me as an Initiate.
story.skycraft.q.mp_the_riddle_thar.pitc: Then you must first learn the Riddle'Thar, the order the moons gave our people when we were scattered and quarrelling. It is not difficult. It is only true. Walk with Azadhi under the moons tonight, and come back and tell Hadoba what you saw.
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.desc: Hadoba has sent me to the Moon Temple, where Azadhi will teach me the Two-Moons Dance, the ritual that is also a way of life. Hadoba warns me that the darkness does not like to watch it.
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o1.t: Wait for both moons to rise
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o2.r: Nobody does. That is the point.
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o2.t: I'm ready, though I don't know the steps.
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o3.c: Follow Jone, the bright moon of law and order.
Steady steps. Good. Jone keeps the pattern so the rest of us can stray a little.
Follow Jode, the pale moon of change.
Quick steps. Good. Jode reminds the pattern that it is alive.
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o4.j: The shadow came out of the gap between the moons' light. It did not like being seen. When it fled, the singers did not even miss a note.
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o4.t: Drive off the shadow that comes to break the Dance
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o5.r: Ruin it? Walker, that was the Dance. The darkness always comes to watch. The trick is to keep dancing. Hadoba will hear of this, and then, this one suspects, so will the Mane.
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.o5.t: It's gone. Did I ruin the Dance?
story.skycraft.q.mp_two_moons_dance.outr: I joined the Two-Moons Dance at the Moon Temple and drove off a shadow of Namiira that came to break it. Azadhi says the Mane will hear of it.
story.skycraft.q.mp_voice_of_the_mane.de: The Mane has summoned me to Riverhold. Hadoba warns that Renrijra Krin rebels have been seen near the city, and they would like nothing better than to embarrass the Mane in front of the faithful.
story.skycraft.q.mp_voice_of_the_mane.o1: The Mane knows. The Mane also knows that knives are waiting on the hill road behind the palace. The Renrijra Krin believe a dead priest makes a fine joke. Show them it does not.
story.skycraft.q.mp_voice_of_the_mane.o2: The Laughing Knife laughed right up until the end. I think it was genuine. The Renrijra find a great many things funny that are not.
Ambush the Renrijra Krin on the hill road
story.skycraft.q.mp_voice_of_the_mane.o3: Good. Then come before the moons and the people.
The hill road is clear. No one is laughing.
story.skycraft.q.mp_voice_of_the_mane.ou: I stopped a Renrijra Krin ambush outside Riverhold. Before the moons and the faithful, the Mane named me a Moon-Bishop and one of the Voices of the Mane.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.desc: Well-Keeper Dusk has measured the Basin Well dropping faster at night. Someone is drinking from it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.o0.journal: At dusk, thirty-one fathoms. At dawn, thirty-two and a hand. A single hand of water gone in the dark, three nights running.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.o0.text: Measure the Basin Well at dusk and at dawn
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.o1.journal: The conduit was sound at the well and cracked at the granary. A seam, and a hose, and a second pipe laid in a trench that nobody had dug on any plan.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.o1.text: Find the leak in the clay conduit under the granary
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.o2.text: Take the hidden valve from the second pipe
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.o3.text: Stop the water-thieves at their hidden cistern
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.o4.text: Escort the Well-Keeper with the recovered water to the town
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.o5.c0.labe: Return the cistern to the well. The well comes first.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.o5.c0.repl: Then the well rises, and the granary pays in bread. We are all a little hungrier, but we are alive.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.o5.c1.labe: Split it. Both well and granary get half.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.o5.c1.repl: Then we are all a little thirsty, equally. I find that a better arrangement than I expected.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.o5.reply: Forty families sleeping on that water. The thieves were selling it to a trader and feeding it to the granary at night. I could take the cistern for the well, and let the granary go dry, or I could split it, and both of us go thirsty by morning. It is, I am told, a judgement. I do not feel qualified.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.o5.topic: The thieves are put down. The water is saved. But one cistern supplied a granary that feeds forty.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.offer: You are not thirsty. I can tell. Good. You may be of use.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.outro: The well rose three fingers the next dawn. Nobody believed it. Everybody counted.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.pitch: The well has dropped four fathoms since spring. The rain is not late; it is absent. But a well does not drop four fathoms without help. I have measured it twice and it dropped more at night than by day. Someone is drinking. Come down with me and measure. I trust my own plumb-line less than a stranger's.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_dry.title: The Dry Year
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_steed.desc: Ku-Lasha wants a missing guar found before its merchant owner drinks the inn dry.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_steed.o0.journ: A guar, standing very still in the middle of a camp of ragged tents, being fed dates by three delighted children and looking vindicated.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_steed.o0.text: Follow the guar's tracks east to the camp
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_steed.o1.text: Lead the guar back to the Stable Steed
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_steed.o2.reply: Dates. Of course. Of course it found dates. That animal could find a bribe in a desert. Thank you. I shall add a charge to the merchant's bill: 'for the stress.'
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_steed.o2.text: Tell Ku-Lasha the guar is home
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_steed.o2.topic: Your guar is in the yard. It is being fed dates.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_steed.offer: Do you know guar? Do you know guar manners?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_steed.outro: The guar was returned. The merchant left, and nobody mentioned the dates.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_steed.pitch: A guar of a merchant guest has gone missing from the Stable Steed, and the merchant will not leave until it is found. It is a dull guar. It has eaten first at every meal for six days. I would like it back before the merchant eats the last of my bread. Look east.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_steed.title: The Guar That Ate First
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_verdict.desc: Magistrate Verrus has two farmers and two forged deeds. She needs the true record of the Eastern Cut.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_verdict.o0.jou: A cracked stone archive, a lead tube, and inside it a single strip of parchment with a single line: the Cut belonged to neither farm; it belonged to the road.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_verdict.o0.tex: Search the old Twyllbek ruins for the original grant
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_verdict.o1.tex: Take the lead tube from the archive niche
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_verdict.o2.rep: The road. Then neither farmer owns it and both may use it, which is, I suspect, what they have been doing for fifty years while arguing. I shall write it in the register. A very short ruling. I am delighted.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_verdict.o2.tex: Bring the original grant to Magistrate Verrus
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_verdict.o2.top: The true record. The Cut belongs to the road.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_verdict.offer: Two farmers, one canal, six hours. You will do as an impartial witness.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_verdict.outro: The Eastern Cut is the road's, and both farmers share the last drop.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_verdict.pitch: Two farmers dispute the water of the Eastern Cut. One says it is his by use; the other by deed. I have read both deeds and both are forgeries, and both farmers are honest men who inherited a lie. I need someone to find the true record before I must rule in favour of a lie.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_gd_verdict.title: A Verdict by Weight
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_mortar.desc: Mason Noo's mortar from the old quarry keeps setting in the shape of a hand.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_mortar.o0.jour: A pit of pale sand, a ring of leaning stones, and in the middle a single hand of baked clay, palm up, as if asking for something.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_mortar.o0.text: Visit the old quarry where the mortar sand was dug
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_mortar.o1.repl: A mason's. He fell into the pit on the day the ring broke and was never found. He wants to finish the wall he was building. Set the mortar where he fell, and lay one stone. Just one.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_mortar.o1.text: Ask Elder Teeba whose hand it is
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_mortar.o1.topi: The hand in the quarry. Do you know it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_mortar.o2.repl: One stone. I can do that. I have laid ten thousand. I never thought I would lay one for a ghost. Come, hold the line, and do not breathe near the mortar. It is touchy.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_mortar.o2.text: Tell Mason Noo to lay the one stone
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_mortar.o2.topi: Lay a single stone at the quarry. The hand will be at rest.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_mortar.offer: Can you carry a bag of mortar and keep your mouth shut?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_mortar.outro: The quarry now has one stone laid straight, and no more mortar hands.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_mortar.pitch: I mixed a batch of mortar from the old quarry and it set wrong. It sets in the shape of a hand. Five fingers, every time, whatever mould I use. I have thrown three batches into the swamp. The swamp threw them back. Find out whose hand it was, and why it will not stay buried.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_mortar.title: The Mortar That Remembered
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_rope.desc: Kessa Rope-Walker has a wager on crossing the long rope-walk without touching the rail.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_rope.o0.journa: It was not hard. It was only very high. The posts creaked and the ropes sang, and halfway across I saw, far below, an entire village looking up with a hand over its mouth.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_rope.o0.text: Cross the long rope-walk without touching the rail
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_rope.o1.reply: Without touching the rail! I had five drakes on you falling. I lost four hundred. Here is your share, and my sincere admiration, and a request that you never do that again within my sight.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_rope.offer: Do you have nerve? Do you have good boots? Both, ideally.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_rope.outro: The rope-walk now has a plaque with your name on it. Nobody knows who put it up.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_rope.pitch: A rope-walk is a short bridge in a long argument. Two rebuilders have wagered a week's pay on who can cross the long rope-walk between the ring's broken posts without touching the rail. Both have refused to attempt it themselves. You will cross it for me. I will give you a share of the bet.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_rope.title: The Rope-Walk Wager
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.desc: Rebuilder Pa-Dar wants the ninth stair of the Broken Ring explored. It leads nowhere, and he wants to know why.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.o0.repl: To a gate. A real gate, with a door and a keeper. It was sealed when the ring broke, because what lay beyond it was not meant for the sun. The key is in the mason's old yard, in a jar marked with a spiral. Do not open the gate if you are afraid. Close it again if you are not.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.o0.text: Ask Elder Teeba about the ninth stair
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.o0.topi: Pa-Dar says you remember where the ninth stair led.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.o1.text: Find the stair-key in the mason's old yard
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.o2.jour: Two hundred steps. At the top the stair simply ended; but there was a seam in the air where a gate had been, and the key, in my hand, grew warm.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.o2.text: Climb the ninth stair to the sun-egg ruins
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.o3.text: Fight through what the gate has kept in
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.o4.text: Answer the Warden of the Ninth Gate
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.o5.c0.l: Leave it open. Let the rebuilders read.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.o5.c0.r: Then the ring will be rebuilt with its old knowledge. Some of it will be terrible. Most of it will be tedious.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.o5.c1.l: Close it. Some stairs should lead nowhere.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.o5.c1.r: Then it is shut, and the ring stays a ruin on that side. A stair that leads nowhere is, after all, a kind of peace.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.o5.repl: Open, then. And what is beyond it is not a monster. It is a library, I am told. Of what the ring knew. I can leave it open, and let the rebuilders read. Or close it, and keep it from those who would use what they read. Which is the better ruin?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.o5.text: Return to Pa-Dar and choose the gate's fate
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.o5.topi: The gate is open. It guards something. What do you want done?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.offer: You have steady feet. Good. Steady feet are rarer than steady hands.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.outro: The ninth stair is still a stair. What lies at the top is only partly a secret.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.pitch: There are nine stairs in the ring, and eight lead somewhere. The ninth goes up two hundred steps and stops at the sky. I have wanted to know why since I was a hatchling. Elder Teeba remembers. I do not know whether she will tell. Climb it. Tell me what is at the top. Or what was.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_hs_stairs.title: Stones That Lead Nowhere
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.desc: Keeper Sees-Many-Moons needs a Hist sapling carried by boat through four canals to the eastern grove.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.o0.reply: A boat and a rule: keep to the left of every bend. The fourth canal has an old one living in it, and he is a bad-tempered fellow, but he is not hungry yet. If you startle him, he is. Take this contract; the shrine-keeper will want to see it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.o0.text: Accept the boat from Boatwife Mudtoe
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.o0.topic: The Keeper says you will give me a boat.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.o1.journa: The market stalls were boats, and the boats were stalls; I passed a woman selling eel from a canoe the colour of a ripe plum.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.o1.text: Paddle the first canal past the Canal Market
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.o2.text: Paddle the second and third canals under the rope bridges
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.o3.text: Pass Old Gulper in the fourth canal
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.o4.c0.lab: Plant it in the Tender's Pool. The Hist keeps its own.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.o4.c0.rep: Then the Pool has another voice. It will not forget you, and you will not understand why.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.o4.c1.lab: Sell it to the botanist. The money will feed the city.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.o4.c1.rep: Then the city is fed and the Pool is a little lonelier. I shall not forget you either. I shall not say how.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.o4.reply: Alive, and humming. Good. A choice, now, and one I would rather you made than I. The sapling may be planted in the Tender's Pool, where it will keep the Hist company, or it may be sold to an Imperial botanist who offers a great deal for it. The botanist will not plant it in a pool. He will plant it in a glass box.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.o4.text: Bring the sapling to Keeper Sees-Many-Moons
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.o4.topic: The sapling is alive. The tide is only now turning.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.offer: You are not afraid of water. That is the first requirement.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.outro: The tide turned. The boat was returned. The canals did not say what they thought.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.pitch: A sapling of the Hist must go by boat from the Tender's Pool to the shrine on the eastern grove, along four canals, before the tide turns. It cannot go by road; the Hist dislikes the road. I would carry it myself but the tide has taken my knees. Speak to Boatwife Mudtoe. She will give you a boat and a warning.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_boat.title: A Boat for the Hist
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.desc: Boatwife Mudtoe's cousin Jelu is held by a debt that never shrinks. She wants her free.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.o0.journa: Seven debt-boats moored in a row, each with a mark painted on the prow. In the counting-house, a ledger the length of a canal and a clerk who blinked when I asked for it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.o0.text: Find the merchant's counting-house on the fourth canal
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.o1.reply: A Cyrodiilic factor with friends. He keeps a second ledger in the rafters of the counting-house, under a sack of rice. The first one lies. The second one remembers. If someone happened to burn the first and read the second aloud in the market... well. I cannot say what would happen.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.o1.topic: A merchant with debt-boats. Who is he?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.o2.text: Take the second ledger from the rafters
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.o3.c0.lab: Read it aloud in the market.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.o3.c0.rep: Then every canal knows his name. They will not forget. They are not forgiving.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.o3.c1.lab: Trade it for the freedom of all seven boats.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.o3.c1.rep: Seven boatwomen, free and surprised. It is a quieter victory. I shall have to learn to enjoy it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.o3.reply: Four times. I knew it. Now: we can read it aloud in the market, and the merchant's face will be wiped from the canals. Or we can trade it, quietly, for the freedom of all seven debt-boats. Both are right. One is louder.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.o3.text: Bring the ledger to Boatwife Mudtoe
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.o3.topic: The honest ledger. Jelu's debt, repaid four times.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.offer: Do you believe a person can be owned? I do not. I have been told I am wrong.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.outro: Jelu poled her own boat out of the counting-house canal that evening, and did not look back.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.pitch: My cousin Jelu poled a debt-boat for a rice merchant three years. The debt was forty drakes. She has paid it four times over and the ledger shows it as forty and rising. The merchant says it is the interest. I say it is a trap with a very good accountant. Free her. I do not mind how.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.title: A Boat Owed
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_glass.desc: The botanist paid. Now someone wants to know how the Hist sapling died in the glass.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_glass.o0.reply: It sits in a glass box on my desk. It does not hum. It faces the window. I have, quite unreasonably, begun to talk to it. I need you to take it back before I lose my professional distance.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_glass.o0.text: Meet the botanist at the Legion customs house
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_glass.o0.topic: The botanist has the sapling. Is it well?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_glass.o1.text: Carry the sapling back to the Pool with Boatwife Mudtoe
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_glass.outro: The sapling went back to the Pool, humming faintly. The money was not returned.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_glass.title: The Glass Box
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.desc: The reeds beyond the Dripping Reed whisper at night. Wet-Whiskers thinks a drowned man is asking the way home.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.o0.journa: The whisper said: "East. Left. East. The long way. Is the tide in? East." It repeated all night.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.o0.text: Listen to the reed-bank at midnight
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.o1.journa: At the end of the route, a small pier and a tidy house. A widow on the pier looked at me as if she had been expecting me for a year.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.o1.text: Follow the whispered route to Alten Meerhleel
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.o2.reply: Then we shall send word. A lantern in the window of the reed-bank, lit every night. He will see it. He will go home. Thank you. I think I shall sleep.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.o2.text: Tell Wet-Whiskers where he wanted to go
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.o2.topic: He was lost. He wanted to go home to Alten Meerhleel. His wife is still waiting.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.offer: Do you sleep? I do not. The reeds are talking.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.outro: The reeds no longer whisper. A lantern burns in the bank each night.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.pitch: The reed-bank beyond the inn whispers at night. Not a wind-whisper. Words. The guests complain, and I cannot sleep for wondering what they say. A man drowned there last season. I think he is still asking his way home.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.title: Reeds That Whisper
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.desc: The sapling is planted. The Hist asks one more thing, in a voice only the Keeper can hear.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.o0.reply: It asks for a story. Not a prayer. A story, told by someone who has never heard the Hist before. Go to the Dripping Reed and ask Wet-Whiskers for the oldest tale the inn knows. Bring it back.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.o0.text: Ask the Keeper what the Hist wants
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.o0.topic: The sapling is in the Pool. What does it ask?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.o1.reply: That is the tale of the first boat. Nobody knows who built it. It floats on every canal on the same night once a year. Tell the Keeper the boat never sinks. Tell her it never lands. That is the whole tale.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.o1.text: Ask Wet-Whiskers for the oldest tale
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.o1.topic: The Hist wants the oldest tale in your inn.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.outro: The Pool took the tale and was quiet. In the morning, a new leaf had opened.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.title: The Pool Remembers
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.desc: Trader Ocheeva is nine crates of wine short. She suspects the harbour pilot, a Tribune's cousin.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o0.reply: A man with a Cyrodiilic accent and a Legion belt, in a boat with a hidden floor. He sells by the bottle at the Fourth Canal Steps at dusk. I did not tell you that. I did not tell you anything, and the price of not telling is six drakes.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o0.text: Ask Sap-Fence Ruu who sold wine on the canals
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o0.topic: Nine crates of red. Who bought?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o1.text: Catch the pilot at the Fourth Canal Steps at dusk
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o2.c0.lab: Let him pay it back quietly.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o2.c0.rep: Then it is quiet. It is also fair, which surprises me.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o2.c1.lab: Make an example. A public count.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o2.c1.rep: He will stand at the wharf with a sign. It is humiliating. It is also effective. I did not have the nerve myself.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o2.reply: My cousin. Of course. A Legion belt on a rogue is the worst of all disguises. I shall see he pays Ocheeva back, in kind and in coin, and spends a week counting rice on the south wharf. Thank you for not making a scene.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o2.text: Tell Tribune Varro about his cousin
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o2.topic: Your cousin's been selling the Trader's wine.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.offer: You look like you can count bottles and not drink them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.outro: Ocheeva counted forty crates, and sold nine of them at a discount to the man who found them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.pitch: Forty crates of Cyrodiilic red landed at my pier three days ago. Forty crates were delivered to my cellar. In my cellar I count thirty-one. Nine crates have gone for a swim, or a walk, or a sale. I think the pilot, Tribune Varro's cousin, has been 'inspecting' them. Please be gentle. He is a Tribune's cousin.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.title: The Thirsty Bottles
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.desc: Rice-Mother Mussa has a croak under the north paddy and sallow rice.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.o0.journ: At midnight, a bubble rose, and then a head: a bullfrog the size of a washtub, wearing the green-gold collar of a drowned noble. It croaked, regarded me with grave dignity, and sank.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.o0.text: Watch the north paddy at midnight
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.o1.text: Drive the toad-thing from the paddy
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.o2.reply: A noble's collar. How very Cyrodiilic. I shall hang it on the scarecrow, as a warning. Thank you. Eat. You are still too thin.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.o2.text: Tell Mussa the paddy is clear
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.o2.topic: The croak was a bullfrog in a noble's collar. It is gone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.offer: Something croaks under the paddy at night. Not a frog. A frog has a cheerful croak.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.outro: The north paddy greened by the next moon, and the scarecrow wore a collar.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.pitch: The rice grows sallow in the north paddy. By night the water bubbles, and a low croak comes from the mud. A frog, say the children. A drowned man, say the old. I say a drainage problem, and I am a practical woman, but I cannot sleep for it. Look under the paddy.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.title: The Croak Beneath the Paddy
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.desc: Hunter Teek communicates, wordlessly, that the egg-nests of Murkmire have been raided three nights running.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.o0.journa: At dusk, three shapes came out of the reeds: not thieves. Hatchlings, thin and fast, no larger than a hand, hungry enough to take eggs. They took one each and left the rest. They were not greedy. They were starving.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.o1.text: Drive off the true raider, a marsh predator that has been driving the hatchlings from their feeding-grounds
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.o2.reply: Then they will eat from the paddy, and no one shall begrudge them. I shall set out a bowl at dusk. The hatchlings will take it. You will not tell the elder. She will tell me she knew.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.o2.text: Tell Rice-Mother Mussa the hatchlings are fed
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.o2.topic: The hatchlings were hungry. The bully is gone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.offer: ...(Teek holds up three fingers, then points at the reeds.)
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.outro: A bowl is set out at the village edge each dusk. It is always empty by dawn.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.pitch: Teek says nothing. Teek holds up three fingers, then a clutch of eggs, then an empty basket. The nests at the edge of the village have been raided three nights running. Teek does not believe in thieves. Teek believes in hunger. Teek would like you to look.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.title: Hungry Hatchlings
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.desc: Elder Nulaa invites you to walk the Spiral Path of Murkmire in silence.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o0.jour: The path wound three times about the middle. A frog watched me from a reed. Somewhere ahead, a fire crackled, and the mist smelled of cedar and rain.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o0.text: Walk the spiral to its centre and hold your tongue
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o1.c0.r: Then you have answered. Take the coal. Walk it out, and do not drop it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o1.repl: Three questions. The first: what do you carry? The second: what do you leave? The third: where is your door? You need not answer aloud. You need only know.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o1.text: Answer three questions from the elder at the centre
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o2.jour: The coal was warm as a held hand and did not once flicker. Halfway out I passed a child sitting at the path's edge, who looked at me, and at the coal, and smiled, and said nothing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o2.text: Carry the coal back out along the path
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o3.jour: I lit it. The coal went out with a sigh, and the fire it began burned a long time, and kept my hands warm. The mist closed around it like a hand.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o3.text: Light a fire at your own door
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.offer: You are not from the mire. Good. The path does not mind.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.outro: The mire kept your fire. You may find it again, if you stop looking.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.pitch: Every child of the mire walks the spiral once. It is not a trial, it is a listening. You do not speak. You walk it, to the middle, where my fire burns. Then you carry a coal back along the path to your own door and light your own fire from it. Tell no one what the fire says.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.title: The Spiral Path
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.desc: Warden Scales-Her-Chains reports the north ziggurat's sleeping idol gone. Both hills blame each other.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o0.jour: The bridge swayed. Halfway across, a scrap of grey cloth snagged on the rail. A thief with a poor sense of balance.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o0.text: Cross the bridge between the two ziggurats
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o1.repl: Four hundred and twelve ounces, a hair under. A thief would need a sling, not a pocket. Gorge-Eel uses a sling. He is a river man gone wrong. He sleeps in the gorge-caves under the south hill. Here: this is his cord. He tied it at the last job.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o1.text: Ask Stone-Carver Nook about the idol
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o1.topi: The idol is gone. Who knew its weight?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o2.jour: Footprints, a dragged sling, a dropped bandage. The ruins gaped, and in the middle of them sat a man with a stolen idol, rocking it like a child.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o2.text: Chase the thief down the gorge to the old ruins
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o5.c0.l: Return it to the north hill's ziggurat.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o5.c0.r: Then the north hill sleeps well. The south hill will grumble. It is the order of things.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o5.c1.l: Place it on the bridge, between the hills.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o5.c1.r: A bold thing. The bridge will have a god in the middle. Both hills will argue over whose it is. That is an improvement.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o5.repl: The idol is whole. One eye is open. The carver says it was always so; I say it is a new thing, and the south hill carved it. I do not know which of us is right. I could return it to the north hill's ziggurat, as the law says. Or I could place it on the bridge itself, between them, so that neither owns it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o5.text: Return the idol to Warden Scales
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o5.topi: The idol, whole. The thief, down. What now?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.offer: You walk like someone who has never looked down. Good.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.outro: The bridge held. The idol slept. One of its eyes was open, and nobody mentioned it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.pitch: The idol that sleeps in the north ziggurat was gone this morning. Not stolen, I think; borrowed, which in Stormhold is worse. Both hills blame the other. There is a bridge between them, and the thief used it. I want it back before the dusk bell, before the south hill hears and the north hill answers.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.title: The Bridge Between
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.desc: Scout Fast-Eyes watched twelve people enter the White Rose prison dock and eleven leave.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o0.journa: A single lantern in a barred window. A prisoner, an old Argonian, writing on the wall with a splinter. The guards had been told to leave him a lamp.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o0.text: Go to the old White Rose prison dock
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o1.reply: An elder who was convicted of a crime he did not commit, twelve years ago, and has been waiting for someone to ask. He does not wish to leave. He wishes to be asked. Go and ask him. Gently.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o1.text: Ask Warden Scales who the twelfth is
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o1.topic: Who is the twelfth in the White Rose?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o2.reply: Then I have seen it and never asked. A tenth of what I see, and the rest I carry. Thank you. I shall take him a pipe, and a witness.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o2.text: Tell Fast-Eyes what the twelfth wants
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o2.topic: The twelfth wants to be asked.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.offer: I saw something. I will tell you a tenth. That is a lot, for me.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.outro: The old elder left the prison on the arm of a scout who had never before said more than a tenth.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.pitch: From the south tower at dawn I saw a boat on the river carrying twelve people and putting in at the old White Rose prison dock. Twelve went in. Eleven came out. The twelfth did not. I am a scout, not a judge. Go and see. Tell me what the twelfth is doing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.title: A Tenth of What I See
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.desc: Stone-Carver Nook wants to know whether a block carved on the south hill was a gift or a theft.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o0.reply: A third party. A Hlaalu merchant with a rope-rig and a bill of lading nobody read. He sold it to both hills at the same price, on the same day, and left on the evening boat. I did not tell you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o0.text: Ask Pebble-Pocket who sold the block
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o0.topic: A block of north-hill stone ended up on the south hill. Who sold it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o1.journ: A rope-rig, a bill of lading, and a single ledger page with two names and one price. The merchant had sold the same stone twice, to two sides, and was long gone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o1.text: Find the Hlaalu merchant's rope-rig below the south hill
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o2.reply: Both hills paid. Neither is owed. Then it is neither's stone. I shall carve it in half, and set each half on a hill, with a single seam that matches. Let them argue over the seam.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o2.text: Tell Nook the block has two buyers
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o2.topic: Both hills paid for it. The merchant is gone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.offer: Have you ever felt a stone argue with you?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.outro: The seam is visible from both ziggurats, and neither hill will admit to looking at it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.pitch: A block was delivered to the south ziggurat from the north hill quarry, and the south hill has been carving it for a week. It is marked for the north. A mistake, or a theft, or a provocation. The mason on the south side says it is a gift. The north says it is a bribe. I say: I just carve what I am handed. Find out which.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.title: Stone for the Wrong Hill
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.desc: Barge-Mother Seeth cannot row tonight. She needs you to carry a drowned man's urn to the Isle of Tombs.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o0.reply: The lantern keeps the way. Do not let it go out. If it goes out, the passenger will wake, and ask where he is, and you must answer honestly. Take the urn.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o0.text: Take the urn and the lantern
