I do not mind being cheated; it is my profession. I mind being cheated by an amateur. He is at the Bright Scimitar, drinking my money. Go and ask him for it. Be polite. I have found that politeness, with a sword nearby, is very persuasive.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ab_receipt.title: The Fence's Receipt
The arena's books are open and the fixed bout is public. Bookmaker Rim has a sour face.

Ruinous. The honest bettors are back, and the dishonest ones have gone, and I have discovered that I am best at neither. The Arena-Master has put my name on the notice board, in a very large hand. I am to give back eleven hundred. I shall, in instalments, and I shall make them very small. I will tell you this: a fair arena is a duller place. It is also a safer one for a man who owes you a favour.
Visit Bookmaker Rim as the arena opens its books
The books are open. How is business?
The books of the Dragonstar arena are open and Bookmaker Rim pays his debts in small instalments. The seven fights are, at last, seven.
The arena's books are open and the fixed bout is public. Bookmaker Rim has a sour face.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_after_quiet.de: You took the star without opening the arena's books. Gladiator Safiya has thoughts.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_after_quiet.o0: It is a pretty thing. I held it for a night, once, and I put it back, because I did not trust my own hands. You have taken it and left the arena standing. I do not know if you were wise or cowardly. I will say that Dahab has sacked Odalric's partner, and that Rim now takes only honest bets, mostly, and that I have not been paid this quarter. I am content. It is the nearest I have come to happiness in a pit.
Hear Safiya's thoughts on the quiet victory
I took the star quietly. What do you make of it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_after_quiet.ou: The Star of Dragonstar bears a new name, and the arena's books are closed. The seven fights are honest, mostly, and nobody asks.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_after_quiet.pi: You took the star without opening the arena's books. Gladiator Safiya has thoughts.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_beast.desc: A sabre cat refuses to fight in Dragonstar's arena. Armourer Grisha Teth wants it quietly taken to the Taorra Oasis before the beast-master notices.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_beast.o0.text: Wait for night and unlatch the cat's cage behind the arena
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_beast.o1.text: Lead the sabre cat to the Taorra Oasis
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_beast.o2.text: Drive the oasis-hunters from the cat's new home
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_beast.o3.reply: A sabre cat that smiles. Hm. Good. The beast-master will say it escaped. I will say it was sold. Nobody will ask which. Thank you. Take this. It is a collar-plate, and the name on it is not the cat's. It is the first fighter who ever freed an animal, and it was a woman, and her name is lost.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_beast.o3.text: Tell Grisha Teth the cat is free
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_beast.o3.topic: The cat is at the Taorra Oasis. It is drinking, and I believe it is smiling.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_beast.offer: Grisha, there is something wrong with the beast?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_beast.outro: A sabre cat lives by the Taorra Oasis, and is spoken of by caravan drovers as a good omen. The beast-master has stopped asking.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_beast.pitch: The arena's beast-master brought in a sabre cat for the third bout. It will not fight. It sits in the corner of the cage and watches the gate. The beast-master says it is ill. I say it is smart. It is waiting for someone, and I will not be the one to tell the crowd. Take it out. Take it to the Taorra Oasis, where it can go, and be quick, before the beast-master finds out.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_beast.title: The Beast That Would Not Fight
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.desc: Dragonstar's Arena-Master offers a place in the Seven Fights, three tiers of bouts from the pit to the Star. A fixed bout, a bookmaker and a debt of honour lie in wait.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o0.reply: Your name is on the roll. The first tier is the pit. Three bouts, one after another, with no rest between. Wolves first, then bandits, then bears. Win, and you move up. Lose, and Rim collects. Go to the sand.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o0.text: Sign the roll with Arena-Master Dahab
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o0.topic: I sign. Put my name to the roll.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o1.text: Win the first bout of the pit against the wolf pack
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o10.c0.l: Expose it. A fixed arena is a lie told to ten thousand people.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o10.c0.r: Then it is the books, and the names, and a very long winter. Take the Star, and the right to say you did not need the fixed one.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o10.c1.l: Take the star quietly. The arena survives on its faith.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o10.c1.r: Then the star is yours, and the books are closed, and we will both pretend. I do not like it. But I have never been so grateful.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o10.repl: Fixed. In my arena. Under my banner. I have run this place for twenty-two years and nobody has dared. Hm. The purse has the arena seal. That is mine. I shall have to open the books, and I shall have to name names, and half the city will be insulted. Or I can let it lie, and you may take the star as the seventh. What would you have?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o10.text: Bring the Champion's Purse and the truth to Arena-Master Dahab
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o10.topi: Seven fights, or six and a half. The last was fixed. Odalric paid for it. Here is his purse.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o2.text: Win the second bout of the pit against the pit-bandits
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o3.text: Win the third bout of the pit against the bears
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o4.text: Win the fourth bout, the ring, against Brakka the Gate-Crusher
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o5.reply: The next bout is fixed. Not against you, around you. The odds on Horn-Sister Zenda have been moved. I have seen the bookmaker's clerk carry a purse into the pit door. Someone has paid for her to lose, and it is not for your sake. Watch the minotaur. If she pulls her last charge, you will know. Do not say I told you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o5.text: Speak to Gladiator Safiya before the fifth bout
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o5.topic: You have won thirty-one. You said you were the better liar. What do you know about the next bout?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o6.journ: Zenda's last charge slowed a half-beat. She looked at you, once, with an expression you would later recall as apology. Then she dropped her horns and took your blade in her shoulder. The crowd screamed. The bookmaker's clerk smiled.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o6.text: Win the fifth bout, the ring, against Horn-Sister Zenda
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o7.reply: Paid? I do not pay anyone. I merely accept. A man came to me with a purse and said, "Take it, and say nothing." I took it. I said nothing. The man is Odalric, a silent partner, whom nobody has ever seen. I am sorry. I am a bookmaker. I take what is offered.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o7.text: Confront Bookmaker Rim about the fixed bout
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o7.topic: You moved the odds on Zenda. Someone paid her to lose. Who?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o8.text: Win the sixth bout, the Star, against the Unbeaten Basim
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.o9.text: Face Odalric the Silent Partner, who has come to settle the debt
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.offer: Arena-Master, I would like to enter.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.outro: The Star of Dragonstar bears a new name, and the arena bears a new rumour. Rim the Bookmaker offers odds on whether the name will be there next year, and the odds are not good.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.pitch: Seven fights. Three tiers. Three bouts in the pit, against wolves, bandits and bears. Two in the ring, against ogres and minotaurs. Two in the Star, against champions. One body, one name, one chance. If you win seven, you take the star and you are a legend. If you lose, I bury you with honour and sell your gear to pay the bookmaker. Sign here. Do not read the fine print. It is only fine print.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_seven.title: Seven Fights
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_strongbox.desc: Gladiator Safiya wants the arena's tally of what Bookmaker Rim owes her, locked in a strongbox under his stall.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_strongbox.o0.r: Under the stall, in an iron box with three padlocks and a very old lock-pick scratch on the third. It has been picked before, many times, by people who thought he would not notice. He notices. He just has a bad habit of being right about who will not tell. Go at night. He sleeps at the Odds, in the loser's chair by the door.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_strongbox.o0.t: Ask Hanif of the Wounded Odds where Rim keeps his accounts
Safiya says Rim keeps a tally of what he owes the gladiators. Where does a bookmaker keep such a thing?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_strongbox.o1.t: Wait for night and approach Rim's stall
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_strongbox.o2.t: Take the tally from the strongbox under Rim's stall
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_strongbox.o3.r: Large. Yes. Thirty-one bouts, and every one a profit he kept. I shall walk it to the Arena-Master tomorrow, and he will have to pay, or be known as the man who did not. Thank you. Take this. It is not much, but I have been saving it for the day I was free.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_strongbox.o3.t: Give the tally to Gladiator Safiya
The tally was in Rim's strongbox. Your name is in the wrong column, and the sum is large.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_strongbox.offe: Safiya, you said you want out.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_strongbox.outr: Gladiator Safiya has her name in the right column of the arena's books, and her thirty-one bouts have been paid in full. She has retired to a small house near the Taorra Oasis and keeps goats.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_ds_strongbox.pitc: I have won thirty-one bouts and each of them made Rim a richer man. He owes me a purse. He will not pay it. There is a strongbox under his stall, and in the strongbox is the arena's own tally of what I am owed. I do not want his money. I want my own name written down in the right column. Fetch the tally. I will do the rest.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_after_gold.des: The beacon burns gold and caravans are coming. Qadir Windfall has a full house.
Full. Every room on every landing, and a queue on the stair. Caravan masters, tax-men, a poet from Rihad who has paid for the top landing, which is mine, and which I have vacated, and which I regret. The raiders are fewer, because the watch is doubled. The wind sings a better song now, because it is drowned out by money. Have a drink. Have four.
Count the new custom at the Hundredth Step
The beacon is gold. How is trade?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_after_gold.out: The gold beacon of Elinhir draws caravans from the sand. The Hundredth Step has a queue on the stair, and Qadir Windfall has stopped sleeping.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_after_gold.pit: The beacon burns gold and caravans are coming. Qadir Windfall has a full house.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_after_white.de: The beacon burns white. Stairs-Keeper Jul has been watching it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_after_white.o0: My grandmother, on the third landing, at dusk. She is not there. She is not a ghost. She is a place where the light is a little warmer. I did not tell the priests. I put the hundred-and-first step's lamp on her landing and I said her name. The white light is not for the town. It is for the stair. I have never been prouder of my count.
Sit with Stairs-Keeper Jul under the white beacon
The beacon is white. What do you see?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_after_white.ou: The white beacon of Elinhir lights the stair for those who climbed it before. Stairs-Keeper Jul counts a hundred and one, and says each name.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_after_white.pi: The beacon burns white. Stairs-Keeper Jul has been watching it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_step.desc: Stairs-Keeper Jul says the Spire has one hundred and one steps. The priests say one hundred. He wants a neutral person to count, and to find the extra.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_step.o0.text: Count the steps up to the first landing
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_step.o1.text: Count the steps to the second landing
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_step.o2.journa: There was a hundred-and-first step. It was a hand-span tall, set into the floor of the third landing, with a small bronze plate. A loose stone beside it hid a shallow niche, and the niche held a tiny carved figure of a woman, her arms around a lamp.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_step.o2.text: Search beneath the third landing for the hundred-and-first step
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_step.o3.reply: The Lamp-Mother. A saint of the old stair. The story is that the builders left a step out of the count, for her, so that she could be said to be under the Spire without being counted among its people. I have the story in my notes. It is a lovely custom. I did not think anyone still kept it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_step.o3.text: Ask Brother Amir what the figure in the niche is
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_step.o3.topic: Under the third landing there is a hundred-and-first step and a carved figure of a woman with a lamp. Who is she?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_step.o4.reply: The Lamp-Mother. Of course. My grandmother used to say her name when she climbed. I thought it was an old woman's habit. Thirty years I was right, and I did not know what I was right about. Take this, from the Keeper's own pocket. It is a very small lamp. It will not go out.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_step.o4.text: Tell Stairs-Keeper Jul what is under the landing
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_step.o4.topic: The hundred-and-first step is a place for the Lamp-Mother. It is a custom, and a kind one.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_step.offer: Jul, where is the hundred-and-first step?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_step.outro: The Spire has a hundred steps, and one more, which is for the Lamp-Mother. The priests have been told, and have said that they always suspected.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_step.pitch: Every year the priests say one hundred. Every year I say one hundred and one. Every year I count it myself, in front of them, and every year I find a hundred and one, and they find a hundred, and nobody asks why. I have been the Keeper for thirty years and I am sick of being right. Count with me. Count the steps. Tell me what you find. Do not tell the priests.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_step.title: One Step Too Many
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.desc: Elinhir's beacon-keeper is ill, the wind-wall is cracked and raiders watch from the dunes. Warden Kaia Sun-Rhan needs a climber to carry water, defend the ramparts and light the beacon.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o0.text: Climb the first fifty steps of the Spire stair
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o1.reply: Here. A skin of the cold spring, from the cistern at the bottom. It is heavy, it is slippery, and it is the last thing you will want to carry up a hundred stairs in this wind. I will walk beside you to the fiftieth. After that, you are alone, and the water is your friend.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o1.text: Collect the water-skin from Mira the Water-Bearer
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o1.topic: Warden Kaia says the beacon-lighter carries the water. Where is it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o2.text: Climb the second fifty steps with the water-skin
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o3.reply: A hundred? Hm. A hundred and one, and you did not spill a drop on the extra one. You have a good back. I shall not tell you where the extra step is. But I shall tell you that the beacon-flint is under the third landing, behind the loose stone. Go. Take it. The raiders will be at the wall by now.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o3.text: Hand the water-skin to Stairs-Keeper Jul on the top landing
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o3.topic: The water, Stairs-Keeper. A hundred steps, not a drop lost.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o4.text: Defend the cracked wind-wall against Zahra Sand-Cutter's raiders
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o5.text: Wait for dusk on the Spire's top landing
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o6.text: Light the beacon of the Spire
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o7.c0.la: Burn it white. Elinhir should see its own ancestors.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o7.c0.re: Then white it is. The old ones will find their way home, and the caravans must find theirs by the stars. It is a quiet answer. I like it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o7.c1.la: Burn it gold. A road lit is a road used, and Elinhir should be used.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o7.c1.re: Then gold. I will post a double watch, and the Crown's tax-men may complain. A city that does not shine is a city that is forgotten.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o7.reply: Then Elinhir sees its own light. I have a choice to ask of you. The beacon can burn white, for the town, or gold, for the caravans that cross the sand. White draws the wind-spirits and the old ancestors. Gold draws trade, and raiders, and the Crown's attention. Which shall it be?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o7.text: Tell Warden Kaia how the beacon burns
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.o7.topic: The beacon is lit. I did not spill a drop. The raiders are broken.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.offer: Warden, what is the Hundred Steps?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.outro: The beacon of the Elinhir Spire burns, white or gold, each dusk. Mira the Water-Bearer carries water as she always has, and the Stairs-Keeper still will not show you the hundred-and-first step.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.pitch: Every dusk the beacon of the Spire is lit by a climber who has carried water up the Hundred Steps. It is the oldest custom in Elinhir. This year the beacon-keeper is ill, and the wind-wall is cracked, and raiders are watching from the sand. I need someone to climb, carry, defend and light, in that order. I will not insult you with a reward. I will insult you with a very hard climb.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_steps.title: The Hundred Steps
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_wall.desc: The wind howls through a crack in Elinhir's wind-wall behind the Hundredth Step inn. Qadir Windfall needs sawn logs and quarried stone to mend it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_wall.o0.reply: Six! Good, good. Now the stone. A mason's block is best, but a quarried block will do. Six, as I said. And mind the cat, he is under the stairs, and he is not mine.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_wall.o0.text: Bring six sawn logs to Qadir Windfall
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_wall.o0.topic: Six sawn logs, as asked. For the wind-wall.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_wall.o1.reply: A mason would be paid. I am paying in tea and sympathy. There. Hold the board. ... A little left. ... Gods, that is a good crack. It is also a very bad crack. Thank you. The wind will have to find another song.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_wall.o1.text: Bring six quarried stone to Qadir Windfall
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_wall.o1.topic: Six blocks of quarried stone. A mason would be insulted.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_wall.o2.reply: Qadir mended it? With timber and tea? I would not have believed it. A wall is a wall, and a crack is a crack, and a man who mends one with his own hands is a man I should have been paying. See that he is paid. And tell him to stop using the cat.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_wall.o2.text: Tell Warden Kaia the wall is mended
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_wall.o2.topic: Qadir Windfall has mended the wind-wall behind his inn. It sings no more.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_wall.outro: The wind-wall of Elinhir is mended, in timber and tea. The wind has found a new song, which it sings by the western ramparts, and which nobody has complained about.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_wall.pitch: Every night the wind comes down the stair and gets into the Hundredth Step, and sings. Last night it sang a very sad song, and a guest left in the small hours. I have traced it to a crack in the wind-wall behind the third landing. I cannot afford a mason. I can afford sawn timber, if you bring it, and a bit of stone. Bring me six logs and six blocks, and I shall mend it myself, and be a quieter man.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_el_wall.title: The Cracked Wind-Wall
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.desc: Spice-Master Rasul Karim needs a sealed bag carried through Rihad's maze to an unnamed recipient before sunset, past a watch that must not stop it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o0.reply: Do not open it. Do not squeeze it. Do not hand it to anyone who asks for it by name. Only the one who says "the hour of the returning shade" is the one. You will know. Go. The watch changes at the second bell.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o0.text: Take the sealed bag from Rasul Karim
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o0.topic: Give me the bag, Spice-Master. I will carry it, and I will not open it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o1.text: Slip past the watch at the Spice Gate customs
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o2.text: Hide in the caravanserai until the watch changes
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o3.reply: Cross? In one afternoon? You are lucky. The long shadow falls on the right path at the third hour. Follow me. Do not talk. Do not look at the walls. Look at the ground, where the dark falls. I know which lanes are real. The others are only jokes the city tells.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o3.text: Find Lila the Guide at the Courtyard Caravanserai
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o3.topic: Rasul Karim says you know the maze. I need to cross Rihad before sunset.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o4.text: Follow the minaret's shadow through the first lane
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o5.text: Follow the shadow through the second lane
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o6.text: Follow the shadow into the Hour-Keeper's courtyard
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o7.c0.labe: Give them to the Forebears. They have tended the Well since the ships came.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o7.c0.repl: Then the Forebears shall plant them at the Well of Two Names. Imran Bel-Tavir will weep. It is a good day.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o7.c1.labe: Give half to each. The Well is shared; so should its seed be.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o7.c1.repl: Half and half. Two groves, one well. Perhaps that is the oldest wisdom there is. Thank you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o7.reply: The hour of the returning shade. I have not heard those words in forty years. My grandfather said them on his deathbed and I never knew the rest. Give it here. ... Seeds. Date-palm seeds, from the very first grove of the Well. He kept them, and lost them, and Rasul Karim found them in a wall. I will plant them. But there is a thing you should know. Rasul wanted me to give half of them to the Crown. I want to give them to the Forebears. Who should have them?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o7.text: Hand the bag to Hour-Keeper Tahir bin-Haddar
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.o7.topic: The hour of the returning shade, Hour-Keeper. I have the bag.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.offer: Spice-Master, you said a bag needs moving.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.outro: Two groves of old date palms are growing, or one, or none, depending on whom you ask. Hour-Keeper Tahir has added a verse to the Minaret's list, and Rasul Karim has a new line of silence in his stall.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.pitch: A small bag. It weighs less than a goat's head and more than a promise. It must reach a particular person before the sun sets, and I cannot carry it, because the watch will stop me. They will not stop a stranger, if the stranger is quick. I will not tell you what is inside. I will not tell you who is to receive it. A guide will tell you the second. Ask Lila, in the Spice Gate.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_bag.title: A Bag Through the Maze
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_scale.desc: The customs scale at Rihad's Spice Gate is weighing light. Old Farid wants it examined in the night and, if false, laid on the Governor's desk.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_scale.o0.text: Wait for night, then enter the Spice Gate customs-house
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_scale.o1.text: Examine the customs scale and take it if false
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_scale.o2.c0.la: Take it to the Governor. A false scale is a theft from every honest trader.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_scale.o2.c0.re: Then it shall be done. Ghassan will weep. I will not.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_scale.o2.c1.la: Keep it as a lever. A customs master who fears his scale will charge fairly.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_scale.o2.c1.re: A lever. Yes. I like that better than I should. I shall put it in a drawer and look at it, sometimes.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_scale.o2.reply: The customs master, Ghassan. He has been doing this for six years. I know because I have lost a tenth of my cinnamon every season, and I wondered. Now. If I take this to the Governor, he will be ruined. If I put it back, no one will know. If I keep it, I have a very good lever. Tell me which is the more Redguard.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_scale.o2.text: Show the lead-weighted pan to Spice-Master Rasul Karim
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_scale.o2.topic: The scale is weighted. The pan has a lead plug. Who has been using it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_scale.offer: Old Farid, the customs scale? What is the matter?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_scale.outro: The customs scale at Rihad's Spice Gate weighs true, or very nearly. Old Farid says he does not mind, and that a camel is a camel.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_scale.pitch: The customs scale at the Spice Gate has been weighing light for years. A traveller pays for what he does not carry, and a trader loses a tenth of what he does. I have a suspicion about which pan. I would like it examined in the night, when the customs-house is dark and the watch is at supper. If it is false, I should like it taken, quietly, and put on the Governor's desk.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_scale.title: The Honest Pan
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_seventh.desc: Dhalia's inn is named after a seventh courtyard no one has ever found. She wants the lemon-leaf key and the door.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_seventh.o0.rep: A key! A lemon-leaf one? It is in the Hour-Keeper's collection of keys, in the box with the little brass lock. He does not know what it opens. I do. It opens a gate in the lemon tree. I have seen it when the wind moves the leaves. I was not allowed to say.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_seventh.o0.tex: Ask Lila the Guide about a lemon-leaf key
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_seventh.o0.top: Dhalia says there is a lemon-leaf key, and a seventh courtyard. Do you know it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_seventh.o1.tex: Take the lemon-leaf key from the Hour-Keeper's key-box
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_seventh.o2.jou: The lemon tree had a gate in it, the height of a small child, built of the same pale wood as the trunk. Beyond it was a courtyard no wider than a bed: a bench, a pool, a single lamp, and a very old woman's shawl folded on the seat.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_seventh.o2.tex: Open the gate hidden in the lemon tree of the Seventh Courtyard
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_seventh.o3.rep: A shawl! My great-grandmother's. She sat there and told no one. I had always thought she was lying about the seventh. I am a fool. I am a happy one. Take this. I shall sit there tonight, with a cup of tea, and think of her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_seventh.o3.tex: Tell Dhalia what you found in the seventh courtyard
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_seventh.o3.top: There is a seventh courtyard, Dhalia. A bench, a pool, a lamp, and a shawl.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_seventh.offer: Dhalia, what is the seventh courtyard?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_seventh.outro: The Seventh Courtyard of Rihad exists, and Dhalia sits there each evening, with a cup of tea and a shawl. The lemon tree has been left alone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_seventh.pitch: Every guest asks. The inn is called the Seventh Courtyard. There are six. My great-grandmother named it after the seventh, which is lost. There is a key, a lemon-leaf key, that opened it. The key is somewhere in Rihad. Lila the Guide knows every door and says there is no seventh. But she is eleven, and I have never heard a child say no to a mystery.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_seventh.title: The Seventh Courtyard
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.desc: Hour-Keeper Tahir bin-Haddar has lost the verse of the hour of the returning shade. Fragments are said to be in the caravanserai and the Seventh Courtyard.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.o0.reply: In a camel's harness. It was sewn under the girth, for luck. I have been carrying it for thirty years, and never thought to read it. Take it. If it is a verse, let it go home.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.o0.text: Ask Old Farid for the verse fragment found in the caravanserai
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.o0.topic: Hour-Keeper Tahir says you found a palm-leaf with writing on it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.o1.reply: A strip of palm-leaf. It is under the bar, in a jar of dates. I had it from my mother, who had it from hers. We used it as a bookmark. Oh, you are going to put them together, are you? Mind the dates. They are very old and very sticky.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.o1.text: Ask Dhalia of the Seventh Court for the second fragment
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.o1.topic: Old Farid had half a line. Hour-Keeper Tahir says you have another.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.o2.reply: A second half. Hold it up to the lamp. Yes. It fits the first as a key fits a lock. Bring me the other, and I shall read them together.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.o2.text: Give Hour-Keeper Tahir the fragment from the Seventh Court
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.o2.topic: This is the second fragment, from a jar of dates under Dhalia's bar. Its end is torn, and it ends mid-word.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.o3.reply: The hour when the traveller sets down his load. Of course. It is not a prayer. It is an instruction. The returning shade is the sundown, and the hour is the rest. I have been chanting a lullaby for forty years and calling it a hymn. Thank you. I shall say it at dusk. I shall say it for all of Rihad.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.o3.text: Return the first fragment to Hour-Keeper Tahir
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.o3.topic: And this is the first, from Old Farid's camel harness. Together they read: "...and the hour of the returning shade is the hour when the traveller sets down his load."
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.offer: Hour-Keeper, what is the lost verse?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.outro: The hour of the returning shade is chanted aloud now in the courtyard of Rihad's Minaret, and the long shadow falls, and travellers set down their loads.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.pitch: The hour of the returning shade has a verse, and I have lost it. It has a first line and a last, and I am missing the middle. A fragment of palm-leaf was found in Old Farid's caravanserai. Another, I am told, in the hands of Dhalia of the Seventh Court. Find the pieces. Put them together. I would like, before I die, to say the whole verse.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_rh_verse.title: The Lost Hour of the Minaret
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_after_governor: The Governor now holds the map of the hidden dock. Toll-Reeve Zahra Vane has seen the garrison arrive.

Fifty men by spring, and a toll-house on the north quay. The harbour is quieter, and the Draggin' Tale has half the custom, and Captain Makki sits on his deck with his chin on his fist. I record the new tolls. They are recorded in the Governor's favour. I find I do not like it. I find I never liked the old ones, either. I am a toll-reeve. We are not made to like things.
Hear Toll-Reeve Vane's account of the garrison's arrival
The Governor has the dock. What has changed?
A garrison stands on the north quay of Stros M'Kai, and the hidden dock is a toll-house. Captain Makki sits on his deck, and the sea is the same.
The Governor now holds the map of the hidden dock. Toll-Reeve Zahra Vane has seen the garrison arrive.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_after_makki.de: The hidden dock stays in Captain Makki's keeping. He promised you a cut of the next ship in.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_after_makki.o0: In the hold of a brig called the Evening Gull, which came in last night. I did not ask what she carried. I never do. There is a share under the third crate, marked with a gull. Take it, and a bit extra for the trouble. The Governor has asked twice about the dock. I told him it was a rumour. He said he would see. I said, "See what?" It is a very good answer.
Collect your cut from Captain Makki Red-Sail
The dock is yours. Where is my cut?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_after_makki.ou: The hidden dock of Stros M'Kai stays hidden. Captain Makki Red-Sail pays his debts in brig-loads and keeps his counsel in the dark.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_after_makki.pi: The hidden dock stays in Captain Makki's keeping. He promised you a cut of the next ship in.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_lighthouse.des: Stros M'Kai's lighthouse flashes once for every ship that passes and twice for those that do not pay the toll. Toll-Reeve Zahra Vane wants to know whether it is a man or a mechanism.
Clear the lighthouse base of whoever is guarding the rig
There was no mechanism. There was an old woman in a rocking chair, with a bell-rope in her hand and a long list of ships on her knee. She looked up and said, in the mildest way: "Oh, dear. Is it time for the next one? I do lose count."
Climb to the lamp room and examine the toll-rig
An old woman! Gods. That is Auntie Nuri, who was the Governor's nurse when he was a child. I had forgotten she was alive. Hm. She is a better toll-collector than any I have hired. I will not stop her. I shall pay her. In sweets.
Tell Toll-Reeve Vane who has been counting ships
It is a woman, Reeve. An old woman with a bell-rope, who says she loses count. She has been doing it for years.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_lighthouse.off: Zahra, you want the lighthouse looked at?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_lighthouse.out: The lighthouse of Stros M'Kai still counts ships. Auntie Nuri sits in her rocking chair, and Toll-Reeve Vane brings her sweets each evening, and the toll-book has never been more accurate.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_lighthouse.pit: The Stros M'Kai light has been counting ships. Not shining: counting. Every ship that passes, it flashes once. Twice for a ship that does not pay. Someone has rigged the lamp to the toll-book, and I want to know who. I have my suspicions. I will not say whom. Go up. Look. Tell me if it is a man or a mechanism.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.desc: Old Salim sells half of the map to Stros M'Kai's hidden dock. The other half is held by Captain Makki. A toll, a hidden dock and a choice of theft or defence await.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.o0.reply: The price is that you do not ask where I got it. And that you pay the Toll-Reeve her due, so that she cannot say you were on the island without leave. A thief with a receipt is a customer. A thief without one is merely a thief.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.o0.text: Take the half-map from Old Salim
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.o0.topic: I will buy your half. What is the price?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.o1.reply: A half-map! You declared it. How very honest. The toll for a half-map is nothing, but the toll for the man who carries it is five. Thank you. A receipt, with my seal, and a word of advice: do not be seen near the north quay at night.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.o1.text: Pay Toll-Reeve Zahra Vane the harbour toll in emeralds
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.o1.topic: Five emeralds. The toll for one visitor, one satchel and one half-map.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.o2.text: Wait for night and find the hidden dock beneath the harbour fort
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.o3.text: Defeat Warden Hamza One-Eye, who guards the hidden dock
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.o4.c0.la: Give him the map. A pirate's dock is a pirate's, and the island is more honest for it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.o4.c0.re: Then I will keep it, and I will keep it hidden. It is an old arrangement and a good one. Take a cut of the next ship in. I will make it a large one.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.o4.c1.la: Sell the dock to the Governor. A hidden harbour is a stolen harbour.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.o4.c1.re: Then the Governor will have a garrison by spring, and a toll by summer, and a very large problem by autumn. I will say nothing to you. I will say a great deal to the sea.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.o4.reply: Both halves! In one pair of hands. Hm. The dock is the only thing between this island and a Crown garrison, and I would sooner it were mine than the Governor's. Give me the halves, and I will burn them. Or keep them, and sell the dock to the Governor, and watch what happens to a harbour that has no secret.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.o4.text: Face Captain Makki Red-Sail with both halves of the map
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.o4.topic: I have both halves. The hidden dock is yours. What would you have me do with them?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.offer: Salim, what is the price of this map?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.outro: The hidden dock of Stros M'Kai is known, or unknown, depending on whom you ask. Old Salim has sold a third map to a third man, and swears it is the first.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.pitch: Half a map. It shows the hidden dock of Stros M'Kai, the one the Toll-Reeve does not tax and the Captain does not admit exists. I had it from a dying man, who had it from another. The other half is held by Captain Makki, who will not sell it, because it shows the dock too. Two halves make a whole, and a whole makes a very large problem for someone. Take my half. Pay the toll. Find the dock. Steal the other, or defend it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_price.title: The Island's Price
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_tall_tale.desc: Brulla of the Draggin' Tale will give a free drink to anyone who tells a better story than the forty on her menu. She wants you to gather the island's best.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_tall_tale.o0.r: The Gull and the Governor. A seagull stole the Governor's wig on the morning of his coronation, and flew it to the roof of the harbour fort, and refused to give it back. The Governor stood in the square, bald, for a full hour, while the gull sat on the wig and ate his cake. I was there. I have never laughed so hard. I am the gull's patron to this day.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_tall_tale.o0.t: Brulla says you have a tale better than anything on her menu. What is it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_tall_tale.o1.r: The Honest Map. A man sold a map of the island to three different buyers, each for a different treasure. All three followed it. All three dug in the same place. All three found each other. They set up a shop there. It is now the best-run chandlery on the north quay. The map was a lie. The shop is the truth. That is the best story I know.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_tall_tale.o1.t: Brulla says you have a tale better than anything on her menu. What is it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_tall_tale.o2.r: The Toll That Was Paid Twice. A captain came in, paid his toll, and left. A day later he came back and paid again, for no reason. I asked why. He said the first time was for the harbour, and the second was for a debt he owed the previous reeve, who had saved his life and never asked for anything. He wanted to pay it. The old reeve was dead. So he paid it to me. I wept at my desk. It was the most honest toll I ever collected.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_tall_tale.o2.t: Brulla says you have a tale better than anything on her menu. What is it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_tall_tale.o3.c: The Gull and the Governor. It is the funniest.
Then it shall be The Gull's Wig, and the drink shall have a feather in it. I have never been so happy.
The Honest Map. It is the cleverest.
The Honest Map. A sour drink with a little sweetness at the bottom. Yes. That is the island, and I love it.
The Toll That Was Paid Twice. It is the truest.
Then I shall pour it plain, in a plain cup, and charge nothing. It is the only one I will not name. I know exactly who it is for.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_tall_tale.o3.r: Three. And all three true. I shall have to decide, and I find that I want to hear them again. Tell me which you think is the best. I will put it on the menu in your name.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_tall_tale.o3.t: Tell Brulla which tale is the tallest
I have three, Brulla. The gull and the Governor, the honest map, and the toll that was paid twice. Which one do you want?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_tall_tale.offe: Brulla, you said nobody has won the free drink.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_tall_tale.outr: The menu of the Draggin' Tale now has forty-one stories, and at least one of them is true. Brulla pours the drink in your name each time you visit and will not take payment.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_tall_tale.pitc: My menu has forty stories, and I swear every one of them is true. The Kraken's Lunch, the Cursed Mudcrab, the Admiral's Wife. A drink is free only if your story is better than the one on the menu. I have been waiting years. I think the island has a better one than any of mine, but I cannot hear it, because I am always pouring. Ask around. Bring me the best. If it is better, I shall pour you a drink named after it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sm_tall_tale.titl: The Tallest Tale in the Draggin' Tale
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_after_burned.d: The Cobalt Ledger was burned. Zareen the Dye-Seller has noticed the smoke.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_after_burned.o: The whole bazaar knows. Not what was in it. That it burned. A smell like singed wool and old cobalt, over the awnings at dusk, and a very particular silence from the Harbour Guild. I have added a pinch of the ash to a new blue. It is a very beautiful colour. I call it Nothing Was Written. It sells like water in the desert.
Hear what Zareen the Dye-Seller makes of the ashes
The ledger is ash. Does the bazaar know?
A blue called Nothing Was Written sells in the Bazaar of Winds. The Cobalt Ledger is ash, and everyone knows it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_after_burned.p: The Cobalt Ledger was burned. Zareen the Dye-Seller has noticed the smoke.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_after_crowns.d: The Cobalt Ledger went to the Crown Council. Vizier Samir ibn-Cassim has news.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_after_crowns.o: Four Crown lords have been asked to travel. Four Forebear factors have been asked to explain. Four others have been asked nothing at all, and those are the ones I watch. Sentinel is quiet, which is the sound a city makes when it is holding its breath. The palm-print in cobalt matches a hand I know. I will not say whose. Thank you. Take this, with the Council's regard.
Hear what the Crown Council made of the Cobalt Ledger
The ledger is with the Council. What has changed?
The Crown Council has the Cobalt Ledger. Four lords have been asked to travel, and Sentinel holds its breath.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_after_crowns.p: The Cobalt Ledger went to the Crown Council. Vizier Samir ibn-Cassim has news.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_after_crowns.t: A Quiet Month on the Council
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_after_forebear: The Cobalt Ledger went to the Forebear speakers. Captain Layla Ashraf has a report from the docks.

Loud. The Forebear speakers read the names aloud from the Bazaar steps, in order, and three Crown lords left the city before the fourth. The Harbour Guild is in an uproar. The dye-sellers have doubled their prices. I have eleven men on the quay and a bad feeling in my sword-arm. But the cobalt is off the market, and nobody will be burned for it again. Take this.
Hear Captain Ashraf's report from the docks after the Forebear reading
The Forebears have the ledger. What do the docks say?
The Forebears read the names of the Cobalt Ledger from the Bazaar steps. Sentinel is loud, and the cobalt is off the market.
The Cobalt Ledger went to the Forebear speakers. Captain Layla Ashraf has a report from the docks.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.desc: Haroun the Ink-Maker needs a seller for the Bazaar of Winds' annual Haggling Tournament, and has lost to Zareen four years running.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.o0.repl: A blue-black for contracts, a sepia for love-letters, and a red for the sort of document that is signed in a hurry. Sell them for what they are. Do not lie about the red.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.o0.text: Collect three inks to sell from Haroun the Ink-Maker
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.o0.topi: I will sell your inks, Haroun. What are the three?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.o1.repl: Haroun! He sent a mercenary. I know the price. I will pay the price, and then I will tell you the colour is dull, and that you should be ashamed. I will give you a penny extra if you let me. I enjoy it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.o1.text: Sell the blue-black to Zareen the Dye-Seller
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.o1.topi: Haroun's blue-black ink, Zareen. A fair price.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.o2.repl: Red! For hurried documents! I will take three. My patrons sign everything in a hurry. And tell Haroun the parrot says he is a very handsome man. I do not know if that is true. The parrot has never been wrong.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.o2.text: Sell the red ink to Dalia the Peacock
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.o2.topi: Haroun's red, for hurried documents. A fair price.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.o3.repl: Too sad. Of course. That is the sepia. I shall keep it. I won! Not the richest, but the best-loved. The Bazaar voted. For once, my sins are forgiven. Take this, with my gratitude.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.o3.text: Report the tournament's result to Haroun
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.o3.topi: The blue-black sold at a fair price. The red sold three times over. The sepia was too sad for anyone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.outro: Haroun the Ink-Maker won the Haggling Tournament by a single vote, and Zareen the Dye-Seller has demanded a recount. The recount is expected next year.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.pitch: Once a year the stall-holders of the Bazaar of Winds hold a tournament. Each contestant is given three goods and sent to sell them for more than their weight. No lying, no weighting, no tears. The winner is not the richest, but the best-loved. I need someone to sell my three inks. I have been defeated four times by Zareen. I would like it to be five.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_haggle.title: The Haggling Tournament of the Bazaar of Winds
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.desc: A scrap of cobalt-dyed ledger cost a man his life in the Sentinel bazaar. Zareen the Dye-Seller wants the rest of the ledger found, and the dye's source named.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.o0.repl: Cobalt. The Harbour Guild uses it for tallies that must not be copied. A ledger that is copied in a different ink looks different, so the cobalt gives it away. Anyone who has seen the real thing knows the forgeries at a glance. It is a good system. Whoever is using it must be a very careful thief, or a very careful official.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.o0.text: Ask Haroun the Ink-Maker what the cobalt dye is for
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.o0.topi: Zareen gave me a scrap of paper stained cobalt. Haroun, what is it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.o1.text: Wait for night and watch the Bazaar of Winds from beneath the awnings
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.o2.text: Catch the runners moving crates under the bazaar awnings
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.o3.text: Raid the harbour warehouse and take Idris the Cobalt Hand
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.o4.c0.l: Give it to the Crown Council. The Dome Palace should know its own.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.o4.c0.r: Then it is law, and I will see it done. The Forebears will be angry. They have a right.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.o4.c1.l: Give it to the Forebear speakers. The sea-trade has been cheated, and they know their own ledger.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.o4.c1.r: Then it is theirs. The Crowns will not forgive me, and I will not ask them to. Take this, from the Forebear coffers.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.o4.c2.l: Burn it. Eleven hundred petitioners deserve a city that still holds together.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.o4.c2.r: Then it is ash, and I never saw it. I will deny it to my last breath. You are a more dangerous person than you look.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.o4.repl: A palm-print. The print of a Crown lord, I think, or a Forebear merchant. I can read the names, and I will not say them to you. The ledger names twelve. Four are mine. Four are theirs. Four are neither, and those are the ones that frighten me. Tell me, as a stranger, what I should do. If I give this to the Crown Council, the Forebears will cry persecution. If I give it to the Forebears, the Crowns will cry treason. If I burn it, eleven hundred petitioners lose a rumour.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.o4.text: Bring the Cobalt Ledger to Vizier Samir
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.o4.topi: The Cobalt Ledger. The names are in it, and a palm-print on the last page. I did not look at the print.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.offer: Zareen, a colour that tells a rumour?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.outro: The Cobalt Ledger is in someone's hands, or ash, or both. Zareen the Dye-Seller has added a new colour to her stall, and refuses to tell anyone where it came from.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.pitch: Every dye in my stall has a rumour. This one has a death. A man brought me a scrap of ledger, stained cobalt, and asked what dye it was. I told him. That night his stall burned, and he was in it. The dye is not from the bazaar. It is from the Harbour, and someone is using it to mark paper that must not be copied. Find the paper.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_ledger.title: The Cobalt Ledger
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_parrot.desc: Dalia's parrot Vizier, who announces every debt in Sentinel, has been stolen from the Cobalt Peacock. Someone wants the debts.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_parrot.o0.text: Search the dock warehouses for the stolen parrot
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_parrot.o1.text: Catch Sakr Greasefinger, the thief who stole the parrot
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_parrot.o2.repl: Oh, my darling. My treasure. You have been shouting, I can hear. What do you say? ... Gods. He says the Harbour Master owes eleven hundred, the Vizier owes forty, and an unnamed person in a blue coat owes a name. A name. Well. I shall not repeat it. I shall let him go on shouting, and the blue coat may do as it pleases.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_parrot.o2.text: Return Vizier to Dalia at the Cobalt Peacock
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_parrot.o2.topi: Here is your parrot. He has been shouting for two days. I believe he has named the thief's employer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_parrot.outro: The parrot Vizier shouts debts from the Cobalt Peacock every evening, and the blue coat has not been seen in the bazaar since.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_parrot.pitch: My parrot Vizier knows every debt in Sentinel. He has been announcing them every evening for six years, and it was a joke until someone took him. They want the debts, you see. The people who owe money to people who do not wish it known. Vizier is in a cage somewhere on the docks. He is, I imagine, shouting. Please bring him home. I will pay you in whatever is left of my dignity.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_parrot.title: The Parrot Who Knew Too Much
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.desc: Two of Captain Layla Ashraf's guards, a sword-singer and a scribe, are rivals for the same woman's hand, and each has written her a wedding verse.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.o0.reply: The sword-singer's ink is mine, a plain black. The scribe's is Zareen's, a deep indigo, which is odd. A scribe does not usually write in indigo. He is trying to impress. Or he is trying to be someone else. I leave you to decide which.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.o0.text: Ask Haroun the Ink-Maker whose ink each verse was written in
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.o0.topic: Two verses, two rivals. Whose ink is whose?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.o1.reply: To the sword-singer. Do you see? He bought it to write the scribe's verse in. So that he could say it was a forgery. I knew. I said nothing. I am a dye-seller, not a judge. But I thought it was a very sad little trick.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.o1.text: Show Zareen the verse and ask her whom the indigo was sold to
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.o1.topic: The scribe's verse is in your indigo. You sold it. To whom?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.o2.c0.la: Be gentle. A sword-singer who forges a verse is a man in love.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.o2.c0.re: Then I will speak to him as one who has also loved, and I will not mention the indigo again.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.o2.c1.la: Be severe. A verse is a vow, and a forged vow is no vow at all.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.o2.c1.re: Then it shall be the stocks for a night, and the apology on the Bazaar steps. A sword-singer should know better.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.o2.reply: A forgery! Of a verse. By a man of the sword. Gods. I did not think it of him. I shall speak to him, and I shall tell the scribe, and the woman may choose for herself. Or she may choose neither, which would not surprise me. Tell me: shall I be gentle or severe?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.o2.text: Bring the verse back to Captain Ashraf
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.o2.topic: The sword-singer bought indigo to forge the scribe's verse. It is a poor trick, but a very sad one.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.offer: Captain, you have a rivalry on your hands?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.outro: The woman whom both guards loved has married a third man, a quiet shipwright. Both guards attended the wedding. They sat together, and neither wrote a verse.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.pitch: Two of my harbour guards, a sword-singer and a scribe, each love the same woman. Each has written her a wedding verse. Each has shown it to me, privately, and each swears the other's is a forgery of his. I am not a judge of poetry. I am a judge of honest work. Take them each a verse, and bring me what they say. I want to know who is the more honest man.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_sn_verse.title: Two Sword-Singers, One Verse
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_pools.desc: Najwa the Gardener and her rival Karim have quarrelled over the pool-garden for thirty years, and she wants a truce, and also, secretly, supper.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_pools.o0.reply: Karim! Ha. He is at the pool of lanterns, drinking a verse he has not yet written. He has been at it a week. He claims it is for a wedding. It is not. It is for a woman. I will not say who. It is not a very well-kept secret.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_pools.o0.text: Ask Sulayman the Pearl-Diver where Karim is today
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_pools.o0.topic: Najwa wants me to find Karim, the lower-terrace gardener. Do you know him?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_pools.o1.reply: A truce. Hm. I have a verse, you see, and it is nearly finished. It begins "To the gardener of the upper pool, who has never forgiven me my roses." I cannot finish it. I am a better gardener than a poet. Tell her I will come to supper. Tell her I will bring the lilies. Tell her I am sorry for the thing with the hose.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_pools.o1.text: Find Karim at the Pool of Lanterns
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_pools.o1.topic: Karim, I come from Najwa the Gardener. She asks for a truce.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_pools.o2.reply: Unfinished. Of course it is. He has never finished anything in his life but a wine bottle. Give it here. ... Oh. Oh, the old fool. He has put my name in the third line, in his bad handwriting. I will finish it myself. I have the ending in my head. It is a good ending. I wrote it thirty years ago.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_pools.o2.text: Bring Karim's unfinished verse to Najwa
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_pools.o2.topic: He is coming to supper. He is bringing lilies. And he sends you this, unfinished.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_pools.outro: Najwa and Karim share the upper pool of Taneth, and quarrel gently about it every evening. The lilies, it is said, have never been so well-behaved.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_pools.pitch: There is a man named Karim, a gardener of the lower terraces, who says the pool-garden is his by right of a verse. He is a charming, wretched, magnificent liar, and I have loved him for thirty years, and he has never once been wrong about a flower. I want him to stop. I also want him to come to supper. I do not know how to ask for both. Go to him. Ask for a truce. Make it sound like it was your idea.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_pools.title: Two Gardeners, One Pool
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_ship_book.desc: Harbour-Reeve Benyam's page of marginal notes, recording the true fates of Taneth's ships, has been stolen. He wants it found, and whoever reads margins.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_ship_book.o0.r: Asked? No. Paid, yes. A woman in a blue veil, three nights this week. She buys a drink, she writes a verse, and she leaves a coin under the cup that is not a coin of Taneth. It is a Sentinel coin. She sits where she can see the harbour office. I thought she was lovelorn. She is not.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_ship_book.o0.t: Ask Dina of the Lanterns who has been asking about the ship-book
Someone took a page of Benyam's margins. Have you heard anyone ask?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_ship_book.o1.t: Watch the harbour office from the Pool of Lanterns
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_ship_book.o2.t: Stop the woman in the blue veil and her hired men
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_ship_book.o3.c: Keep the margins private. A Reeve's notes are his own.
Then they are ink and silence, and I will tell nobody, and I will keep them in a drawer.
Show the scuttlings to the Emir. The owners should answer for it.
Then I will carry them to the Emir myself. I am a thorough man. I am also, apparently, a brave one.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_ship_book.o3.r: Eleven ships. Hm. The ones I recorded as lost to wreck and weather. Which they were, mostly. But three of them, my friend, were scuttled by their own owners for the insurance, and I wrote it in the margin because I am a thorough man. Someone would very much like to collect what a scuttling pays. I would like to keep my margins. And my head.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_ship_book.o3.t: Return the page of margins to Harbour-Reeve Benyam
The woman in the blue veil was working for a Sentinel factor. She wanted the fates of eleven ships.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_ship_book.offe: Reeve, what is missing from the ship-book?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_ship_book.outr: The margins of the Taneth ship-book are intact, or exposed, depending on the choice. Harbour-Reeve Benyam has bought a small lock for his drawer, and has been seen to sleep.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_ship_book.pitc: A page. Not a page of ships. A page of margins. Eleven years of notes I wrote at the edges, the true fates of the ships, in my own hand. Someone has taken it. They are not interested in the ships. They are interested in the notes. I wrote what I knew, and I knew a great deal, and I did not think anyone would read the margins. Find it. And find who reads margins.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_ship_book.titl: The Margin Where the Ships Go
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.desc: Emir Jalil ibn-Roshan wishes to give the sea its generational verse, whose three stanzas are kept by a gardener, a reeve and a diver. He asks you to gather and recite them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o0.reply: You may hear it, and carry it. It is the gardener's line: "Where the water has nowhere to go, it learns to listen." That is the whole of it. I have said it every morning for thirty years, and I am never sure whether it is a verse or a gardener's complaint.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o0.text: Learn the first stanza from Najwa the Gardener
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o0.topic: The Emir says you keep a stanza of the sea-verse. May I hear it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o1.reply: Of course. It is written in the margin of the oldest page, beside a lost ship. "The ship was named Patience, and the wind was named Not Yet." Beautiful, is it not? I keep it because it is the only entry in the ship-book that makes me weep.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o1.text: Learn the second stanza from Harbour-Reeve Benyam
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o1.topic: The Emir says the ship-book keeps a stanza. May I hear it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o2.reply: It is not said. It is shown. Take the shell. Hold it to your ear in the dark and you will know the words. It is my grandfather's, and his grandfather's. I trust you with it, because you are a stranger, and that is the only reason it is safe.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o2.text: Learn the third stanza from Sulayman the Pearl-Diver
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o2.topic: The Emir says you keep the last stanza. May I hear it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o3.text: Climb to the palace roof to recite the verse
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o4.text: Wait for dusk and speak the verse to the sea
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o5.text: Face the sea's answer rising in the harbour
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o6.c0.la: The Sea-Pearl. A jewel the sea itself shaped.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o6.c0.re: Then it is yours. May it remind you that the sea listens, and that it is not always kind.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o6.c1.la: The right to name a ship. Taneth's harbour is its pride.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o6.c1.re: Then Taneth shall have a vessel that carries a stranger's name. Benyam will write it in the ship-book, and it will be the only entry that makes him smile.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o6.reply: It answered. It always answers someone, and it chose a stranger. I have waited my whole reign. Very well. The sea has a gift for the one who says its verse, and I have the right to give it in the sea's name. Choose. The Sea-Pearl, a jewel of the deep. Or the right to name a ship of Taneth, which will carry your name over every wave.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o6.text: Tell Emir Jalil what the sea answered
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.o6.topic: The sea answered. I said the verse, and something rose out of the harbour, and asked me to say it again.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.offer: Emir, you want a poem delivered?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.outro: The sea has been answered, in the Emir's name and a stranger's voice. In Taneth they say the harbour is a little bluer at dusk now, and that the water-lilies have stopped biting.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.pitch: The Emirs of Taneth have given a verse to the sea at the turn of every generation. It has three stanzas, and each is kept by a different person, who will not share it with anyone but a stranger. I am the fourth Emir, and I have never been entrusted with them. I am told it is because I am too eager. It is true. Go. Ask the gardener, the reeve and the diver. Bring me the verse. And say it, at dusk, from the roof, to the sea.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hf_tn_verse.title: A Verse for the Sea
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_after_plain.de: The plain peal rang and the warning stayed silent. Archpriest Elric Ashby wants a word.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_after_plain.o0: Quiet. Too quiet, some say, and I do not know if they are right. I have lit a candle at the Mara altar each night for the warning I did not send. If the war comes, I will answer for it. If it does not, I will have answered for a silence. I am an old man. I have learned that a silence can be a sin as readily as a word. Thank you, stranger, for not saying so.
Visit Archpriest Elric Ashby after the plain peal
The plain peal rang. Is the bay quiet?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_after_plain.ou: Camlorn rings its bells on schedule. Archpriest Elric Ashby lights a candle each night, and does not say for whom.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_after_plain.pi: The plain peal rang and the warning stayed silent. Archpriest Elric Ashby wants a word.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_after_true.des: The true peal rang out over the bay. Bellwright Tam Selby has heard the answer.
From Daggerfall, at dusk, on the Gate Span's small bell, which is the only bell in the city nobody remembers casting. The reply was one note, held very long. I have been told it meant: received. The Knights of the Dragon have doubled the watch on the Glenumbra road. I cast a new clapper this morning. It rings like a promise. Take this.
Hear from Bellwright Tam Selby how the true peal was answered
The true peal rang. Did anyone answer?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_after_true.out: The bells of Daggerfall and Camlorn speak in the old code again, and the Knights of the Dragon watch the Glenumbra road.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_after_true.pit: The true peal rang out over the bay. Bellwright Tam Selby has heard the answer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_courtship.desc: Lady Hvarine Mauvesse forged a pair of love letters for a wager and now wants them delivered, and the two lovers brought together, before the joke turns into a tragedy.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_courtship.o0.r: Lord Alden. A very quiet guest. Third table, back. He has been drinking since noon and has asked for a pen four times, and each time has thrown it down. If I had a coin for each ruined sheet, I would be a Duchess.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_courtship.o0.t: Ask Wynn Arrowsmith whether Lord Alden Vesey is at the Quiet Peal
I have a letter for Lord Alden Vesey. Is he a guest of yours?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_courtship.o1.r: She is in the bell tower. She comes up every night to look at the Daggerfall road. She is waiting for someone. I should not say. You cannot say I said.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_courtship.o1.t: Take the second letter to Dame Rosamund at the Cathedral
I have a letter for Dame Rosamund. Is she at the Cathedral?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_courtship.o2.j: They met on the stair, each holding an envelope, each looking at the other as though at a stranger and a certainty. Neither said a word for a long while. Then Dame Rosamund laughed, and Lord Alden, who had been wearing the face of a man at a funeral, began to cry, and they went down the stair together.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_courtship.o2.t: Bring the lovers together at the tower stair
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_courtship.o3.r: Darling. I did not hope. I merely wagered. But I am delighted, I am simply delighted. Take this, and, if you can, tell no one that the letters were forged. They think the other wrote them. It is much more romantic, and I have never been so proud of a lie.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_courtship.o3.t: Tell Lady Hvarine how it ended
They met. They laughed and they wept. Your forged letters did exactly what you hoped.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_courtship.offe: Lady Hvarine, you have a letter to deliver?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_courtship.outr: Lord Alden Vesey and Dame Rosamund are to be married at the Cathedral of Mara before Frostfall. Lady Hvarine will wear green, and tell everyone she is not at all smug.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_courtship.pitc: Two letters. One from Lord Alden Vesey to the lovely Dame Rosamund, and one from Dame Rosamund to Lord Alden. Each thinks the other has been cruel. Neither has. I wrote both, you understand, to settle a bet. Now I should like them to meet, before one of them proposes to a different person. Carry them to each other, and do not let either see the other's envelope.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.desc: Camlorn's great bell rang by itself three nights ago, in a pattern every ringer recognises but will not name. Sexton Osric Pell wants the clapper examined.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o0.text: Climb the bell tower of the Cathedral of Mara
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o1.text: Take the scroll wound round the bell's clapper
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o2.reply: Dots and bars. Ha. That is change-ringing, boy. Not the call, the code. Every bell in the bay can speak in it, if the ringers are bored enough. This one says: seven, three, nine, nine. The old signal for danger-to-the-keep. It was not meant for here. It was rung for Daggerfall, and someone is blocking it before it can be sent.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o2.text: Ask Bellwright Tam Selby to read the dots on the clapper scroll
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o2.topic: This grid of dots was wound round the clapper. Can you read it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o3.reply: Darling. Anyone who sells to the Dragon's enemies. Anyone who takes silver from a certain Direnni house that shall remain nameless. Anyone, in short, with a pocket. If you want one name, ask the Archpriest why he asked for the ringers to be sent home early last month. I overheard. I always overhear.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o3.text: Ask Lady Hvarine who benefits from a silenced bell
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o3.topic: Someone is blocking a danger-signal meant for Daggerfall. Who in Camlorn would want that?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o4.text: Wait for dark and climb the tower again
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o5.text: Confront Brother Cael the Hushed, who has been silencing the bell
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o6.c0.lab: Ring the true peal. The warning must reach Daggerfall.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o6.c0.rep: Then I will not stop you. And I will pray, as I have not prayed in a decade, that you are right.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o6.c1.lab: Ring the plain peal. A false alarm is worse than a missed one.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o6.c1.rep: Then I have gained a friend, and I do not deserve one. Take this. It is the Cathedral's thanks, in hard coin.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o6.reply: For the peace. Do you think I do it for coin? Camlorn has two thousand people, and the danger-signal means a war, and the war means a thousand of them dead. I have been keeping the bell quiet for the sake of the quiet. I am not proud. I am not repentant. Decide for yourself. Ring it true, and send the warning. Or ring it plain, and let the bay sleep.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o6.text: Confront Archpriest Elric Ashby with the Peal Key
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.o6.topic: The Peal Key was in the tower. Cael has been silencing the bell for you. Why?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.offer: Sexton, what do you mean, the bell has a memory?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.outro: The great bell of Camlorn rings on schedule now, and the ringers go home at the proper hour. Whether the warning reached Daggerfall is something the Company of the Peal will not say, but they hum the sequence in the street, and children skip to it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.pitch: It rang three nights ago. Alone. No ringers, no ropes, no wind. A long sequence, falling, and then silence. Every ringer in the Company of the Peal knows what it was. They will not say. I tried to ring it myself, to see, and someone cut the rope. Look at the clapper. There is a thing wound round it that should not be there.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_peal.title: The Peal That Rang Alone
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_quiet.desc: The Quiet Peal Inn's cellar hosts a monthly meeting of six whispering guests, and someone is leaving with ink on their hands. Wynn Arrowsmith wants to know what is written.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_quiet.o0.text: Wait for the cellar meeting at the Quiet Peal
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_quiet.o1.reply: Six. Three bell-ringers, a clerk, a goldsmith, and the Archpriest's own scribe. They are writing a peal of their own, darling. A private code that does not use the Cathedral's bells. They think I do not know. I have been invited, twice. I declined. It is rude to eavesdrop on a meeting you are already in.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_quiet.o1.text: Ask Lady Hvarine who attends the monthly cellar meeting
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_quiet.o1.topic: There is a monthly meeting at the Quiet Peal. Six whispering guests. Who are they?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_quiet.o2.reply: It is for the day the Cathedral's bells are silenced. A free peal, rung on small hand-bells from six rooftops at once. It is meant to be heard all over the city and traced to no one. I have cast the bells. I am sworn to say nothing. I have said it. Gods. I need a drink.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_quiet.o2.text: Ask Bellwright Tam Selby what the private peal is for
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_quiet.o2.topic: Six of them are writing a private peal. What is it for?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_quiet.offer: Wynn, why is your inn soundproofed?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_quiet.outro: The Quiet Peal is just as quiet as it was, and the meeting in the cellar goes on, and the ink on the whisperers' hands is a little fainter than it was.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_quiet.pitch: My grandmother lined the walls with wool and wax, and nobody has asked why. I know why. There is a cellar. In the cellar, once a month, six people meet and speak in whispers. I do not listen, because I am a professional. But someone has been coming up the cellar stair with ink on their hands. I would like to know what is being written down.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_cm_quiet.title: What the Quiet Peal Hears
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_boots.desc: The third drying frame in Tannery Row rattles every night with no wind to blame. Tanner Perrin Voss wants the noise to stop.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_boots.o0.text: Keep watch at the third drying frame after midnight
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_boots.o1.reply: The boy! Wulfric. Fourteen. A fever. He was working on a pair of boots for his sister's wedding, and he died before they were stitched. The sister married barefoot. The family has never forgiven the Row. I thought it was forgotten. It is not.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_boots.o1.text: Ask Hobb Cressey if an apprentice of Tannery Row died unfinished
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_boots.o1.topic: The hides on the third frame rattle at night. Do you know of an apprentice who died on the Row?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_boots.o2.reply: Enough? Gods, I do not know. But put them on the frame. Tonight. Say his name. Wulfric. And say that the sister was not to blame.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_boots.o2.text: Bring a pair of leather boots to the third frame
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_boots.o2.topic: A pair of leather boots, as Hobb described. Do you think it will be enough?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_boots.offer: Tanner, you said the frames make noise?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_boots.outro: The third drying frame in Tannery Row is quiet. Tanner Perrin Voss says the hides hang straight, and a pair of very small boots sits on a shelf by the door, which no one touches.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_boots.pitch: Every night, on the third drying frame, the hides rattle. Not the wind: the wind is on the north side and the frame is sheltered. I have asked the priest. The priest says leave a candle. I have left four candles. The frame has not been satisfied. I do not believe in ghosts. I do believe in noise at three in the morning, and I would like it to stop.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_boots.title: Skins That Will Not Settle
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_pledge.desc: The Bridge-House has taken a widow's bed in pledge and the ledger says she owes three times what she borrowed. Ines Balancier wants the ledger copied, or taken.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_pledge.o0.text: Wait for night, then approach the Bridge-House cellar
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_pledge.o1.text: Quiet the cellar guard in the Bridge-House
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_pledge.o2.text: Take the pledge ledger from the cellar strongbox
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_pledge.o3.c0.l: Keep the ledger. Publish the forgery to the Guild council.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_pledge.o3.c0.r: Then a hundred widows will thank you, and the Bridge-House will not. Take this. It is Berenice's thanks.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_pledge.o3.c1.l: Cut the page and return the book. Quiet is cheaper than war.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_pledge.o3.c1.r: Then it is quiet. The widow keeps her bed and the Bridge-House keeps its shame. I will not tell a soul.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_pledge.o3.repl: Wrong by two hundred, in her favour, not theirs. They have been forging the count and sticking to it. I shall have the page copied tonight. Now. The book is a hot thing. If we keep it, the Bridge-House will know within the week. If we return it, with the page cut out, they will think a rat took it. Which?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_pledge.o3.text: Bring the ledger to Ines Balancier
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_pledge.o3.topi: The ledger is here. Berenice's page is marked with a violet. The sum is wrong.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_pledge.offer: Ines, what is the pledge book?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_pledge.outro: Berenice Tarn sleeps in her own bed again, and Ines Balancier's brass scales stand in her window, weighing nothing, balanced perfectly.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_pledge.pitch: The Bridge-House lends against furniture and kin. My friend Berenice Tarn pledged her wedding bed against her late husband's debt, and the bed has been taken, and a pledge-ledger in the Bridge-House cellar says she owes three times what she borrowed. I cannot read the ledger and I cannot enter the cellar. Someone who knows how to be quiet could do both. I shall pay.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_pledge.title: The Widow's Pledge
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_spans.desc: Hobb Cressey of the Three Bridges Inn has entered you in Daggerfall's Race of Seven Spans, a run across every toll-bridge in the city, free of charge for one day only.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_spans.o0.text: Start the Race of Seven Spans at the Three Bridges
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_spans.o1.text: Cross the Guild Span without breaking stride
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_spans.o2.journ: You touched the castle gate a full breath ahead of a baker's son and a very large dog. The crowd cheered. Madam Pelline Tessier did not.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_spans.o2.text: Cross the Gate Span and touch the castle gate
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_spans.o3.reply: A month! And I shall give you thirty tankards, all in a row, so the Guild sees. Sit down. Drink slowly. And please do not tell the Madam that the race was not entirely legal.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_spans.o3.text: Claim the winner's month of free ale from Hobb Cressey
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_spans.o3.topic: I touched the gate first. A month, you said.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_spans.outro: The Race of Seven Spans is run each year now, and the winner's name is cut into the lintel of the Three Bridges Inn. Yours is the first.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_spans.pitch: Every Tirdas of Sun's Height we run the Seven Spans, from the Three Bridges to the castle gate and back, one foot on each bridge and one hand on the rail. The winner drinks free for a month. The Guild would like it banned, because nobody pays toll during the race. Hence, it is free to enter, and I am entering you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_spans.title: The Race of Seven Spans
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.desc: Sir Alaric Brune has a letter that must cross Daggerfall's two toll-bridges unread. He wants a traveller who can pay the toll, then slip through the toll-houses.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o0.reply: Four. Per person, per crossing. The letter is an additional charge, and I shall have to inspect it. No? A matter of principle. Very well. Here is your tally-stick. Show it at every toll-house. Do not lose it. We count sticks at the end of the day.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o0.text: Pay Madam Pelline Tessier the bridge toll in emeralds
