story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o0.topic: Four emeralds. A passage for one, and one letter, as the schedule says.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o1.text: Wait for dark and slip across the Guild Span
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o2.text: Reach the Gate Span without being read
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o3.text: Break the Gate Span's toll-gang before they search you
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o4.reply: No seal. Of course. That is the point. Hm. It is from the Duchess of Daggerfall to a lady in Camlorn, and it says that the bridges are to be opened, free of toll, for one year. The Guild will not like it. Madam Pelline will like it even less. She has taken this city's bridges for twenty years, and I believe she has been cheating on the count. Foil her, and the Duchess's hand is free.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o4.text: Deliver the unsealed letter to Dame Clemence Aubry in the castle
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o4.topic: Sir Alaric Brune sent this. It has no seal. I did not read it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o5.text: Catch Tollmaster Sorel counting double at the Guild Span at night
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o7.c0.lab: Raise the tolls. Daggerfall pays for its bridges. Better honest than free.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o7.c0.rep: Then it shall be a penny more on the Gate Span, and a promise to the Duchess that no one will count twice again. Take this, from the Guild's box.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o7.c1.lab: Open the bridges. A city that taxes every crossing has stopped being a city.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o7.c1.rep: Then the Guild will howl, and I will weep, and the bridges will open at dawn. I will go to the Duchess myself.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o7.reply: Let me see. ... Yes. That is my scale. That is my master's hand. That is Garrick, who I trusted. I have been cheated by my own tollmaster for four years, and I did not see it, because the scale is always right. I am not a thief. I am a fool. Daggerfall has a right to know either way. Tell me what to do. Raise the toll, to cover what I have lost? Or open the bridges, and let the Guild hold the debt?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o7.text: Confront Madam Pelline Tessier with the double tally
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.o7.topic: Your toll-house counts every crossing twice. You pocket the second count.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.offer: Sir Alaric, what is the letter?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.outro: Daggerfall's bridges are either more honest or more free, depending on whom you ask, and Madam Pelline Tessier has taken to checking her own scales twice. Sir Alaric Brune has never once admitted he was involved.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.pitch: It is a letter, and it must cross two toll-houses, the Guild Span and the Gate Span, to reach the castle. The tolls there are not tolls, they are tithes, and each toll-house reads every letter that passes. This one must not be read. Buy the right to cross, as any honest traveller does, and then be a good deal less honest. If caught, I never met you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_dg_toll.title: A Toll on the Bridges
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_after_kept.des: The Water Rose stays in the lakebed, and Evermor Cathedral will be moved to the hill. Brother Ansel has the plans.
A hundred years, give or take a flood. We have marked the first stone, and I have drawn the plan: a nave on the hill, a tower with a bell, a window of plain glass. The Bishop will not live to see the roof. I will not live to see the door. But a child has been baptised in the old font and will see it, and she is only two. Take this. It is the first stone, and it is yours to lay.
Hear Brother Ansel's plan to move the cathedral
The rose stays down. What of the cathedral?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_after_kept.out: The first stone of the new cathedral of Evermor stands on the hill, and the lake is a little higher each winter. Nobody in the town is frightened of it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_after_kept.pit: The Water Rose stays in the lakebed, and Evermor Cathedral will be moved to the hill. Brother Ansel has the plans.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_after_kept.r0: First Stone of the New Nave
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_after_kept.tit: Stone by Stone to the Hill
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_after_placed.d: The Water Rose has been set back in the east window of the cathedral. Bishop Mallory Fenn invites you to see it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_after_placed.o: Dry. For the first time in my life the nave floor does not weep. The glass is cold in the mornings and warm at dusk, and the candles stand upright. The lake has settled a finger-joint, and the lower nave is quiet. I have said a mass for the Canon. I felt, at the end of it, very faintly, that someone said Amen. It was not a human voice. It was not unkind.
See the east window with Bishop Mallory Fenn
The rose is back in the sill. How does the nave feel?
The Water Rose sits in the east window of Evermor Cathedral, and the nave floor is dry. The Canon of the lower nave has not spoken again.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_after_placed.p: The Water Rose has been set back in the east window of the cathedral. Bishop Mallory Fenn invites you to see it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_candle.desc: The candles of the Wet Candle burn upside down, by miracle or by trick. Pernel Oak wants a test, with a candle from outside.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_candle.o0.repl: A candle. Here. It is from the cathedral steps. It has never burned upside down in its life, and I would be very pleased if it did. I will say that every candle I have lit in the Wet Candle has gone right way up, and nobody has ever believed me, because nobody has ever asked.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_candle.o0.text: Ask Lamplighter Vey for a candle burned elsewhere in Evermor
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_candle.o0.topi: I need a candle from a different house in Evermor, to test the Wet Candle's miracle.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_candle.o1.repl: There. A fresh candle. Watch. ... It burns the right way up. Of course. Because it is a cathedral candle and the cathedral does not believe in miracles. Now this one. ... There. Upside down. Do you see? It is the room. It is not the candle. It is the room, and the room is built over something, and I have never been brave enough to dig.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_candle.o1.text: Light Vey's candle in the Wet Candle with Pernel Oak
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_candle.o1.topi: Here is Vey's candle, from the cathedral steps. Let us see what it does.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_candle.o2.repl: Below it? The old cathedral, the first one, the one built before the lake rose. The Wet Candle is a guesthouse built on its crypt. The air down there is drawn from the lake, and the lake breathes. I suspect that is all it is. A draught that runs the wrong way. But I would not tell Pernel. It is a lovely draught.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_candle.o2.text: Show Brother Ansel the inverted wick
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_candle.o2.topi: The candle burned upside down only inside the Wet Candle. The room is the cause. What is below it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_candle.offer: Pernel, you said you would pay to have the trick revealed?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_candle.outro: The candles of the Wet Candle burn upside down, as they have since the first. Pernel Oak has put up a new sign that reads: A MIRACLE, OR A DRAUGHT. PLEASE DO NOT ASK WHICH.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_candle.pitch: Every candle in the Wet Candle burns upside down. The flame holds at the bottom and the wax runs up. It has done so since my grandmother lit the first. The priests call it a miracle. A man from the Wayrest chandlers' guild says it is a trick of the wick. I would like both of them to be quiet. Bring me a candle from a different inn, and I will show you what it does under this roof.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_candle.title: The Upside-Down Candles
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_race.desc: Ferrywoman Iselle needs a bailer for the Evermor feast-of-Mara ferry race, which she has lost six years running.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_race.o0.text: Take your place in the ferry at the quay
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_race.o1.text: Race the ferry round the Pilot's Rock
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_race.o2.text: Reach the cathedral island steps first
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_race.o3.reply: The winner! Seven years, and not once did I think... Take this. I stole it from Hob Corwin's boat last night. It is a very good oar-lock. Do not tell him. Tell him it is a gift from a grateful lake.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_race.o3.topic: The ferry beat the others by a boat-length. You are the winner.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_race.offer: Iselle, what is this about a race?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_race.outro: The ferry race of Evermor has a new champion. Hob Corwin sulks, and Iselle has added a very small flag to her stern, which says nothing, in an extremely pointed manner.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_race.pitch: Every feast of Mara the ferrymen race to the island. Four oars, two steersmen, and a dispute about who won. I have a place in the stern and nobody to bail. You will bail. You will bail very hard. I have been beaten six years by Hob Corwin, who is a cheat, and I wish to be beaten this year by someone more honest.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_race.title: The Ferry Race to the Island
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.desc: The Water Rose, a glass rosette that once sat in the cathedral's east window, has fallen into the lakebed, and the lake is rising a finger-joint each winter. Bishop Mallory Fenn wants it found.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.o0.text: Take Ferrywoman Iselle's boat out to the cathedral island
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.o1.reply: Not the lake. The undercroft. The cathedral is built over a lower cathedral, and the lower one is flooded. The rose fell through the east sill and into the old nave, and the old nave is a hundred feet down. I can draw you a map. I will not come.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.o1.text: Ask Brother Ansel where the Water Rose fell
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.o1.topic: Brother Ansel, the Bishop says the rose fell into the lake. Where?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.o2.text: Dive the shallows below the east window and find the Water Rose
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.o3.journa: The lower nave was lit with a pale glow that came from no lamp. Pews rose from silt like rows of drowned teeth. At the far end, below an arch, a figure in a canon's robe knelt in the silt, with its hands cupped around nothing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.o3.text: Fight through the drowned canons of the lower nave
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.o4.text: Put down the Drowned Canon who has kept the rose
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.o5.c0.lab: Put the rose back in the sill. A promise should be kept.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.o5.c0.rep: Then the lake will settle, and the lower nave will sleep. I will say a mass for the Canon. Thank you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.o5.c1.lab: Keep it down. Let the lake have its due, and let the cathedral move to higher ground.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.o5.c1.rep: Then we will move the altar, a stone at a time, to the hill. It will take a hundred years. I will not see it done. It is a good plan. I will go on saying so.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.o5.reply: The lake rises because it is lent. Whoever set that rose in the sill was not decorating. They were holding a promise. I may put it back, and the lake will settle, and the lower nave will drown for another nine centuries. Or I may leave it in the cold lower dark, and the lake will rise, and the cathedral will have to be abandoned in a generation. Which of these is the lesser sorrow?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.o5.text: Bring the Water Rose to Bishop Mallory Fenn
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.o5.topic: I have the rose. A canon in the lower nave was holding it. The lake rises because of it, I think.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.offer: Bishop, you said the cathedral lost something?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.outro: The Cathedral of Evermor still stands on its island. The lake is a little higher or a little lower than it was, and Lamplighter Vey, who has no opinion on the matter, goes on lighting seven hundred lamps.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.pitch: There is a glass rose in the lakebed, under the cathedral. It was set in the sill of the east window when the cathedral was founded, and it fell. Not stolen: fell. The window has wept since, and the nave floor is damp. The lake is rising a finger-joint each winter. I think the rose is holding something back, and I think it must be put back, or at least found. Take a boat. Look.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_ev_rose.title: The Water Rose
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_bell.desc: Old Corwin Tarne has heard the Lonely Tortoise's bell ring at low tide for thirty-one years. He wants it brought up, or explained.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_bell.o0.text: Wait for low tide at the wreck of the Lonely Tortoise
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_bell.o1.text: Drive the drowned crew from the wreck
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_bell.o2.journa: The bell hung in the forecastle on a rotten bracket. Wedged beside it was a crab no bigger than a thumbnail, working a small iron ring back and forth against the clapper. The bell rang once, in the dark, quite beautifully.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_bell.o2.text: Recover the ship-bell from the Tortoise's forecastle
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_bell.o3.reply: A crab! Thirty-one years, and it was a crab. Gods, I could weep. A crab that rings a bell for no reason. I could take its example. Give me the bell. I shall put it on my mantle. And at low tide, I shall go down to the shore with a bucket, and take the crab home, and call it the Captain.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_bell.o3.topic: A crab, Corwin. A very small crab, and a very good bell.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_bell.offer: Corwin, the bell rings at low tide?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_bell.outro: The bell of the Lonely Tortoise hangs on Old Corwin's mantle, and a very small crab named the Captain lives in a bucket by the fire.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_bell.pitch: At low tide, in the dead of night, the Tortoise's bell rings. I have heard it every winter for thirty-one years. I have never been brave enough to go down and look. I am an old man. I should like to know, before I die, whether it is a bell, or a ghost, or a crab. Take the bell and bring it up, if you can. Or tell me it is a crab.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_bell.title: The Bell of the Lonely Tortoise
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_light.desc: Glencombe Lighthouse has been dark for three nights and its keeper, Old Fenwick, has not been seen. Pilot Edda Marrow asks you to climb the tower and see.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_light.o0.text: Clear the lighthouse of what has crept in at the base
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_light.o1.text: Climb to the lamp room and find Old Fenwick
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_light.o2.reply: His lamp! The stubborn old fool. Fifty years and he will not sit still. I will take the lamp up myself tonight. And I shall sit with him until the leg is mended. Thank you. Take this. It is the pilot's knot, and it has never been tied for a stranger.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_light.o2.topic: The keeper is alive, Edda. He fell on the stair and broke his leg. Two days in the dark. He has asked for his lamp.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_light.outro: Glencombe Light burns again, tended by a pilot who has promised to spend a week in the tower, and a keeper who has promised, with his leg in a splint, to say thank you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_light.pitch: Glencombe Light has not shown in three nights. Old Fenwick, the keeper, has kept it fifty years and never let it go out. Something has happened to him. I cannot leave my boat; the tide will not wait. If you are brave, and if you are not sensible, go up there and see.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_light.title: The Keeper of Glencombe
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.desc: Glenpoint's salt-pans are selling twice what they produce, and the Count's tax-man is on the road. Reeve Dunstan Blythe wants the smugglers found and the landing sealed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o0.reply: On the dark of the moon, at slack water, between the Pilot's Rock and the lee of the headland. The tide is dead for a quarter-hour, and you can slip a ship in sideways. I have watched it three times and said nothing. I did not like my choices. Go to the pans tonight. They will land at the second hour.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o0.text: Ask Pilot Edda Marrow when the tides are wrong
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o0.topic: Someone is landing salt at Glenpoint. When would a boat come in unseen?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o1.reply: More than a kitchen! A man called Marrick, who says he cures hams. I have never seen a ham. He buys forty pounds at a time and pays in Skingrad silver. And he does not drink. A man who buys that much salt and does not drink is a man with something to preserve, and I would not like to know what.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o1.text: Ask Sorrel Whitlow who has been buying more salt than the Brine Pan needs
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o1.topic: The pans have sold twice what they produced. Has anyone been buying more salt than a kitchen could use?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o2.text: Watch the salt pans at the dark of the moon
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o3.text: Catch the landing crew at the salt pans
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o4.reply: The Emeric Crypt cove. Of course. That is where my father kept his boat. I thought it was sealed. It was merely quiet. Go. Seal it. Take as many men as you like from the Reeve's own, which is to say three.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o4.text: Show the Reeve the second tally
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o4.topic: The crew carried this. A second tally in the back. It names the cove they ship from.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o5.text: Seal the smugglers' cove and take Marrick Saltfist
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o6.c0.lab: Give it to the tax-man. The crooked pay. The honest ones can be spared.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o6.c0.rep: Then I will name only Saltfist's crew, and the pans will stand. It is the law, and it is just enough.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o6.c1.lab: Burn it. Let the tax-man find nothing, and the pans go on.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o6.c1.rep: Then there is no tally, and no landing, and the salt is only a very good harvest. I shall say so to anyone who asks.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o6.reply: The tally. The tax-man will want it. I will not give it to him. The pans were landed honest by the men who sold salt in the lee of the headland, and who did not know it was untaxed. Or I will give it to him, and the tax-man will find the smugglers, and the honest ones will pay for the crooked. Which is it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.o6.topic: The cove is sealed. Saltfist is down. What do you want to do with the tally?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.offer: Reeve, what is wrong with the pans?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.outro: The salt of Glenpoint is exactly the quantity it should be. The Brine Pan serves it with every dish, and Sorrel Whitlow has been heard to say that it has never tasted better.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.pitch: Salt tax is paid at the Gate, and every crate is stamped. This quarter we sold twice the salt we produced, and the Count's tax-man is on the road. Someone is landing untaxed salt, and mixing it into ours, and the books look as if we have made a miracle. I do not mind a miracle. I mind the hanging at the end of it. Find the landing. Stop it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_gp_salt.title: The Salt Run
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_after_doused.d: The second lamp has been doused. Keeper Sorley Vance asks you to sit with her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_after_doused.o: Dark. I put the lamp out at dusk and sat on the step and waited for the moor to be angry. It was not. A mist came up at midnight, very soft, and I thought I heard footsteps on the peat. Going away. Not coming. It is a kind of peace. I think they have gone home. I think Isolde has gone with them. I am not sure I mind. Take this. It was hers.
Sit with Keeper Sorley Vance on the first dark night
The moor is dark tonight. How are you?
The second lamp of Northpoint is dark, and the moor is quiet. Keeper Sorley Vance sits on the step each dusk and watches the mist go out.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_after_doused.p: The second lamp has been doused. Keeper Sorley Vance asks you to sit with her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_after_kept.des: The second lamp burns on as a grave-light, with a notice posted. Reeve Maude Harrow has news.
They have. Captains read it twice, and bow to the moor as they pass. One man left a ribbon at the first stake. The lamp burns, and a boy asked me yesterday why it is not a lighthouse. I told him that a lighthouse is for the living, and a grave-light is for the ones who did not get a lighthouse. He nodded. It is the best answer I have ever given.
Hear the Reeve's news of the posted notice
The notice is posted. Have the ships learned?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_after_kept.out: Ships steer by the tower and bow to the moor. The grave-light burns on, and no one has followed it astray.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_after_kept.pit: The second lamp burns on as a grave-light, with a notice posted. Reeve Maude Harrow has news.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_fog.desc: A boy has wandered out onto the Northpoint moor in the fog and the town's horn has not brought him home.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_fog.o0.text: Search the east fence of the moor in the fog
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_fog.o1.text: Drive off the moor-wolves circling the lost boy
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_fog.o2.text: Bring the boy home to Hester Dunmoor at the Fog Horn Arms
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_fog.o3.reply: He is safe! And scolded. And fed. And scolded again. Take this. It is the horn's own silver, struck on the night of the great fog. I have been saving it for someone who would walk into a fog without a lantern, and I find it was you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_fog.o3.text: Tell Hester Dunmoor the boy is safe
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_fog.o3.topic: He had a stick as long as a spear and a very bad attitude. He is safe.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_fog.outro: The boy of the Dunmoor farm has been forbidden to walk the moor alone. He has taken it as a challenge.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_fog.pitch: The fog came in at noon and Wilmer Dunmoor's boy went out for the sheep. It is now dusk. The horn is going every minute, and he cannot hear it, or will not. I cannot leave the horn. You can. Take a lantern and go east, along the fence, and look for a small boy with a very large stick.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_fog.title: Lost in the Fog
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.desc: A second, unmapped lamp burns on the Northpoint moor on moonless nights, and ships are steering by it. Reeve Maude Harrow wants to know whose it is.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o0.text: Watch the moor from the Bramgate Stones at dusk
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o1.text: Drive off the moor-lights luring travellers into the peat
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o2.reply: A book, a month ago. Preserved. A ship's diary, I think, from the Blue Tankard. It was in the oldest bank, at the bottom, tied to a skeleton's wrist. I did not read it. I put it in the church. The priest is not, I think, a man for old things.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o2.text: Ask Gill Thrupp what the peat cuttings have given up
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o2.topic: Reeve Harrow says a lamp burns on the moor. You cut the banks. What have you found?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o3.reply: Every captain who smokes his catch in my shed says the same thing. "The lamp on the moor is a good lamp." They say it as though it were a friend. I asked one of them whose it was. He said, "It is the Tankard's, and the Tankard is still out." Then he ordered a pound of eel and would not speak again.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o3.text: Ask Tolliver Quill what the shipmen say of the second lamp
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o3.topic: Reeve Harrow says ships are steering by a lamp on the moor. Do your customers say so?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o4.text: Lay the Blue Tankard's mate to rest
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o5.text: Dive the wreck of the Blue Tankard for the ship's lantern
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o6.c0.lab: Douse it. A lamp meant for one ship should not mislead a hundred.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o6.c0.rep: Then I will douse it, tonight, and sit in the dark, and she will not find her way. But the bay will. It is the right thing. I wish it were not.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o6.c1.lab: Keep it, but have the Reeve post a notice: this is a grave-light, not a beacon.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o6.c1.rep: A grave-light. Yes. That is what it is. Notice it is, and the ships will steer by the tower, as they were meant to. Thank you. You have a kinder head than most.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o6.reply: Mine. Hers. My wife Isolde's. She was the Tankard's navigator, and she did not come back. I light her lamp every moonless night, so she can find the shore. It is the only thing I have done right. And now ships steer by it, and I know it is wrong, and I cannot stop. What would you have me do?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o6.text: Show the lantern to Keeper Sorley Vance
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.o6.topic: I found the Blue Tankard's lantern. And the diary, from the peat. Whose is the second lamp?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.offer: Reeve, what is the matter with the moor?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.outro: The second lamp of Northpoint burns on, or does not, depending on the night and the notice board. The ships steer by the tower, and Sorley Vance sleeps better than he has in years.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.pitch: There is a second light on the moor. It comes at moonless dusk and burns until dawn, and every ship that passes Northpoint has seen it and set a course by it. I do not like that. A ship that steers by a light that is not on the chart is a ship that will find a rock. The lighthouse keeper says it is nothing. I say it is not nothing. Go and look, and bring me back a reason.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_lamp.title: The Second Lamp
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_peat.desc: Peat-Cutter Gill Thrupp says the moor is moving, and wants someone to look at the Westfield cutting and tell him what is digging.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_peat.o0.text: Clear whatever is digging in the Westfield peat cutting
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_peat.o1.text: Search the cutting for what the bog gave up
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_peat.o2.reply: A diary. Another. Gods. They all say the same thing. "I will leave the lamp lit." Forty diaries in forty years, and every one of them says it. I think the moor has been keeping its own. And I think the lamp is not Sorley's. I think it is older than the lighthouse. Thank you. I will put this in the church.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_peat.o2.text: Take what you found to Gill Thrupp
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_peat.o2.topic: The cutting was full of bog-walkers. Under the last bank I found this diary.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_peat.offer: Gill, you said the moor moves?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_peat.outro: Gill Thrupp has moved his stakes. The bank still creeps, but slower, and he has begun leaving a lamp on the cut's edge, lit, at dusk.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_peat.pitch: I have been tracking it with stakes. Eight stakes, set forty years ago, each a stride from the last. Now the third is gone, the fifth is where the sixth was, and the eighth is in the lighthouse yard. The moor is going somewhere, and it takes its dead with it. I do not like where they are going. Go to Westfield and look at the cutting. Tell me what is digging.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_np_peat.title: The Bank That Moves
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.desc: Mazgul gro-Dumbug runs the Seven Cups challenge at the Iron Throat. He wants three outside ales to compare against, and an outsider with a strong stomach.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.o0.reply: Wayrest ale. Hmm. Thin. Sweet. A Breton's drink. Good, it will make the others look worse. Now: I have seven tokens. Go to each of the seven cup-bearers in Orsinium. Each will give you a cup. Drink. Return. We shall see who is an orc.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.o0.text: Bring Mazgul three tankards of ale from outside
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.o0.topic: Three ales, brewed in Wayrest, as asked. Let the cup-bearers compare.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.o1.reply: First cup. It is not ale, it is a fermented tusk-broth. Drink. Do not breathe through your nose. ... Good. You did not cry. I have a second cup for you if you wish, which is worse.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.o1.text: Take the first cup from Hoardkeeper Bolgrat
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.o1.topic: Mazgul sent me. Seven cups. You are the first.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.o2.reply: Cup the second. I sing as you drink. It is a lament for orcs who did not finish theirs. Ahem. "Oh the cup, the cup, the bitter cup..." Done. Drink. That was a very fine song, and I shall not accept payment.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.o2.text: Take the second cup from Skald Torog
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.o2.topic: Bolgrat sent me. Your cup, Skald.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.o3.reply: Two! Two is more than most. Two is a fine number. Take the token. If you ever come back for the other five, I will have them ready, and I will have made them worse. It is, you understand, a compliment.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.o3.text: Return to Mazgul to claim the Iron Throat token
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.o3.topic: Two cups, and I stand. The rest I will take when I am less brave.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.offer: Mazgul, what are the seven cups?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.outro: The Iron Throat has a new name on its wall. It is small, and in chalk, and underlined twice. Mazgul has promised the other five cups will be ready any time you like.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.pitch: The Iron Throat has a tradition. Seven cups, seven houses of Orsinium, seven awful brews. Drink one from each and you are an honorary orc. Fail, and you pay for the other six. I do not care which. But if you take the challenge, bring me three ales from outside, so that the cup-bearers can compare. A fair contest needs a control.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_cups.title: The Trial of Seven Cups
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.desc: To stand beneath Chief Gulmak's banner, an outsider must prove worth at the forge, in the trial, at the wall, and by taking a clan name. Smith-Mother Ushra will set the first test.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o0.repl: Orichalcum. Green iron, orc-iron. A softer metal than the Bretons think, and a harder one than they deserve. Stand by the forge and watch your hands. A smith who cannot watch her hands is a smith who cannot be watched. Now. Carry the hammer to the Chieftain's hall. Do not drop it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o0.text: Bring four orichalcum ingots to Smith-Mother Ushra
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o0.topi: Four orichalcum ingots. For the forging.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o1.repl: Ready. The word is a hammer and a lie. No one is ready. You will fight Durbul Hammer-Knuckle in the yard, with your hands and a rough shield. If you fall, you rise. If you rise, he falls. If neither falls, he and I drink. I have never seen it come to that.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o1.text: Report to Chief Gulmak at the Chieftain's Hall
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o1.topi: Smith-Mother Ushra says I have passed the forge. I am ready for the Chieftain's trial.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o2.text: Defeat Durbul Hammer-Knuckle in the Chieftain's Trial
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o3.text: Man the wall with the garrison as the horn sounds
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o4.text: Defend the gate against Lurth the Gate-Breaker
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o5.c0.l: The forge. Smith-Mother Ushra tempered me.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o5.c0.r: Then you are a Forge-Born. Gro-Ushra. Your hammer-mark goes beside hers, and your name goes on the great anvil. Orsinium has a new smith.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o5.c1.l: The wall. The garrison held, and I held beside them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o5.c1.r: Then you are a Wall-Born. Gro-Gulmak. A very old name, and a very loud one. The garrison will drink in your honour for a week.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o5.repl: Gate stands, Lurth is down, and you stand. Then you will take a name. Not a clan name. A clan name is a thing you give a stranger. Yours will be one you earned, and I will give it to you in front of my whole hall. Choose whom to honour: the forge, or the wall?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o5.text: Return to Chief Gulmak to take your clan name
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.o5.topi: The gate stands. Lurth is down. I stand under your banner.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.offer: Smith-Mother, you said the gate needs a hammer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.outro: The gate-hammer of Orsinium hangs a little differently on its chain. A new name has been cut into the stone, and Skald Torog has been up all night composing a song with several more orcs in it than there were.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.pitch: Orsinium is half a city and half a promise. The gate is the promise. Every orc who wishes to stand under the Chieftain's banner must strike the gate with the great hammer, once, and say a name. It is a simple rite. Most orcs strike it and are done. A few strike it and are asked to prove it. I say you will be asked. Prove yourself at the forge first. A hammer that has not been tempered will not carry the name.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_hammer.title: Hammer on the Gate
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.desc: A Breton factor has been stuck outside the Merchant's Gate of Orsinium for six days, refusing to pay the toll. Chief Gulmak wants a bargain.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.o0.text: Meet the Breton factor Lysander Bray at the Merchant's Gate
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.o1.reply: Walls. The garrison. The road to the gate, which we mend each spring. And a portion for the tusk-shrine, which the Bretons do not know about. I will not take their silver for a shrine they do not worship. Tell Gulmak: charge them the stone-price, and let the tusk-shrine be paid by orcs.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.o1.text: Ask Hoardkeeper Bolgrat what the toll truly pays for
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.o1.topic: The Bretons say the toll is excessive. What does it truly pay for?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.o2.c0.lab: Tell the factor it was Gulmak's generosity.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.o2.c0.rep: A generous Chieftain. He will like that. It will cost him nothing and buy him a great deal.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.o2.c1.lab: Tell the factor it was Bolgrat's suggestion. The Hoardkeeper deserves the credit.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.o2.c1.rep: Then Bolgrat will be insufferable for a month, and Orsinium will be a little richer for it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.o2.reply: Charge less and sell more. It is not an orcish idea. It is a good one. The Breton may enter. Tell him I said so, and that he may bring whatever he likes, provided it is not a sword.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.o2.text: Carry the bargain to Chief Gulmak
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.o2.topic: Charge the Bretons for the stone only. Let orcs pay for the shrine. They will bring twice the trade.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.offer: Chieftain, the Merchant's Gate. A dispute?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.outro: The Merchant's Gate of Orsinium has a new sign in two languages. The Breton factor is said to be very pleased, and the garrison is said to be less so, and the tusk-shrine is, as ever, paid by orcs.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.pitch: The Bretons say we charge too much to enter. We say they are charged what the stone cost. Neither is lying. A Breton factor, Lysander Bray, has been waiting at the Merchant's Gate for six days and will not pay. My gate-wardens will not let him in. I will not be seen to lose to a Breton accountant. Go. Find a bargain.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_toll.title: The Price of the Merchant's Gate
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_tusk.desc: A Breton thief has taken the ancestor's tusk of Skald Torog's grandfather and fled west toward Ogrmok Delve. Hoardkeeper Bolgrat wants it back.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_tusk.o0.text: Clear the thief's hideout at Ogrmok Delve
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_tusk.o1.text: Catch Fenwick Bree, the thief with the good coat
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_tusk.o2.reply: The tusk. I thought I would never hold it again. Do not smile at me. I am an orc. I am not crying. I have a cold. Sit. I will sing the ancestor's song, and you will hear it. It is not long. It is only the length of one man's whole life.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_tusk.o2.text: Return the tusk to Skald Torog
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_tusk.o2.topic: Your grandfather's tusk. A thin Breton had it. He is not a thin Breton any longer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_tusk.outro: Skald Torog sings a new verse now, about a stranger who walked through a Breton thief and returned a grandfather. The verse is long, and the thief grows taller in every telling.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_tusk.pitch: A tusk. Not for sale, never for sale. It belongs to Skald Torog's grandfather. It was in my keeping because the Skald did not have a place for it. A Breton took it three days ago, a thin man with a very good coat. He said it was a curio. I said it was a grandfather. He did not think that was funny. He went west toward Ogrmok Delve. I would go myself, but I am old, and I am already angry, and an old angry orc is a dangerous thing to be.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_or_tusk.title: The Ancestor's Tusk
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_fletching.desc: Alder the Fletcher sponsors the garrison's annual shooting match at Shornhelm and wants an entrant who will buy his arrows and win with them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_fletching.o0.r: Honestly! Ha. Let me see. There. Nine arrows, and a very good quiver. Walk to the muster-ground and shoot. If you miss, the targets are not at fault.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_fletching.o0.t: Buy nine steel arrows from Alder the Fletcher for the match
Nine arrows, fletched in goose. I will shoot them honestly.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_fletching.o1.t: Shoot the first target from the muster-ground line
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_fletching.o2.t: Shoot the second target from the palisade
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_fletching.o3.j: The third target was a swinging barrel, and your last arrow caught the stave just as it turned. The garrison cheered. Sergeant Brom, rather unsteadily, raised a mug.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_fletching.o3.t: Shoot the third target from the gate arch
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_fletching.o4.r: You have. The red feather is yours, and the right to say my name without being struck. Do try to say it sparingly. And, if anyone asks, tell them Alder's arrows are, as always, grossly overpriced and exactly right.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_fletching.o4.t: Collect the red feather from Marshal Garreth
Nine arrows, three targets, one barrel. I believe I have won.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_fletching.offe: Alder, you are running a shooting match?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_fletching.outr: A red feather sits in the cap of the garrison's newest champion. Alder the Fletcher sold sixty arrows in an afternoon and has promised, in the name of his own honour, to not mention it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_fletching.pitc: The garrison has an archery match on the muster-ground every year. Three targets, three arrows each, nine arrows for the glory. The winner gets a red feather for the cap and the right to say the Marshal's name without being struck. I have sixty arrows to sell, and nobody to buy them. Win, and you will be famous. Lose, and you will be a customer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.desc: Marshal Ysolde Garreth has three men missing from the night muster of Shornhelm, one of them her best sergeant. She wants the list run, and the men found.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o0.text: Check the east gate post of the Night Muster
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o1.text: Check the north wall post of the Night Muster
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o2.text: Check the outer wall post of the Night Muster
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o3.repl: Three men who were at my stall a week ago, buying very expensive arrows and talking low. Brom was one. The others were Hale and a boy called Pip. They were going to a place in the old wall. Hale said, "a thing behind the buttress." I did not ask. A fletcher who asks is a fletcher who loses his best customers.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o3.text: Pay Alder the Fletcher eight steel arrows for what he overheard
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o3.topi: Eight steel arrows. Marshal Garreth has three men missing. What did you hear?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o4.repl: A thing. A hag, I think, or something that has been a hag for a hundred years. It came out of the stone one night, and Brom went in after it, and we have not seen him since. We ran. I am not proud of it. We saw nothing, and then we saw too much.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o4.text: Find Corporal Wat Hale at the outer wall
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o4.topi: Marshal Garreth has you down as missing, Corporal. What is behind the buttress?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o5.text: Wait for night and enter the outer wall behind the third buttress
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o6.text: Slay the Buttress Hag in the outer wall
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o7.repl: Because I was drinking the hag's wine, which is considerably better than the garrison's, and I did not wish to leave until it was gone. I am joking. I was bound, and gagged, and a very bad poet. Ysolde will have me flogged. Hale will have me thanked. Come, I know how to be sober for a day. I will do it for her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o7.text: Find Sergeant Brom Halloway where the Hag held him
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o7.topi: You were in the wall for a week, Sergeant. You are alive. Why did you not come out?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o8.c0.l: Bring them home. A soldier who runs and returns is still a soldier.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o8.c0.r: Then I will mark them returned and say nothing of the leave. A soldier is what a soldier is allowed to be. Thank you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o8.c1.l: Let them go. They have done enough for a lifetime of muster.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o8.c1.r: Then they are on extended leave, in perpetuity, with my blessing. I will tell Brom to say a very sober prayer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o8.repl: A hag. In my wall. Gods. And my men ran from her. I should flog them. I should not. Tell me honestly, and I will decide. Should I bring them home, as soldiers, or let them go as men?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o8.text: Report the night muster to Marshal Garreth
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.o8.topi: Brom is alive. Hale and the boy ran, but not from cowardice. A hag was in the wall. I have killed it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.offer: Marshal, you want someone to run the muster?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.outro: The night muster of Shornhelm counts true again. Sergeant Brom Halloway has been seen sober on three consecutive days, which the garrison regards as an omen.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.pitch: Every garrison has a night muster. Count the posts, count the men, count the bunks, report. Tonight, three names are missing from the count. One of them is my best sergeant. He is a drunk and I love him. The other two are men I do not know well enough to miss. I do not like missing men, and I like missing men I do not know even less. Run the list. Report.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_muster.title: Night Muster
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_standard.desc: The red keep's standard has turned up on the Thornham Stones, ringed by wolves. The garrison won't march without it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_standard.o0.te: Drive the wolves off the Thornham Stones
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_standard.o1.te: Take the standard from its ash staff
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_standard.o2.re: Red wool. Of course. Someone from the Red Keep put it there, or someone from the Red Keep was meant to think so. I will have the knot examined. Good. We march at dawn. Tell Hazel the garrison drinks free tonight, and tell her I said so only once.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_standard.o2.te: Return the standard to Marshal Garreth
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_standard.o2.to: The standard, Marshal. It was on the Thornham Stones among wolves. It was tied to an ash staff with red wool.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_standard.outro: The standard of the Red Keep flies from its proper pole once more. No one has claimed to have put it on the Thornham Stones, and the knot has been placed in a drawer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_standard.pitch: The red keep's own standard has gone missing from the muster pole. It turned up three nights later on the Thornham Stones, on a staff of ash, with wolves around it. I cannot say who put it there. I can say that the garrison will not march until it is back. A standard on the wrong pole is, as any soldier will tell you, bad luck, and bad luck in Rivenspire has teeth.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_sh_standard.title: The Banner on the Wrong Pole
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_after_buried.d: The doubled manifest was burned and only the pilot named. Quartermaster Jules Garrow knows more than he says.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_after_buried.o: Crates. I count crates, as I always have. But I count one more than I did before, and I put it on no manifest, and I carry it up to a certain house in the Lower Bridges every month. The pilot is hanged. The ship is a rumour. A woman who should not be in Wayrest is, and sleeps in her own bed. I have not told you any of this. I do not know you. Good evening.
Hear the Quartermaster's thoughts on the buried manifest
The book is ash. What do you count now?
Quartermaster Jules Garrow counts one extra crate each month and carries it up to a house in the Lower Bridges. Wayrest's harbour book has no record of it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_after_buried.p: The doubled manifest was burned and only the pilot named. Quartermaster Jules Garrow knows more than he says.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_after_named.de: Chamberlain Aumaric Dessaux took the doubled manifest to the Duchess himself. He wants to speak.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_after_named.o0: With a long silence, and then a very short sentence. She said: "You might have told me." I had no answer. She has not dismissed me. She has restored her sister to a house in the Lower Bridges and told no one. The Marguerite is a berth fee in the harbour book now, in plain ink. I sleep. Not well. But I sleep. Take this, in the Chamberlain's name.
Call on Chamberlain Dessaux after his audience with the Duchess
You told the Duchess. How did she take it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_after_named.ou: The Duchess of Wayrest knows her sister is in the city. The Marguerite has a berth, and the harbour chain is raised by honest hands.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_after_named.pi: Chamberlain Aumaric Dessaux took the doubled manifest to the Duchess himself. He wants to speak.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.desc: An unlisted ship, the Marguerite, passed Wayrest's harbour chain unchallenged four nights ago. Chamberlain Aumaric Dessaux wants to know who lowered the chain and why.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o0.reply: Nothing. That is what troubles me. No cargo on the manifest, no ballast in the log, and a draught that says she was riding heavy as a bull. A ship that carries nothing and rides like a bull has hidden something in her bones. I would look at her hold. But the harbour office will not let me go aboard.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o0.text: Ask Quartermaster Garrow about the Marguerite
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o0.topic: The Chamberlain says an unlisted ship passed the chain. You count the crates. What did she carry?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o1.text: Take the winding key from the Chain Tower lever-house
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o2.text: Raise the harbour chain by hand at the Chain Tower
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o3.text: Fight your way past the Marguerite's deck crew
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o4.journ: The hold was clean. No crates, no casks, no bilge. But under a false deck I found a cabin with a table and a locked chest, and in the chest, a doubled manifest, in two hands. The right column listed passengers, not cargo. One name had been struck through in the Chamberlain's own hand.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o4.text: Search the Marguerite's hold under the Chamberlain's eye
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o5.text: Take down Pilot Renaud Sabin, who lowered the chain
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o6.c0.la: Name the traitor and the master. The duchess should know what stands behind her own harbour.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o6.c0.re: Then I will carry the book to her myself. I have been a coward for eleven years. Let me finish what I started.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o6.c1.la: Name only the pilot. The sister is not a danger. She is a person who needs hiding.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o6.c1.re: Then the pilot hangs, the book burns, and the harbour goes back to counting crates. I owe you, and I do not forget debts.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o6.reply: Struck through. My own name. In my own hand. Ah. I see. I should tell you that this was a very small mistake, committed a long time ago, and that it has a very large shadow. The duchess does not know. I wrote it to protect a friend. The friend is on that list, and the friend is the duchess's sister, and she is not meant to be in Wayrest at all. What would you have me do?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o6.text: Bring the doubled manifest to Chamberlain Dessaux
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.o6.topic: The ship carried passengers, not cargo. And your own name is struck through in the right column.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.offer: Chamberlain, you spoke of a delicate matter.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.outro: The boom chain of Wayrest has been raised and lowered by lawful hands since. The Marguerite does not exist, and everyone in the harbour office has become very good at not looking at the third berth.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.pitch: A ship came through the harbour mouth four nights ago, in the dark, with no pilot of ours aboard and no manifest of ours on the quay. She is called the Marguerite. She is not listed. She should not exist. The duchess would prefer that she not be discussed. But she is, I assure you, in the harbour, and the boom chain was not raised to stop her. Someone in the harbour office decided it should not be. I want to know whom.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_chain.title: The Boom Chain
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.desc: The duchess's moonstone diadem has been stolen during the Seven Bridges Masque, and Madame Corisande Vray wants it found by a masked guest before anyone is embarrassed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.o0.repl: Early? No one leaves the Cormorant early. They leave late, or they leave embarrassed. But a masked woman asked me for the way to the sewers. A woman in grey silk, with a gold fox mask. I told her the sewers are not on the menu. She laughed. She said she knew.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.o0.text: Question the Cormorant's host about the masked guests
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.o0.topi: Someone at the Masque lifted the diadem. You host half the city. Who left early?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.o1.repl: To the old overflow, where the Gaudrel sisters used to keep their less respectable correspondence. She said she wanted to see what was left. She seemed disappointed. A gold fox, you say. I would follow her, but I am a man of fixed habits and the overflow is not one of them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.o1.text: Ask Pike the Sewer-Warden about a woman in a gold fox mask
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.o1.topi: A woman in a gold fox mask came down your stairs, tonight. Where did she go?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.o2.jour: The overflow chamber was empty, but for a small gold fox mask on the floor and a moonstone diadem set carefully on a cold stone altar, as if it had been returned. A note under it said: "I only wanted to wear it once."
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.o2.text: Find the diadem in the overflow chamber below the Masque
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.o3.c0.l: Say nothing to the Dessaux household. The note is not yours to answer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.o3.c0.r: Then it is a quiet little matter, and very Breton. I thank you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.o3.c1.l: Return it to the duchess in person and tell her of the note.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.o3.c1.r: Then she will have a very interesting evening. You are a braver soul than I.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.o3.repl: A gold fox. I sold that mask to a duchess. Not this duchess. The old one, who is, I am told, a very fine person. Well, the mask is gone and the diadem is back, and I shall say nothing. Take this. If you ever need a glove that fits a very particular hand, come and see me.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.o3.text: Return the diadem to Madame Vray
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.o3.topi: The diadem is whole. Whoever wore it left a note, and a gold fox mask.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.offer: Madame Vray, you needed a masked guest?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.outro: The Seven Bridges Masque ended with one moonstone diadem and no embarrassment. Madame Corisande Vray has put a gold fox mask in her window, and does not sell it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.pitch: I have sold three hundred masks for the Seven Bridges Masque, and the duchess's moonstone diadem has gone missing from the Dessaux box before the music has even begun. It was taken by someone wearing one of my masks. Someone I sold a mask to. That is, shall we say, bad for business. Go as a guest, find the mask that does not fit its face, and bring me back the diadem before anyone is embarrassed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_masque.title: The Masque of Seven Bridges
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_quay.desc: Wayrest's quay merchants think the Quartermaster's scales are rigged. Quartermaster Jules Garrow says the false weights are inside the Merchant Guildhall itself.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_quay.o0.text: Search the Merchant Guildhall's weight cupboard on the quay
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_quay.o1.text: Drive off the Guildhall's hired watchmen
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_quay.o2.c0.lab: Expose them. A cheat on the quay is a cheat on the whole bay.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_quay.o2.c0.rep: Then I shall nail the weights to the Guildhall door. A long overdue lesson in the cost of courtesy.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_quay.o2.c1.lab: Swap the weights quietly. The quay needs honest scales more than a scandal.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_quay.o2.c1.rep: Then it shall be done by morning, and no one the wiser. You have a politician's soul.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_quay.o2.reply: A hair. Yes. It adds up to a stone in a week and a sack in a month. Now. A Guildhall that cheats its own members is a Guildhall that can be unseated, and there are men on the council who will pay a good deal to unseat it. Or I can fix the weights quietly and let the Guildhall keep its dignity. Which is the less Breton?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_quay.o2.text: Bring the false weights to the Quartermaster
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_quay.o2.topic: The cupboard held these. Every one is a hair too light.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_quay.offer: Quartermaster, you said the weights were wrong.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_quay.outro: The quay at Wayrest weighs honest now, or very nearly. Master Ferrand Lisle was heard to compose a couplet about it, which was the highest praise the harbour could give.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_quay.pitch: Every merchant on the Wayrest quay pays a tithe by weight, and every merchant on the quay says the scale is cheating him. The Merchant Guildhall says it is the Quartermaster. I say it is a set of false weights somebody has slipped into the guild's own cupboard. I cannot search the Guildhall. You can. Find them. Let a Breton merchant be cheated by a Breton merchant for once, and let it be provable.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_quay.title: The Quay Tithe
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_ring.desc: An old woman of Wayrest dropped a betrothal ring into the harbour eleven years ago, and wishes to know it was not lost. Sister Odelle asks you to dive for it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_ring.o0.text: Drive off the harbour crabs at the old pier
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_ring.o1.text: Dive for the ring beneath the old pier
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_ring.o2.reply: The mussels! Of course. Thank you. I will take it to her. And I shall say nothing of the sailor, who is a better man for being forgotten. Take this, with the Sisterhood's blessing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_ring.o2.text: Return the ring to Sister Odelle
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_ring.o2.topic: It was under the old pier, in the mud, in a bed of mussels. The mussels had kept it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_ring.offer: Sister Odelle, you wanted a diver?
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_ring.outro: An old woman of Wayrest wears a ring on a ribbon round her neck now. Sister Odelle says it is for luck, and that the sea has never been unkind to her since.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_ring.pitch: There is a custom here. A sailor's betrothed drops a ring into the harbour for luck, and the sailor fishes it out on his return. Eleven years ago a girl dropped hers off the old pier, and her sailor never returned, and the ring is still down there. She has married since. Another man. She is happy. But a woman in her last years wishes to know the ring was not lost. Will you look? I would ask her husband, but he would be hurt.
story.skycraft.q.mq_hr_wy_ring.title: A Ring for the Sea-Wives
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_duelnight.des: Councilor Brara has accepted a formal duel in the cousin's place, and you are her second.
Three rules. Do not strike a man who has yielded. Do not yield to a man who has not struck. Do not look at the Council, because they will be looking at you, and it is vulgar to look back.
Seek Durgul Ash-Born for the formal rules
I am to second a duel before the Council. Teach me the rite.
Second Councilor Brara in the formal duel
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_duelnight.out: The champion yielded; the Council was silent a long time, then they struck the floor with their staves, which in Ald'ruhn is applause.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.desc: Councilor Brara needs an impartial witness to a Redoran duel at the gate of the Skar.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.o0.jou: The cousins bowed, crossed blades, and one of them stumbled backward, clutching a scratch no deeper than a thorn-prick. He was dead before the second bell had rung.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.o0.tex: Witness the duel at the gate of the Skar
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.o1.rep: A scratch will not. Resin on a blade might. It is a poison, not a weapon of honour, and honour is the one thing the Redoran may not forgive. Take it to the apothecary, Tevra Dren, quietly.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.o1.tex: Ask the guard-captain to examine the blade
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.o1.top: A scratch should not kill a man. May I see the blade?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.o2.rep: Kwama-egg resin, boiled and thickened. Only one kind of person has a vat like that: a miner with a grudge and a licence. Try the egg-mine tunnels, below the Skar, behind the third gallery.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.o2.top: What is this resin? Whose receipt?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.o3.tex: Track the poisoner into the egg-mine tunnels
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.o5.tex: Take the poisoner's jar and the receipt
Accept the duel in his place. Let the Council see you fight.
It will be a good evening. Bring a cloak; the shell is cold.
Make him answer for himself. Let the Council judge.
Then he stands before his peers with nothing but his name. It is the harsher sentence, and the more honest.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.o6.rep: My own cousin bought it. Twice. And paid with a House ring. Under Redoran law the accused may demand a duel; I may accept in his place, or I may stand down and let him defend his own name. Which shall it be, witness?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.o6.tex: Present the proof to the Council
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.o6.top: Councilor, here is the poisoner, the vat, and the buyer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.offer: You have the look of a witness. Are you one?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.outro: Redoran honour was satisfied, and the shell stood as it has stood for ages.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.pitch: A duel will be fought at the gate of the Skar at the second bell. Two Redoran cousins, one old grievance. I need a witness who owes neither house a favour, because I suspect the grievance is not what the cousins believe it is. Watch the blades. Particularly the blades.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_honour.title: The Honour of the Shell
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.desc: Nerva Hlavis of the Rat in the Pot is being fined for her sign. She wants proof the rat is a mascot, not a pest.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.o0.reply: Reported? The inspector's cousin runs the tavern across the way: the Skar's Last Word. Only a very jealous man could notice a sign that high up. Bring a witness who has eaten here for years. That would be me, sera, and I am free at the second bell.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.o0.text: Ask Brarmin who first called the pot rat-infested
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.o0.topic: Who reported the Rat in the Pot?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.o1.journa: The inspector came, ate three bowls, and could not stop staring at the sign. He did not leave a tip. He left an apology.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.o1.text: Bring the Council inspector to the pot for an honest tasting
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.o2.reply: Then we have both survived an honest day. I will name a stew for you. Do not ask which one; it is the one nobody orders.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.o2.topic: The inspector has withdrawn the fine.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.offer: You look like you have eaten somewhere worse than here.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.outro: The sign still has a rat on it. It now has a very small crown.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.pitch: There was a rat. It's on the sign. Last week a Council inspector found the sign, found the rat, and fined me for 'advertising a pest.' Prove the rat is a mascot, not a menace. The fine is nine drakes a day and my tolerance for this is limited.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.title: The Rat in the Pot, Honestly
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.desc: Brarmin the egg-miner hears a tune rising from the tunnels beneath the Skar.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.o0.jou: The wrong third note comes from a row of clay pipes set into the wall, tuned to the wind. Somebody has built a flute that plays the whole shell.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.o0.tex: Follow the three-note tune down into the old egg tunnels
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.o1.tex: Silence what has gathered to listen
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.o2.rep: Then it was a prank by dead masons, and it will ring on the ninth day of every Sun's Dusk. I shall hang a bell in the cellar. If it chimes the third note, I will whistle the right one.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.o2.top: Pipes in the wall. A tune only the wind could play.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.offer: You do not whistle, do you? Say you do not whistle.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.outro: The shell sings on certain nights, and everyone in Ald'ruhn now knows the proper third note.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.pitch: The shell has ribs, sera, and the ribs have hollows, and the hollows hum when the wind is right. Last night a new note came up through the floor of my cellar. Not a hum. A tune. Three notes, and the third was wrong. I do not like a song I have not been taught.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.title: Whistle Not Under the Shell
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ash.desc: The ledgers burned. The people they ruined want to say thank you, and some others want to ask why.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ash.o0.reply: Then somebody I know is out of debt, and somebody I used to know is out of work. I have a mind to throw a dinner. Go and make sure nobody throws a knife.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ash.o0.text: Meet Nilena at the south-bank steps
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ash.o0.topic: It is done. The ledgers are ash.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ash.o1.text: Defend the south-bank steps from the ruined bookkeeper's men
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ash.outro: Balmora ate well that night, and nobody asked for a receipt.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ash.title: Ash on the Odai
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.desc: Factor Dron Hlaalu wants three ledgers from three places: a fence on the south bank, the Council Manor, and a toll-keeper on the bridge.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o0.re: A freight consultant never holds, sera; she merely receives. The ledger is in the second crate, left of the sacks. And, for free: whoever wrote it kept a second book in the Council Manor, and I am not the only one who knows.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o0.te: Buy the first ledger from Nilena Vandas
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o0.to: Factor Dron says you are holding something for him.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o1.jo: The Manor smells of beeswax and old favours. A ledger sits unwatched in the steward's study, which means somebody wants it taken.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o1.te: Slip into the Council Manor and find the steward's ledger
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o2.te: Take the second ledger from the steward's study
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o3.te: Meet the toll-keeper's ambush on the high bridge
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o4.c0: Sell all three to the Temple.
Splendid. Rivals are expensive. Temple justice is ruinous. I shall send flowers.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o4.c1: Burn all three. The river has had enough.
A merciful fool, or a very clever one. I shall decide over breakfast.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o4.re: Now I own the river a little more than yesterday, and you are the only person who knows the number of ledgers I needed. I could pay you. I could sell all three to the Temple, who would pay far better and ruin my rival. Or burn them, and be clean. It is, I am told, a matter of taste.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o4.te: Hand the three ledgers to Dron
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o4.to: All three. River dues, Manor tallies, and the bridge toll. What now?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.offer: A man in my position cannot be seen to ask what I am about to ask.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.outro: The Odai ran as it always had, and nobody on either bank could say who owned it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.pitch: Three ledgers, three banks, one rival merchant who has hidden the truth of his river dues in each. I will not be seen to take them. You, on the other hand, are nobody, which is the most useful thing in Balmora. The first is with a fence on the south bank. Pay the fence. Do not ask for a receipt.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.title: Three Ledgers, One River
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.desc: Sirela Marvos of Eight Plates wants a nameless girl's letter delivered to a ship, safely.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.o0.rep: It is addressed to nobody and sealed in plain wax. Mind the Hlaalu men at the bridge; they have been asking after a grey cloak.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.o0.tex: Take the letter from the ninth guest
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.o0.top: I will carry it for her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.o1.tex: Get through the bridge-watch asking after a grey cloak
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.o2.rep: A letter for nobody. I have been waiting two years for this letter. The boat leaves tonight, and she will be on it. You never saw her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.o2.tex: Give the letter to the silt-strider captain
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.o2.top: This is for the west-dock boat.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.offer: You are hungry. Sit. No, not that seat. That one has a reservation.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.outro: The ninth plate was set out the next night too, and nobody sat at it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.pitch: Eight plates a night, no more. The ninth person goes hungry. Tonight she is a girl in a grey cloak who will not take charity, only work. She needs a letter carried to a boat at the west docks and she says it will end badly for whoever carries it. I would like it to end better.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.title: The Ninth Plate
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.desc: Port-Master Orrel has a silt strider that will not budge, and he suspects something beneath her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.o0.jo: A neat square hole under her middle leg, packed with silk. Somebody dug here and has been coming back at night.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.o0.te: Examine the strider in the caravan yard
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.o1.te: Catch the smugglers coming back for their cache
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.o2.re: Then she is a better citizen than half this town. Keep the silk, report the skooma, and for pity's sake, do not tell her she has been brave. It goes to her head.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.o2.te: Tell Orrel what Dowager was guarding
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.o2.to: She was sitting on a smuggler's cache. Silk and skooma.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.offer: Do you have a calm voice? A very, very calm voice?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.outro: Dowager rose the next morning with a long, sceptical sigh.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.pitch: Old Dowager has not moved in six days. A strider will not stand still for six days unless it is sulking, ill, or sitting on something. I have checked sulking. Take a lantern and a bucket of sorrow and have a look under her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.title: The Strider Who Wouldn't Walk
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_trial.desc: The ledgers are in the Temple. Witnesses are needed, and the factor's rival is not happy.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_trial.o0.repl: Then they will be crossing under my eye. I am not hiring a protector, sera; I am being thorough. Come at dawn and walk where I say.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_trial.o0.text: Ask the bridge guard to escort the witnesses
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_trial.o0.topi: The Temple wants witnesses crossing the bridge by morning.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_trial.o1.text: Break the rival's attempt to drown the witnesses
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_trial.outro: The witnesses reached the Temple dry and rather annoyed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_trial.title: The Temple Reads the River
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.desc: Legate Corvus Pello wants the name of whoever is selling gate keys into the Dunmer quarter.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o0.rep: Not 'who', sera, 'which'. There are three sellers and one customer. The customer is a Legion officer who buys one on the first of every month. I do not name officers for free.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o0.tex: Ask Aryn the Informer who sells the keys
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o1.jou: At the third bell a guard unlocked the south gate, took a purse from a shadow and said nothing. He did not look back. He locked it again after the shadow had passed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o1.tex: Slip into the Dunmer quarter and watch the south gate
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o2.rep: My mother is sick. The Legion pays in coin that does not arrive. I sell the gate; I do not sell the walls. Please. Take this list, and this key. And tell no one my mother's name.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o2.tex: Turn the guard who sells the keys
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o2.top: I saw you sell the south gate. I am not Legion. Tell me why.
Arrest the guard and publish the list.
Order restored. The Quarter will remember me as the man who punished a son for his mother. I will bear it.
Disarm the plot. Take the list to the Quarter Elders instead.
The Elders will decide, and decide wisely, which I could not. You have wasted the Legion's time and saved it from a mistake.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o3.rep: A guard, sixty drakes, a sick mother. I could have him flogged in the square. I could burn the list and let the gate go on as it has. Or I could keep the list, and have you walk it to the Quarter Elders instead. I will take the lesson you give me.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o3.tex: Bring the list to Legate Corvus
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o3.top: Here is your name. And your buyer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.offer: You are not Legion, not Dunmer, not Company. Good. You are nobody.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.outro: The south gate was locked properly that week, and a sick woman was found a physician.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.pitch: Someone is selling keys to the Dunmer quarter gate. A key buys a night's entry, a barrel's smuggling, a knife in the dark. I want the seller's name by sunrise and I would like it delivered quietly. A man who is arrested by rumour is a martyr by morning. Go in, ask, come out. Do not wear Legion colours.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.title: The Bastion and the Quarter
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_confession.des: Chaplain Loris needs an outsider to learn why three guards confessed the same sin.
At dusk the three guards left their posts together, crossed the bridge without speaking, and stood in a field of ash-flowers looking at a small stone. They did not pray. They saluted.
Watch the garrison walls at the lamp-lighting hour
Their fourth. Died last winter on a night watch when the lamp went out. They each left their post to tend a lamp for him. They would be flogged for it. They would do it again. Do not tell the Legate.
Ask Marga Ironhand about the stone
Three guards salute a stone in the ash-flowers. Whose?
Then I shall confess it for them, in the only way I can: I shall relight the lamp myself at the right hour, and let the walls think it is routine. Bless you. And bless a very quiet war.
It is a lamp for a dead comrade. Nothing worse.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_confession.off: Do you confess? I do not ask, but I hear.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_confession.out: The garrison lamp has not gone out since.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_confession.pit: Three of the garrison have confessed the same sin this week, in three different words: a night off the walls, a gate left open, and a lamp left lit. Each was told to speak to no one. I must break the seal if I am to prevent it. I need an outsider to ask where they were, without ever asking.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.desc: Felmin Rothal wants to know what the Company parrot's repeated sum means.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.o0.jour: The parrot says: "Four hundred and twelve. Silk. Pay at dusk. Do not tell the Factor." Then it says a name I cannot print.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.o0.text: Listen to the parrot in the customs yard
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.o1.repl: A clerk named Vedran, fired last month for double-booking. He has been paying the dockhands to forward the silk his way. The parrot was his; he left it behind. Parrots, sera, are very poor at keeping secrets.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.o1.text: Ask Aryn whose voice the parrot copies
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.o1.topi: The parrot speaks like a Hlaalu clerk. Which?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.o2.repl: A dishonest clerk undone by a bird. I shall give the bird a promotion. A small one. A cracker and a perch.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.o2.topi: The sum is a smuggled silk shipment. Vedran, the sacked clerk.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.offer: Do you speak parrot? No? A shame. Neither does anyone here.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.outro: The parrot now says "Order. Order. Order." in a very flat voice.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.pitch: A Company parrot has been repeating a sum in the customs yard for three days. Nobody knows what it means. It is either a ransom, a price, or a lottery. It is four hundred and twelve drakes, repeated every ten minutes, in a Hlaalu accent. Find out whose.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.title: The Customs Yard Parrot
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_hotbrass.desc: What you took from the vault is warm to the touch, and someone is following the heat.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_hotbrass.o0.re: I know three, and two will kill you. I will take the third. Keep walking the plaza; do not look behind you, sera, because everyone else will.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_hotbrass.o0.te: Fence the brass through Ravos Dren
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_hotbrass.o0.to: I have something warm. You know a buyer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_hotbrass.o1.te: Shake off the Temple's watchers in the plaza
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_hotbrass.outro: You ended the night richer and a little lighter in the head. The brass is somebody else's problem now.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_hotbrass.title: Hot Brass
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.desc: Lisara Tervyn, a palace archivist, has a map of a palace that exists only under Mournhold.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o0.repl: Right? It is the only one that is. Walk it backwards and you will find the throne room first. Do not sit in the chair. The chair is for someone, and he has been late for a long time.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o0.text: Ask Old Sedyn if the reversed palace map is true
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o0.topi: This map shows the Palace upside down. Is it right?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o1.jour: Stairs that rise when you go down. A window with an interior sky. A door where the map said, and a note in a clerk's hand: "Do not stay."
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o1.text: Walk the palace plan in reverse
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o2.text: Retrieve the seal from the reversed throne room
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o3.repl: Then the archive has a second basement after all, and I shall have to resign or go mad. Thank you. Please never come into my office again.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o3.topi: The reversed palace is real. I brought its seal.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.offer: Can you hold your tongue about basements?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.outro: The archivist now files the second basement under "Weather".
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.pitch: Every palace map I catalogue is accurate except one, and it is accurate in reverse. It describes a palace that does not exist above ground. It describes the one below. Take this tracing to Old Sedyn and ask whether the maps are true; I am forbidden to ask, and cannot stop wondering.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.title: The Palace Has a Reflection
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_quietbell.desc: The Temple is grateful and wants a favour done in the quiet hours.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_quietbell.o0.r: The one who tried to lease the vault will try again, with muscle. Stand in the courtyard at dusk. You need not do anything but be seen to wait.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_quietbell.o0.t: Meet the Archcanon at the dawn bell
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_quietbell.o1.t: Meet the lessor's hirelings at dusk
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_quietbell.outr: The courtyard bells rang at dusk and nobody ever mentioned why.
