Now that is a partnership. The skooma will flow, the coin will flow, and nobody will ask where the Krin's arrows came from.
story.skycraft.q.rk_sugar_and_steel.o2.t: Settle the terms of the alliance
story.skycraft.q.rk_sugar_and_steel.o4.t: Collect the crate of smuggled steel
story.skycraft.q.rk_sugar_and_steel.o5.r: Pickled fish. Ha. Good. I will not ask what you promised him. One day the bill will come, and we will pay it then.
story.skycraft.q.rk_sugar_and_steel.o5.t: Senchal steel, and an arrangement with Dar'jazad.
story.skycraft.q.rk_sugar_and_steel.outr: I struck a bargain with the Senchal smuggler Dar'jazad and brought a crate of steel back past the Thalmor customs post. The Renrijra Krin are armed, and indebted.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.desc: Lord Ri'Vasha, the Anequinan noble who sells his own people's grain and sons to the Thalmor, has a Thalmor guard at his estate west of Rimmen. Shazrah means to end him, and she wants me at the head of the attack.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o0.re: Ri'Vasha's estate. He has Thalmor at his gate and Thalmor gold in his vault. Go in first. When he falls, the rest of his house will fall with him.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o0.to: We're armed. Where do we strike?
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o1.te: Lead the attack on Ri'Vasha's estate
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o3.jo: Ri'Vasha told me the Renrijra were thieves who would starve Anequina within a year. He may even have believed it. He died in a room full of grain.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o4.re: Servants, cooks, a steward, a few cousins. Some fed the Thalmor. Most only fed Ri'Vasha. The band is waiting on your word.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o4.to: Ri'Vasha is dead. What of his household?
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o5.c0: Open the granary to the villages. Let the servants go.
A Laughing Blade who feeds people. The priests will not know what to say about you.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.o5.c1: Burn it. Let every noble in Anequina smell the smoke.
Fear is a weapon too. They will smell it in Riverhold. They may not forgive us for it.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.outro: I led the Renrijra Krin against Lord Ri'Vasha's estate and killed him among his Thalmor guards. Warlord Shazrah named me a Laughing Blade.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_last_laugh.title: The Last Laugh
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.desc: Shazrah sent me to take Lord Ri'Vasha's sugar tithe from a caravan on the road outside Rimmen. The guards serve the noble; the traders only drive his wagons.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.o0.te: Find the caravan on the road outside Rimmen
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.o2.re: Rawan-dar has a wife in Rimmen and two kits who think he sells silk. Please. Take the sugar. Take the silk, too. Only let us go.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.o2.to: The guards are dead. That leaves you.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.o3.c0: Take the sugar. Go home to your kits.
The moons see you. Rawan-dar will tell no one which way you went. He will not even tell himself.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.o3.c1: No witnesses. Shazrah's rule, not mine.
Rawan-dar understands. He does not forgive, but he understands.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.o5.re: Good. Whatever you did on that road, you did it, not me. That is how it works here. Each of us carries our own weight.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.outro: I took Lord Ri'Vasha's sugar tithe from his caravan. What became of the traders was my own choice, and Shazrah made sure I knew it.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.pitch: A caravan carries Lord Ri'Vasha's sugar tithe south of the city. The guards are his. The traders are not; they are hired, and poor, and frightened. What you do with them is your business. The sugar is mine.
story.skycraft.q.rk_the_spice_road.title: The Spice Road
story.skycraft.q.sh_krev_the_skinner.des: Krev the Skinner leads the Silver Hand from the ruined fort of Gallows Rock. Brenna Ashfall wants him stopped before he takes revenge for Greymoor.
Fight through the Silver Hand at Gallows Rock
Krev talked the whole fight: about beasts, about blood, about the pelts he would hang in his hall. He stopped talking at the end.
Then the Silver Hand have lost their knife. But a knife needs a hand to hold it. Krev took orders from someone. I want to know who.
story.skycraft.q.sh_krev_the_skinner.out: I killed Krev the Skinner at Gallows Rock. Brenna Ashfall believes someone above Krev still holds the Silver Hand together.
story.skycraft.q.sh_silver_under_greymoo: The list was written at Fort Greymoor, a Silver Hand hideout west of Whiterun. Njada Stonearm of the Companions went there to settle it alone and has not come back.
Fight through the Silver Hand in the fort
Hrafnhild kept a branding iron shaped like a silver hand heating in the brazier. Njada was chained beside it, and had not yet been marked.
Kill Hrafnhild Silver-Brand, the fort's warden
I can stand, walk and hit things. A Vigilant's errand-runner, saving a Companion? Don't tell Vilkas. Get me out of here and I'll owe you a drink, maybe two.
Good. Whatever the Companions are, they did not deserve that. Hrafnhild answered to Krev the Skinner. He holds Gallows Rock, and he will know by now what we did.
Greymoor is ours. Njada is home in Jorrvaskr.
I cleared the Silver Hand from Fort Greymoor and brought Njada Stonearm of the Companions home alive. Their warden answered to Krev the Skinner of Gallows Rock.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.desc: With Krev the Skinner dead, the Silver Hand in Skyrim answer to one man: Varek Silverfist. Brenna Ashfall has word of a courier carrying his orders on the road north of Whiterun.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o0.r: Krev was the knife. Varek Silverfist is the hand that holds it, and nobody has seen his face in years. A courier rides for him on the road north of the city. Take what he carries.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o0.t: Krev is dead. Is it over?
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o1.t: Stop Varek's courier on the north road
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o3.r: Arrogant enough to write it all down. He gathers the last of them at Driftshade Refuge, north in the Pale. I'm coming with you. Njada says she is too, and I have stopped arguing with her.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o3.t: Bring Varek's journal to Vigilant Ashfall
The courier was carrying Varek's own journal.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o5.j: They kept a werewolf in chains to train their recruits, starved half to madness. When the chains broke, it went for the hunters first.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o5.t: Break the Silver Hand's last stronghold
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o6.j: Varek wore a gauntlet of real silver, his whole right hand. He swore the beasts would inherit Skyrim without him. Then he fell, and the gauntlet rang on the stone.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.o7.r: In Skyrim, at least. Take this. It was Varek's, and it has hunted too many innocent people. Let it hunt something that deserves it.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_last_silver.outr: I took Varek Silverfist's journal from his courier and followed it to Driftshade Refuge, where I killed him and broke the last of the Silver Hand in Skyrim.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_skinners_list.de: Vigilant Brenna Ashfall believes the Silver Hand, a band of self-styled werewolf hunters, murdered a pelt-trader at Chillfurrow Farm because he did business with the Companions.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_skinners_list.o0: He sold wolf pelts to Jorrvaskr for twenty years. That's all. They came at night with silver arrows and said he was 'feeding the beasts.' They camp in the gully east of here. I can still hear them laughing.
Speak with Sigrun at Chillfurrow Farm
Vigilant Ashfall sent me. I'm sorry about your husband.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_skinners_list.o1: The stalkers had a fire going and Sigrun's furs drying beside it. One of them was wearing her husband's boots.
Clear the Silver Hand camp east of the farm
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_skinners_list.o3: Bring the list to Vigilant Ashfall in Whiterun
The Silver Hand were carrying this. It's a list of names.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_skinners_list.of: You look like someone who's lost a trail.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_skinners_list.ou: The Silver Hand murdered a pelt-trader for selling furs to the Companions, and they carry a list of others marked to die. Vigilant Brenna Ashfall means to end them.
story.skycraft.q.sh_the_skinners_list.pi: Not lost. Followed it too far. The Silver Hand murdered a pelt-trader at Chillfurrow Farm because he sold furs to the Companions. They call it hunting werewolves. I call it butchery, and I mean to prove it. Will you help?
story.skycraft.q.side_aka_the_broken_oat: Magistra Ulrika Varo of Solitude asked me to find the Dragonguard's founding oath, left long ago in a Tsaesci shrine on the coast of Akavir.
Land on the serpent coast of Akavir
Cross the field of dragon bones
Find the tidal shrine beyond the bone field
The oath was not to guard emperors. Nine Akaviri swore to hunt the dragons of Tamriel and send the last one alive to the serpent-kings. The Blades' great tradition began as a hunting contract.
Take the oath-scroll from the shrine's altar
Publish it. History should be true, even when it stings.
Then the Imperial Library will have a very uncomfortable autumn. Good.
Seal it away. Some debts are better forgotten.
Sealed, then. In the vault, under my own key. I'll sleep worse for it, I think.
A hunting contract. Signed in blood. Every heroic ballad about the Dragonguard just turned into a bill of sale. What on Nirn do I do with this?
Bring the oath to Magistra Ulrika
The Dragonguard's oath. You'll want to sit down.
The Dragonguard's oath has left Akavir after two thousand years. Vhezhar's katana, carried by the last Coil-Priest, came with me.

The Dragonguard. The Akaviri who came west with their swords and stayed to guard the emperors. Every history says they swore an oath before they sailed, and left it in a shrine on the serpent coast of Akavir. Nobody has ever read it. I am too old for boats. You, I suspect, are not too wise for them.
story.skycraft.q.side_aka_the_ice_drum.d: Maveri Sadras of Sadrith Mora hears a war-drum in her scrying-bowl and fears the Kamal will march again. She asked me to destroy it.
story.skycraft.q.side_aka_the_ice_drum.o: Land on the frozen shore of Kamal
The drum wasn't calling the Kamal to war. It was keeping them asleep. The war-chief Dir-Haskarr wanted it silenced.
Follow the drumbeat to the hall of blue ice
Kill Dir-Haskarr before he silences the drum
I left the old drummer beating it.
Then let him play. I'll listen every night, and if he ever stops, I'll know to run.
I cut a scrap of the drumhead as proof.
A frozen skin that trembles on its own. Delightful. I'll study it very, very carefully.
A lullaby. I heard a lullaby and called it a war-song. Well. I suppose I owe the north an apology. What did you do with it?
Return to Maveri in Sadrith Mora
I found your drum. Destroying it would have woken the whole host.
The Ice-Drum of Kamal still beats, slow and steady. Dir-Haskarr will not be waking anyone.
story.skycraft.q.side_aka_the_ice_drum.p: Drums. In Kamal, the frozen north of Akavir. Our grandmothers still tell how the snow demons came over the ice to Morrowind. My scrying-bowl has frosted over every night this month, and I hear a drum beating under the frost. Find that drum and destroy it, before it calls them south again.
story.skycraft.q.side_atm_the_cold_heart: Brunhild Keelwright of Windhelm asked me to sail to Atmora and learn what became of her great-grandfather Ulfvar, who went to fetch his clan's ancient hearthstone.
Make landfall on the frozen coast of Atmora
Shore Wraith
Drive off the wraiths around Ulfvar's frozen longship
Ulfvar's last entry: 'Found the longhouse. Lit the stone. It burns blue. So cold. The others sit down at the tables and will not rise.'
Chip Ulfvar's log out of the ice
Find the drowned longhouse in the frozen forest
Atmoran Hearth-Guard
Break the hearth-guard of the first Atmorans
Ysgrim Hearth-Jarl fell beside his blue fire. Ulfvar did not rise to fight me. He only lowered his cup.
Kill Ysgrim Hearth-Jarl
Take the cold hearthstone from the fire-pit
Drop it in the deepest water in the harbor.
Aye. Let it burn blue at the bottom of the sea, where no fool can sit down by it. Ulfvar would want that.
Keep it, but never light a hall with it.
A warning on the mantel, then. The clan will tell the story every Midwinter. Ulfvar earned that much.
And you brought the stone. Of course you did; that's what I asked. Now tell me what to do with it.
Tell Brunhild what you found in Atmora
I found Ulfvar. He's been sitting at that stone's fire for eighty years.
Your great-grandfather sailed north?
Ulfvar Keelbreaker still sits at his table in Atmora, but the fire that held him has gone out. Brunhild carved his name on her new ship's prow.

Ulfvar Keelbreaker. He took a longship to Atmora eighty years ago, to fetch the hearthstone of our clan's first longhouse and light it again in Windhelm. He never came back. I've built the ship he'd have wanted. I'm too old to sail it. You aren't.
Keelbreaker's Oath
The Cold Hearth
story.skycraft.q.side_atm_the_hoar_kings: Skjold Whale-Eye of Dawnstar saw frost giants building a great cairn of ice on the Atmoran coast, and the pack ice has been creeping south ever since.
Land on the Atmoran shore where Skjold saw the giants
Fight past the giants guarding the approach
The giants meant to freeze the Sea of Ghosts solid and walk across it into Skyrim. Their Hoar-King was laying the last blocks himself.
Hide near the Moot-Cairn and watch the giants gather
Inside the cairn lay an Atmoran war-axe frozen in clear ice, its edge still white with frost. It had been feeding the cairn's cold for longer than the giants could remember.
Dig the heart out of the Moot-Cairn
The pack ice went out of the bay this morning, all at once, like a door opening. Keep the axe. A thing like that belongs in a hand that knows what it cost.
Bring Skjold the heart of the cairn
The cairn is broken. This was inside it.
What did you see on the ice?
The Moot-Cairn of Atmora is a heap of slush now, and the whales are back off Dawnstar. I carry the axe that froze a sea.

Frost giants. A dozen of them, on the Atmoran shore, piling ice blocks into a cairn as tall as the Jarl's longhouse. Every week it's taller, and every week the pack ice comes a little further south. The whales are fleeing. I think the sea is fleeing. Go and look, and if it's what I think, knock it down.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_chains_in_the_r: Hatch-Mother Esh-Teeka told me nine nameless hatchlings vanished from the Warm-Mud Hatchery outside Stormhold. A shuttered boat was seen in the channel.
Search the Warm-Mud Hatchery for signs of the boat
The men who came back for a second boatload wore old Legion tunics with the badges cut off. One of them carried a contract with a Stormhold seal.
Imperial Contract Guard
Kill the slavers who came back for more
Follow the boat west to the Reedwall Stockade
Stockade Guard
Hired Netter
Break the stockade's guard
Crane meant to sell the hatchlings to plantations along the Niben as 'indentured orphans'. His papers were in perfect order. That was the most frightening thing about them.
Kill Overseer Septimus Crane
Lead Little Wiz-Tul and the hatchlings home to the hatchery
You will stand in front of the hatchery and tell every mother what you did.
Every mother. Yes. I will learn the names of the nine, too. All of them.
Burn the papers and say nothing. Crane is dead.
That is kind, and it is wrong, and I will take it. I will never seal another page without reading it. Never.

They carry the seal for orphans. Crane brought me a list of orphans and coin for the filing fee, and I filed. I did not look at the pools. I looked at the column. Gods of every land, I looked at the column.
Ask Junal-Lei about the seal on the papers
These indentures carry your ledger-seal, Junal-Lei.
I will hang them over the warm-mud so the hatchlings learn what ink can do. You walk like a Shadowscale, warm-blood. Take this. It was left with us by one, long ago, for a day like today.
Give the indenture papers to Esh-Teeka
The nine are home. These are the papers that sold them.
Why are the hatchery pools guarded?
Nine hatchlings came home to the Warm-Mud Hatchery. The Imperial overseer who bought them is dead, and the ledger that made it lawful has been read aloud.

Because nine are missing. Not eggs; hatchlings, small ones, with no names yet. A boat came up the channel at night with a lamp shuttered. The Lukiul clerks say the children wandered. Hatchlings do not wander nine at a time.
Chains in the Reeds
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_mother_of_flood: Many-Notches, a tail-hunter of Stormhold, wants help killing a giant wamasu that ate two of his hunters at the Low-Water Mere in Shadowfen.
Meet the tail-hunters at their stilt-camp in Shadowfen
Drive the hackwings off the hunters' smoking-racks
Storm-Gut died spitting lightning. Then the whole mere bulged upward. The wamasu had not been eating the hunters. It had been running from something bigger.
Wait for the leviathan to surface after dark

A leviathan. In the Mere. I have hunted those waters thirty years and called them shallow. ...I will not cut a notch for this one. I will cut a new tail. Here; you have earned the hunter's share and more.
Bring the leviathan's tooth to Many-Notches in Stormhold
The wamasu was the small one.
Is there room on your tail for one more notch?
The wamasu Many-Notches hired me to kill was fleeing a swamp leviathan, the Mother-of-Floods. Both are dead, and the Low-Water Mere is merely deep again.

One more, yes. A wamasu up in Shadowfen, as long as three boats and fat with lightning. It took two of my hunters at the Low-Water Mere. I want its belly-stone. You want a story to tell. We meet at the stilt-camp.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_salt_for_the_ro: Near Helstrom I found a dead Dunmer courier carrying orders for a garrison at a fort called Ebonroot, in the northern fens of Shadowfen.
A Dunmer courier's bones in a ruined chitin cuirass. His satchel is still sealed: an order to 'hold Ebonroot until the rains', and a crude map to an old fort in the northern fens.
Find Fort Ebonroot in northern Shadowfen
The orders were to salt the roots of the Helstrom Hist before the rains. Captain Sadri came for me before I could finish reading them.
Hurry to the Okeeh-Hist Grove before the rains
Stop the salters at the Hist's roots

Salt. Not fire, not axes. Salt, so that nothing would grow for a hundred years. Some old wars do not know how to die. Thank you, warm-blood. Twice now the Okeeh has you to thank, or once, if you came here first.
A Dunmer garrison meant to salt the Okeeh roots.
A forgotten Dunmer garrison at Fort Ebonroot planned to salt the roots of Helstrom's Hist. Their captain is dead and the salt is in the river.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_small_dreams.de: Near Vaermina's shrine in Shadowfen I found an altar holding a hatchling's doll and a note boasting of dreamers kept in a hollow to the east.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_small_dreams.fi: A black altar crusted with poppy-wax. Tucked under the candles is a hatchling's moss-doll, and a note in a clawed hand: 'Every one of them sleeps in my hollow now. East. Bring more.'
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_small_dreams.o0: Find the hollow east of Vaermina's shrine
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_small_dreams.o1: Kill the sleepwalkers guarding the circle
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_small_dreams.o2: Drinks-Sleep had been reaching into the dreams of Stormhold's hatchlings through this censer, using their small minds as doors for Vaermina. The sleepers in the circle woke when he died, crying for water.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_small_dreams.o3: A smiling man in a hollow. All of them, for a month. We thought it was the Hist teaching them fear. It was not the Hist. ...Last night, for the first time, they slept without crying.
Have the hatchlings been dreaming of a stranger?
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_small_dreams.o4: In the warm-mud, where only the newest hatch. Let it learn what it is to be small and not dream at all.
Give the censer to Esh-Teeka to be drowned
This was his door. Sink it somewhere deep.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_small_dreams.ou: A Vaermina cultist called Drinks-Sleep was using the dreams of Stormhold's hatchlings as doors. His censer is under the warm-mud and the children sleep quietly.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_teeth_on_the_ti: Wanes-in-Shallows of Murkmire says Naga raiders have been striking the fishing stilts every new moon. She thinks someone is paying them.
Naga Raider
Beat back the Naga raid on the Murkmire stilts
Follow the raiders' boats to their tide camp near Lilmoth
Naga Jawbreaker
Clear the Naga tide camp
Kill Kallax Jaw-Wide
Kallax slept on a purse of new Imperial coin stamped with the Lilmoth harbor-tax mark. Whoever pays the Naga collects the harbor tax.
Search Kallax's bedroll
You will repay every family in Murkmire. Twice over.
Twice. Yes. The harbor will wait another lifetime. Go before I change my mind about being sorry.
The King will hear of this.
The King hears many things. But he will hear this one from you, so I suppose it will stick.

Then the raidmaster was a thief as well as a cutthroat. ...No. You have the look of someone who already knows. Empty stilts sell cheap. I meant to buy the whole shore and build a proper harbor where Murkmire stands. It would have been good for everyone. Later.
Confront the Harbor-Warden of Lilmoth
Your tax-silver was in a Naga raidmaster's bed, Jee-Tazei.
A harbor-warden. Of course. The Naga only bite; it takes a city to chew. We will buy new nets with his silver. It is the only sweet thing about it.
Bring the harbor silver back to Wanes-in-Shallows
The raids are over. This is what paid for them.
Where have the fishers gone?
The Naga raids on Murkmire were bought and paid for by Lilmoth's own harbor-warden, who wanted the shore empty. Kallax Jaw-Wide will not paint his jaws again.

Naga. They come up from the south in long boats with their jaws painted red, and they take nets, smoked fish, sometimes the fishers too. They used to raid once a generation. Now it is every new moon. Somebody is feeding them, and it is not the river.
Red-Jaw Cleaver
Teeth on the Tide
Okan-Zeeus, Hist-tender of Helstrom, asked me to find out why the Okeeh Hist is sickening. The town blames a curse; he does not.
Visit the Okeeh-Hist Grove
Someone had been tapping the Hist in the dark, a little from each root so nobody would notice. Not a curse. A harvest.
Sap-Drunk Mudcrab
Pull the tap-spike from the Hist's root
Follow the drag-marks to the river landing
Sap-Runner
Drive off the sap-runners' crew
Vend was loading casks of Hist sap for Bravil, where alchemists pay in gold for one drop. His ledger names a local supplier only by a copper earring.
Kill Gallus Vend, master of the sap-runners
Okan-Zeeus will decide what happens to you.
Then I will go to him with my head down. He is my hatch-brother, you know. That is the worst of it.
Pay back the Hist. Tend its roots every dry season until it forgives you.
Every dry season? That is a long sentence for a short-lived merchant. ...Yes. I will carry the water. Thank you.
So. The tree has a long memory and you have a short road. I wanted a warehouse, a ship, a life that is not mud. The Hist was dying anyway, I told myself. It was not. I made it so.
Find the trader with the copper earring in Helstrom
You wear a copper earring, Seeks-Tomorrow. So does the name in Gallus Vend's ledger.

Seeks-Tomorrow. I knew before you said it; I smelled the sap on her hands at the last naming-day and told myself it was a gift. The Hist will mend. Take what grew in the bark while it slept. It wanted you to have it.
Bring the ledger to Okan-Zeeus
There was no curse. Only hands, and a ledger.
You look tired, tender. Is it the Hist?
The Okeeh Hist was not cursed but bled for Cyrodilic coin, and the hand on the spike belonged to its own tender's hatch-sister. The grove is singing again.

The Okeeh Hist is sick. Its leaves curl, its sap runs bitter, and the hatchlings of Helstrom wake from its dreams crying. The young ones say a Sload has cursed it. I say a curse does not leave footprints. Go and look at it with warm-blood eyes.
The Bitter Sap
Heem-Ra Tullus, a Lukiul healer in Lilmoth, believes the grey cough sweeping the lower city comes from the water. The traditional Tree-Speaker blames the city's neglect of the Hist.
Heem-Ra is clever and loud, which is a dangerous mix. The Hist showed me a dream: a soft grey mouth drinking from the city's cisterns. Water, yes. But not the kind you boil.
Hear Tree-Speaker Asheel's side
Heem-Ra says the cough comes from the water.
Go to the Saltmouth Cisterns north of Lilmoth
Coughing Drowned
Grey Ooze
Destroy the things nesting in the cisterns
The cisterns were full of drowned dead dumped in from a barge, and a smear of grey slime on every stone. Both healers were half right.
Fill a flask from the poisoned cistern

Corpses dumped where the city drinks. That is not sickness, that is a sermon. Someone wants Lilmoth weak and frightened. Asheel's dream said a grey mouth; tell her she was right, and tell her I said so. It will choke me less than this cough.
Bring the cistern water to Heem-Ra
The cisterns are full of corpses and grey slime.
She said that? Aloud? ...Then the Hist and the kettle agree for once. The barge that fed the cisterns is moored east of the city. The fishers call it the Coral Promise and will not go near it.
Tell Asheel what the cisterns held
Heem-Ra says you were right. The grey mouth is real.
Who is coughing in Lilmoth?
The grey cough came from corpses tipped into the Saltmouth Cisterns. Lilmoth's healer and its Tree-Speaker agreed on something, which the city may remember longer than the plague.

Half the lower city. Grey phlegm, grey scales, then a fever that boils the eyes. Tree-Speaker Asheel says the Hist is punishing Lukiul like me for drinking boiled water. I say something is in the water. Help me prove one of us right before we both run out of patients.
Healer's Hood of Lilmoth
The Grey Cough
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_the_ninth_at_mi: Outside Gideon I found a Legion grave scratched with a plea from the Ninth Legion's Second Cohort, who never left Mirefast Penitentiary.
A Legion grave marker sunk to its shoulders in the mud. Scratched beneath the name, fresher than the rest: 'Ninth, Second Cohort. Still at Mirefast. Still waiting to be relieved.'
Find Mirefast Penitentiary in the western marsh
Legionary of the Ninth
Drowned Optio
Lay the restless garrison of Mirefast to rest
The Prefect said Argonians drowned his men. The scratch-marks in the lower cells tell it the other way round: he opened the sluices on his own prisoners and drowned them in their cells.
Search the flooded lower cells
Loyal Legionary
Destroy the ghost of Prefect Aulus Fennic
Take the bent eagle of the Ninth
He drowned his prisoners and lied about it for two hundred years.
...Then the candle was for the wrong dead. I will put out his, and light theirs. Someone in this family should have asked sooner.
He died at his post. His men waited for him to the end.
That is what we always believed. Thank you. I will keep the candle burning for the Ninth.
Prefect Aulus Fennic. We are taught he held Mirefast against the rebellion and died with his cohort. Is that what you found?
Find the Prefect's descendant in Gideon
I found your ancestor at Mirefast.
Bent wings. Someone did that on purpose. I think I understand why, now. Take this, from the family chest. It belonged to an honest soldier of the Ninth, which turns out to be rarer than we were told.
Give Flavia the eagle of the Ninth
This was theirs. The men who waited.
The ghosts of the Ninth Legion's Second Cohort are at rest. Their Prefect drowned his prisoners at Mirefast and lied about it in death as he had in life.
Shield of the Second Cohort
The Ninth at Mirefast
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_the_stone_egg.d: Egg-Speaker Hixil of the Tsleeksh tribe asked me to break a curse that has stolen one clutch of eggs every spring for nine generations.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_the_stone_egg.o: Keep watch over the hatching-sands by night
Pale lights came to the sands at midnight and drifted north with something cradled between them. I followed.
Drive off the wisps drifting over the sand
Follow the lights to the Mourning Pool

...The stone egg. It sits in our naming-hut. My grandmothers called it a gift from the Xhuul, a tribe that died out. Died out, they said. I have never asked how. I am asking now, and I do not like the answer.
The ghost at the pool says the Tsleeksh stole her clutch-stone.
The Mourner would not hear me until she was spent. When the light went out of her, she was only a tired mother looking at a stone.
Face the Hatch-Mourner at the pool
Sink the stone egg into the Mourning Pool and keep vigil

Nine generations of empty nests for one stolen stone. The Hist teaches that everything returns to the roots eventually. It did not say how long the roots would wait. Thank you, warm-blood. The Tsleeksh owe you a name. We will think of a good one.
Tell Egg-Speaker Hixil it is done
The Xhuul stone is home. The Mourner is quiet.
The Tsleeksh curse was a mother's ghost whose clutch-stone they had stolen long ago. The stone is back in the Mourning Pool and the hatching-sands are quiet.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_the_stone_egg.p: We say a curse. Every spring one clutch is empty by morning, no tracks, no broken shells. The Tsleeksh have lived with it for nine generations. My hatchlings are now the age when we start to lay. I would like them to live without it.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_the_ukalith_cal: Livia Corvane, an Imperial antiquarian who stayed in Stormhold after the Legion left, wants me to follow a line of leaning glyph-stones to a buried Xanmeer in northern Shadowfen.
Find the leaning glyph-stones in Shadowfen
Stone-Nesting Chaurus
Take a rubbing of the last stone
Find the buried Xanmeer the stones point toward
Root-Warden
Embalmed Priest
Destroy the root-wardens in the stepped halls
Calendar Acolyte
Defeat Ixtaxh the Sap-Embalmed
The guardian said the stone was his chain, not his treasure. It ticks when I hold it, like a heart that keeps the seasons.
Lift the calendar stone from its socket

It keeps the marsh's time, which is not yours. Our oldest priests turned stones like this to tell the Hist when to wake. It does not belong in a glass case in the Imperial City. But you carried it. You choose.
Ask Elder Hulum-Ei what the stone is
This stone came out of a Xanmeer in Shadowfen. It keeps time.
Then it is decided, and it is done. Whatever happens to the seasons now, at least someone will be watching them.
Give the calendar stone to Livia or to Elder Hulum-Ei
Here is the calendar stone of Ukalith.
What are those charcoal rubbings?
I woke the warden of Xanmeer Ukalith and carried away the calendar stone he was bound to keep. Whoever holds it now holds the count of the marsh's seasons.

Glyph-stones from the far north of Shadowfen. They lean toward one mound, all of them, like signposts. My books say a Xanmeer lies under it, buried in mud for longer than the Empire has had a name. I cannot dig it myself. My knees are Imperial and so is my courage.
The Ukalith Calendar
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_the_voice_of_th: The barge that poisoned Lilmoth's cisterns is moored east of the city. The fishers say a Sload speaks from its hold.

The roots here felt it pass. Cold, like a drowned thing. Murkmire's dead went missing from the mud-graves last season, and their wraps were found floating near Lilmoth. Thras is far away. Its servants are not.
Ask Reezal-Jul in Murkmire about the Coral Promise
What do you know of a barge called the Coral Promise?
Board the Hulk of the Coral Promise
Cut through the barge's acolytes and their dead
Kill Orvas Ilmeth, the Voice of Thras
The Sload in the hold was a speaking-tube and a wet bladder. Orvas Ilmeth needed a master more frightening than himself to keep his acolytes obedient. His plague, at least, was real.
Take the coral idol from the hold
Ha. A false god with a real plague. That is the Sload way, even without the Sload. I will sink this idol in the deep mud where the roots can grind it. Murkmire's dead will come home to the graves.
There was no Sload. Only a Dunmer and a speaking-tube.
The Voice of Thras was a Dunmer necromancer pretending to speak for a Sload. He is dead, the barge is empty, and Murkmire's stolen dead have been put back in the mud.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.desc: Decimus Tsleel, a Lukiul trader of Gideon, wants his late father's bones found. His traditional aunt laid them at the Sedge-Root Hist; now they are gone, and each blames the other.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.o0.re: Then he has learned to lie as well as he has learned to wear shoes. ...No. You believe him. Go to the Sedge-Root and look for yourself. The Hist does not lie, even when nephews do.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.o0.to: Decimus says he did not take his father's bones.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.o1.te: Visit the Sedge-Root Hist outside Gideon
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.o2.jo: Neither of them took the bones. A troll had been digging up the burial-mound for marrow. I nearly laughed, and then I saw what it had been chewing.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.o2.te: Kill the troll gnawing on the burial-mound
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.o4.c0: Give them back to the Hist, the old way.
The old way. He would have laughed at the tomb anyway; he hated marble. Take them to my aunt. Tell her I said yes before she can ask.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.o4.c1: Bury them in the tomb, with his trade-name in marble.
Then he will have both names, one in stone and one in her stories. Take them to Aunt Xil first. She should be the one to carry them in.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.o4.re: A troll. All that shouting, and a troll. You decide. I cannot, and if Aunt Xil decides, I will hear about it for the rest of my life.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.o4.te: Return to Decimus with the bones
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.o4.to: A troll took them, not your aunt. Where should they rest?
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.o5.re: His apology. Hm. Two words from a Lukiul, and both of them mine. ...Thank you, warm-blood. The family will argue about something else now. That is how you know it is healed.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.o5.te: Bring the bones to Old Xil-Mareeh
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.o5.to: Your nephew sends these, and his apology.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.offer: You look like a man between two funerals.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.outro: Decimus Tsleel's father's bones were stolen by a troll, not by family. The Lukiul trader and his traditional aunt chose a resting place together.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.pitch: Exactly between them. My father died last month. I paid for an Imperial tomb, a good one, with his name in marble. My aunt says his bones belong to the Sedge-Root Hist, the old way, to be drunk back into the tree. Now his bones are missing from the Hist altogether, and she says I stole them. I did not. Find them, please, before this family eats itself.
story.skycraft.q.side_bm_two_names.title: Two Names for One Father
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_blood_on_the_v: Aldo Castellus, a Skingrad vintner, says the Merovane family poisoned his vines. He wants proof.
Vine-Rat
Dig up a blighted root in the Castellus rows

Then why are mine rotting too? Same pale threads, same smell. I assumed Aldo did it to me first. Look at the old stump grove near Talwinque if you want something strange. Nothing grows right in those hills, and nobody will say why.
Question Ysmene Merovane
Aldo Castellus says you poisoned his vines.
Visit the stump grove at Talwinque by night
Thorn-Child
Fight off the grove's thorn-children
When the Vine-Wife fell, a warm green seed rolled out of the bark at her heart. It was still beating.
Defeat the Vine-Wife
I planted the heartseed where the grove used to stand. By the time I stood up, a green shoot had already broken the soil.
Plant the heartseed among the old stumps
Tell Ysmene. End the feud.
She'll laugh at me. Then maybe she'll pour me a cup of that sweet tawny I pretend to hate. Fine. Fine! I'll go now, before I lose my nerve.
Keep it quiet. Just pay me.
Easier, yes. Coward's choice, but easier. Here, take this, and a case of the forty-year. Don't drink it all on the road.
...Ennio Merovane and I. We were partners then, before the quarrel. Two boys with one axe. Gods. We have been blaming each other for our own sin.
Tell Aldo Castellus who really blighted the vines
You and old Merovane cut down a spriggan's grove together, thirty years ago.
What's wrong with your vines?
The blight in the West Weald came from a grove two young vintners cut down together. The Vine-Wife is gone, a new grove is growing, and Skingrad's feud is now in the hands of two stubborn families.

Rot. White rot, like hair, all through the roots. Started the week the Merovane woman bought her new press. Coincidence? I'm sixty-one, friend, I stopped believing in coincidence before you were born. Go and look at my rows. Then go and look at her face.
Vintner's Reckoning
Blood on the Vine
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_forty_drakes.d: Feldsa Sadrathi, a Dunmer of Cheydinhal, asked me to recover the stolen ash-urn of her family's ancestor, Grandmother Ilmyna.
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_forty_drakes.o: At the tavern! All night. Mostly. Look, nobody liked Grandmother, all right? Even when she was alive she corrected my posture. Now she does it from a jar. Check Fort Scinia, if you must.
Ask Feldsa's son Ervyn about the night of the theft
Where were you the night the shrine was robbed?
Go to Fort Scinia, east of Cheydinhal
Scinia Bone-Guard
Bought Bones
Get past the bone-buyer's guards
Stop Calvia Rennus, the Ash-Reader
The ghost of Grandmother Ilmyna says her own grandson sold her urn for forty drakes. She seems more offended by the price than by the theft.
Recover the Sadrathi ash-urn
Tell your mother yourself, or I will.
Fine. Fine! But when Grandmother starts on about it, I'm sending her to haunt you.
Your secret's safe. Your grandmother is punishment enough.
That's... true, actually. Thank you. Here, it's what's left of the forty drakes. Well, of the ten I didn't drink.
She TOLD you? Of course she did. She never stops. Please, don't tell Mother. I'll light her candles every day. I'll even sit up straight.
Confront Ervyn Sadrathi
Your grandmother says you sold her for forty drakes.
Thank the Three and every saint. The house feels like a house again. ...She is already complaining about the dust on the shrine, isn't she? Yes. She is home.
Return the urn to Feldsa Sadrathi
Grandmother Ilmyna is home.
Your shrine was robbed?
Grandmother Ilmyna Sadrathi is back on her family's shrine in Cheydinhal, telling everyone exactly what she thinks of them. Her grandson now sits up very straight.
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_forty_drakes.p: My mother-in-law's ashes, sera. We carried her urn all the way from Morrowind when we settled here. Two nights ago someone broke the shrine and took her. The guard says bandits. The neighbors say a woman in black has been buying old bones at Fort Scinia, east of the city. Please. She was difficult, but she was ours.
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_green_and_gold: Lady Cassia Vallarius of Chorrol says every heir of her family dies at thirty. She sent me to the family crypt for her grandfather's household book.
Find the Vallarius crypt in the western hills
A page was cut from the household book. On the next page, in the same hand: 'Livia is not to be spoken of. Payments to the witch at Rayles to continue.'
Vallarius Retainer
Recover the household book from Aurelian Vallarius' tomb
Follow the payments to Fort Rayles
Rayles Feather-Servant
Clear the hagraven's servants from Fort Rayles
Livia Vallarius died cursing a family that had paid her to stay away for two hundred years. Her feather still had the family ribbon tied to it.
Confront Mother Livia
A great-great-aunt nobody remembers, struck from the book and paid to rot in a ruin. And every heir since kept paying, and kept forgetting why.
Tell Lady Cassia what was cut out of her family
The curse had a name. Livia Vallarius.
Write her back in. Names were the curse.
Then she goes back on the page, between her brother and her sister, where she should have been. I feel better already. That may only be pride.
Leave it cut. Some debts are better buried.
You may be right. The Vallarius name has enough stains. I'll burn the feather and say nothing. My grandfather would approve, and that worries me.
I could leave the page cut. Or I could write her back in, and let all of Chorrol read what we did.
Help Cassia decide what the family book will say
What will you write in the book?
You look unwell, my lady.
The hagraven of Fort Rayles is dead and Lady Cassia Vallarius may live past thirty. What the family book says about Livia is now Cassia's to answer for.

Every heir of House Vallarius falls ill in their thirtieth year and is dead by the thirty-first. I turn thirty next month. My grandfather's household book was buried with him in our crypt in the hills west of here. If there is a reason for this, it is written there. Fetch it, and I will pay whatever you ask.
Vallarius Courtesy
Green and Gold
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_lantern_on_the: Tullo Brash, a Bravil moneylender, asked me to follow the green lantern on the Larsius that has led five people, including his brother Pellio, away into the night.
Watch the Larsius from the Bravil docks after dark
Follow the green lantern north to Fort Black Boot

My brother hopes I drowned, before I tell anyone what he does. Every one of those 'lost' souls owed Tullo money they could never pay. I row them out of Bravil before his collectors break their hands. And he's sent the collectors after you, friend. They followed you here.
Speak with the lantern-bearer
Pellio? Your brother thinks you drowned.
Brash Collector
Drive off Tullo's collectors
Grusk had a list in his pocket: Pellio's name, the five 'drowned' debtors, and mine, with a sum beside it. Tullo had never meant for me to come back either.
Kill Grusk gro-Dular, the Collector
Pellio drowned. So did Grusk.
Drowned. Both. What a terrible river. Here's your fee. Don't spend it all in one skooma den.
He's alive, and I know what you are. Your debtors are free.
You... Keep your voice down! Fine. Fine. The debts are torn up, see? Torn up. Now leave Tullo in peace before the guard hears.
Found him? Well? Is he alive? And did you, ah, happen to see Grusk on your way?
Return to Tullo Brash in Bravil
I found your brother.
You look like you've lost something.
The lantern on the Larsius was no drowned spirit, just a brother ferrying debtors out of Bravil ahead of a moneylender's thugs. Pellio still rows at night, and Tullo has stopped asking about him.

My brother Pellio. Went out after a green lantern on the river two weeks back and never came home. Five people have done the same this season. The priests say a drowned spirit lures them. I say find my brother, dead or alive, and Tullo will forgive your next three debts. Generous, yes?
Debt-Cutter
The Lantern on the Larsius
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_mother_mudmout: Seeks-the-Shallows, an Argonian ferrywoman in Leyawiin, asked me to find her son Little-Reed, who vanished in the stilt-village of Drowned Rest.
Travel to Drowned Rest
At midnight the villagers carried a bound stranger down to the water, singing all the way. They were not friendly anymore when they saw me.
Watch Drowned Rest after dark
Rest-Singer
Fight the singers of Drowned Rest
Follow the drag-marks to Mudmouth Pool
Mother Mudmouth went under for the last time. Little-Reed was tied to a cypress root above the pool, alive, and very angry. I sent him home.
Kill Mother Mudmouth before she feeds again
You should tell the Leyawiin guard everything.
Then I will. The water will be cleaner, and my boat will be emptier. Fair trade.
It's over. Keep your secret.
Kind. Or cruel. Hard to tell in the swamp. Take this. It was my mother's, and I do not deserve it today.
I know. I have known for six years. They let my boat pass because I paid them in eels and silence. This time they took the wrong child. Mine. You may think less of me. I do too.
Return to Seeks-the-Shallows in Leyawiin
Little-Reed is home. The village was feeding travelers to the thing in the pool.
You look like you're waiting for someone.
Mother Mudmouth is dead, the singers of Drowned Rest are scattered, and Little-Reed is home in Leyawiin. His mother's silence cost more travelers than I like to think about.

My hatchling, Little-Reed. He went upriver to Drowned Rest to sell eels and did not come back. The people there smile too much. Do you know what a smile is in the swamp? It is a mouth that has not decided yet.
Mudmouth's Tooth
Mother Mudmouth
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_roll_of_istiru: Outside Fort Istirus I found a headstone for twenty legionaries, recut by someone in Kvatch who swears they did not desert.
A plain headstone, far newer than the fort. Twenty names are cut into it, each scratched out and recut more deeply. At the bottom: 'They did not run. - S.M., Kvatch.'
Return to Fort Istirus after dark
Hanged Legionary
Put down the hanged legionaries who still answer the roll
Search the prefect's quarters for the last duty roll
The prefect's shade fought hardest for the roll. It was his own handwriting that damned him: the night the fort was abandoned, the only man absent was the prefect.
Face the shade of Prefect Vibius Aurex

Septima Merula. My great-grandfather was the eleventh name. Let me read it. ...He ran. The prefect ran, and wrote them up as deserters to cover it. My family has been right for eighty years, and nobody listened.
Bring the roll to S.M. in Kvatch
You recut the stone at Fort Istirus. This is the last roll of the watch.
Nail it to the chapel door.
Then the whole Gold Coast will know their names were clean. The Aurexes will hate us both. Good.
Bury it with them. They wanted rest, not revenge.
Maybe you're right. I'll take it to the fort myself and read the names one last time. Properly, this time.
The Aurex family still sits on the Kvatch council. I could nail this to the chapel door. Or I could bury it with the men, and let them rest without a scandal. Which would you do?
Decide with Septima what to do with the truth
What will you do with it?
The twenty hanged men of Fort Istirus no longer answer the roll. Septima Merula has the truth now, and the Aurex name will carry what it deserves, one way or another.
Twentieth Watch
The Roll of Istirus
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_salt_and_starl: Inspector Marcellin Hesk of the Anvil customs house asked me to break a crew smuggling welkynd stones out of Hrota Cave.
Go to Hrota Cave after dark
Brine-Hand Lookout
Fight past the smugglers' lookouts
Then let's sink the Saltworks crew together.
Now you're thinking like a Hesk. Corvo Lask holds the Old Saltworks to the north. Bring me his ledger and we'll see whose name is in it.
I don't care. You're coming back to Anvil.
Then you'll have to drag me, and my people will have something to say about that. Go deal with Lask first. If you live, we'll talk.
Sabine. I run stones, yes. So does the Saltworks crew, twice as many, and their crates go out stamped by the customs house. Father isn't stopping smugglers. He's stopping competition.
Hear out the smugglers' leader
You're Hesk's daughter.
Saltworks Cutthroat
Brine-Hand Smuggler
Survive the ambush on the coast road
Saltworks Hand
Kill Corvo Lask, the Salt King
Lask's ledger lists a payment to the Anvil customs house for every crate. The initials beside each one are M.H.
Take Lask's ledger
...She told you. Of course she did. Fine. Burn the book and keep my pay, and I'll retire quietly to a farm near Kvatch. Or take it to the Count and watch both Hesks hang. Your hand, your choice.
Confront Inspector Hesk with the ledger
Lask paid you for every crate. And the other crew is your daughter's.
Any trouble at the harbor?
I broke the Saltworks crew and learned that the Anvil customs house had been taking its cut. Father and daughter Hesk have both been squinting at me ever since.

Welkynd stones are leaving the Gold Coast by the crate, dug out of Ayleid ruins and sold to Summerset buyers. The crew doing it uses Hrota Cave, north of the city, at night. Clear them out and bring me their leader's books. The Empire pays well for its own history.
Customs Seal
Salt and Starlight
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_the_bone_merch: Pia Lucanus, apprentice to the Imperial City undertaker Orrin Valcis, asked me to find her master, who went into the catacombs under the city nine days ago.
Find the old sewer outfall beside Lake Rumare
Sewer Skeever
Clear the skeevers from the outfall tunnel
Unclaimed Dead
Search the old catacombs under the city
Orrin Valcis had not been lost. He had been working. Half the paupers he buried for the city were sold to necromancers instead, and he kept the best ones for himself.
Sold Dead
Stop Orrin Valcis in the deepest ossuary
And? Your face says it before you do. Give me the book. I can read it myself.
Return to Pia Lucanus
I found your master.
Take it to the watch.
Then the Imperial City learns its undertaker was a ghoul, and I learn to be something else. Thank you. I mean it.
Bury them properly. Quietly.
Then I have a great deal of digging to do. Come by the shop when you want something done right. It will be done right now.
Every name in here was someone's grandmother. I could take this to the watch and close the shop forever. Or I could quietly dig them all up, one by one, and bury them properly myself.
Help Pia decide what happens to the shop
What will you do now?
Where is your master?
Orrin Valcis, the Imperial City's undertaker, had been selling the dead he was paid to bury. He will not sell any more, and his apprentice is putting things right.

Master Valcis went down through the old outfall beside the lake nine days ago. He said the catacombs under the city were flooding and some of our burials needed moving. He took a lantern and two shovels. He did not take his lunch, and he never forgets his lunch.
Undertaker's Mercy
The Bone-Merchant
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_the_frost_oath: Hrefna Cold-Harp, a skald in Bruma, wants the sword Rimeoath from the Nord barrow of Skeldhaugr for her song.
Find Skeldhaugr Barrow east of Bruma
Oath-Warden
Fight through the barrow's draugr
Defeat Hroald Frost-Oath
Take Rimeoath from Hroald's throne
The giant Ymmrok had been frozen under the Giant's Stair since before Bruma had walls. Hroald's oath was the ice. I broke it, and then I had to break him.
Stop Ymmrok before he reaches Bruma
Your song nearly buried Bruma. The sword goes back to the barrow.
Fine. Fine! Put it back with the old jarl. I'll write it as a tragedy. They sell better anyway.
Then sing it well. Here's your sword.
Oh, I will. You'll be the hero of the second verse, and I'll be modest in the third. Here, your fee, and a skald's thanks.
I... knew the verse. Every skald knows it. I thought it was a metaphor. All right, I hoped it wasn't. A saga needs a monster, and Bruma had run out. You must admit it ends well.
Return to Hrefna Cold-Harp in Bruma
The sword was holding a frost giant in the ice. Did you know?
A song about something that bites back?
Hroald Frost-Oath and the giant he kept in the ice are both finished, and Bruma has a new song. Hrefna insists the parts about her are entirely accurate.

Skeldhaugr. A Nord barrow east of Bruma, older than the city. Hroald Frost-Oath is buried there with a sword called Rimeoath, and the old skalds say he swore to hold something in the ice until the mountains fall. A sword like that deserves to hang in a mead-hall, not rot. Fetch it, and I will put your name in the second verse.
Second Verse
Giant's Stair Hood
The Frost-Oath
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_the_last_beare: On a Colovian hillside I found seven duelists' graves, each bearer of the same nameless sword. The latest, Sir Aemon Thrale, carried it east to the Ayleid ruin of Wendir.

Seven headstones in a row on a windy hillside, each for a famous duelist, each dated a few years after the last. The newest is blank except for a scratched line: 'Sir Aemon carried it east, to the white stones of Wendir. Gods help him.'
Find Sir Aemon Thrale at Wendir
Destroy the hollow shades that follow the sword
Sir Aemon thanked me as he fell. The black sword was in my hand before I remember picking it up.
Defeat Sir Aemon Thrale and take the black sword
I dug the eighth grave and left the headstone blank. The sword said nothing the whole time. I did not care for its silence.
Bury Sir Aemon beside the other six bearers
I ended the last bearer of a sword that wears out its owners, and now it is mine. Someday someone may find an eighth headstone on that hill. I mean to make them wait a long time.
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_the_ninth_turn: A courier from Captain Hlaren found me: the cult of the Thrice-Turned Knife gathers at Boethiah's shrine in the Jerall Mountains. Hlaren wants its High Blade dead.
Climb to Boethiah's shrine in the Jerall Mountains
Cut through the Turned Knives at the shrine
Sethra Vael told the truth before she died: Drevis Hlaren is one of them. Every blade I broke for him was a rival on his way to the top.
Kill Mother Sethra Vael, High Blade of the Turned Knife
I'm taking this to the Count of Cheydinhal.
Of course you are. The faithful betray, and betrayal is faith. I will be gone before the guards arrive. We will meet again, knife.
Keep your cult. Pay me and I forget your name.
A practical knife. The Prince approves of that too. Here. And should you ever need a door opened in Cheydinhal, knock twice, then once.
Then you understand the Prince better than most priests. I am High Blade now, thanks to you. Join me, and the next turn is yours. Or turn on me. Either way, Boethiah will be pleased.
Face Captain Drevis Hlaren in Cheydinhal
Sethra is dead. She told me whose knife I've been.

The Thrice-Turned Knife lost its High Blade on a frozen shrine, and Drevis Hlaren climbed into her place over the bodies I left him. At the shrine, Boethiah left a gift in the snow for the knife that turned on its own hand.
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_the_saints_wat: In the Great Forest I found a bull-skull totem with an old Alessian prayer carved on it, and hoofprints followed by a hunting party's boots.

A totem of three bull skulls bound to an oak post. Fresh letters in old Cyrodilic are cut beneath them: 'Son of the Bull, keep the Saint's sleep.' Hoofprints, large ones, lead into the trees. So do boot prints, many of them.
Follow the hoofprints into Bull's Hollow
Stand with Oxhorn against the baron's beaters
Baron Ardo wanted a minotaur head for his hall in Skingrad. He died certain he was the one doing the hunting.
Oxhorn told me the cairn belongs to a priestess of Alessia's time, and that his line has kept her grave for a hundred generations. He did not say what happens if she wakes. I did not ask.
Keep the night watch at the Saint's cairn with Oxhorn
Baron Ardo's hunt is over and the minotaur called Oxhorn still keeps his vigil in the Great Forest. He gave me a shield before I left, and said a watchman should not travel unguarded.
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_the_thrice_tur: Captain Drevis Hlaren of the Cheydinhal watch asked me to find who is killing the city's merchants with daggers turned three times in the wound.
The murder weapon was wrapped in grey silk. A Dunmer neighbor went pale when she saw it, and whispered one name: Boethiah.
Search the last victim's house by the river
Survive the knives sent to stop you
Follow the grey silk to Fort Naso
Break the cult cell in Fort Naso
Thalyn Orvas died smiling. His last words were: 'Well turned, stranger. Tell him he climbed well.'
Kill Thalyn Orvas, the Smiling Knife
The Ninth Turn, at the shrine in the Jerall. So there is a mother to this nest. Well done. Rest, outlander. I will send for you when I know more.
Bring the letter to Captain Hlaren
The cell is broken. This letter was on their altar.
I broke a Boethiah cult cell in Fort Naso and brought Captain Hlaren a letter pointing to a shrine in the Jerall Mountains. Thalyn Orvas' last words keep coming back to me.

A dagger. Turned three times in the wound, every time. Three merchants, three daggers, and not a coin stolen. That is not robbery, it is ritual. Find whoever is doing this, outlander, and I will owe you more than wages.
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_the_undimmed_l: Tullia Vesk, a scholar in the Imperial City, asked me to find a welkynd lamp in the forgotten Ayleid ruin of Narindel, a lamp her glyphs say has never gone out.
Find the ruin of Narindel
Narindel Lamp-Keeper
Destroy the lamp-keepers of Narindel
Take the Undimmed Lamp from its niche
The lich came apart like a snuffed wick. But the lamp in my pack was still burning, and it was warm against my back the whole way home.
Lamp-Keeper
Destroy Herdaril the Undimmed
Here. Study it, and be careful.
Careful. Yes. I will be very careful. Thank you, truly. I will remember who helped me, for a very long time.
No. I'm breaking it here, in front of you.
Don't... Oh. Oh, it's just glass now. You have no idea what you've thrown away. Get out. No, wait. Thank you. I think.
Of course it is. It is not a lamp, it is a vessel. Herdaril poured himself into it. With the right glyphs, anyone could. Give it to me. Please.
Bring the lamp to Tullia Vesk
The lamp kept a lich alive. It is still lit.
What are you copying?
I brought the Undimmed Lamp out of Narindel and decided what became of it. Tullia Vesk will not soon forget that choice, whichever way it went.

Lamp-glyphs from Narindel, an Ayleid ruin north of the Rumare that nobody bothers to rob anymore. The glyphs say the lamp in its lowest hall has never gone out, not once in four thousand years. I want to see it. I would very much like you to walk in front of me.
Wickcutter
The Undimmed Lamp
story.skycraft.q.side_cyr_wells_of_the_f: I found a carved stone in the Heartlands with a starved welkynd stone at its foot and directions to two Ayleid wells and a door.

A standing stone carved with five Ayleid star-marks, four of them chipped dark. Beneath, in fresh charcoal: 'Under stars only. Dusk, then Morrow, then the door.' A dull blue stone sits in a hollow at its foot.
The stone drank the starlight over the Well of Dusk and something down in the dark said thank you.
Hold the welkynd stone over the Well of Dusk at night
Find the Well of Morrow to the south
By the second hour the stone was too bright to look at. The well beside me had begun to hum.
Keep a vigil at the Well of Morrow while the stone brightens
Bring the brightened stone to the sealed door of Anyandil
Fight off the waking wardens of Anyandil
The voice in the wells had never been a ghost asking for help. It was a prisoner asking for a key, and I had carried it all the way to the door.
Break Ilvanor of the Fallen Star before it escapes
Ilvanor shattered into black glass on the floor of Anyandil. Among the shards was a sliver of welkynd that still held the light of the wells.
story.skycraft.q.side_els_grey_sugar.des: Ri'zhassa, a cane-grower of Torval, says the moon sugar in the small fields of western Pellitine has turned grey and maddening, while the large estates are untouched.
Visit the Ja'rassa Cane-Fields in Pellitine
Follow the irrigation ditch upstream to the old distillery
Vashir was tipping grey powder into the ditches that fed only the small fields. His satchel held mortgages on every one of them, all owned by a Senchal lender who signs with a drawing of a sweet-tooth.
Burn the mortgages. Let him try to collect on ash.
Ha! Ri'zhassa will light the fire herself. And when he comes, she will offer him a cup of grey sugar.
Keep them. They are proof against him.
Proof. Yes. Clever walker. Take them to Senchal. The wharf-warden there hates him almost as much as Ri'zhassa does.
Ri'zhassa signed one of those papers, in a bad year. Sweet-Tooth. Everyone in Pellitine knows the name and no one says it. He wanted the fields to fail, so he could take them for his cooks.
Tell Ri'zhassa who soured the cane
The sickness was a poisoner, paid by whoever holds your mortgages.
Ri'zhassa will bury it under the fattest stalk, so the moons can see what was done. Next season, the cane will be sweet again. This one promises you the first cut.
Give Ri'zhassa the tin of grey powder
Here is what poisoned your cane.
story.skycraft.q.side_els_grey_sugar.off: Why does a cane-grower look so worried?
story.skycraft.q.side_els_grey_sugar.out: The grey sugar of western Pellitine was poison tipped into the ditches by a hired alchemist. The lender behind him is a Senchal skooma lord called Sweet-Tooth.
story.skycraft.q.side_els_grey_sugar.pit: Because her cane has gone grey, walker. Grey sugar, and the ones who eat it see things and bite their friends. Every small field in western Pellitine is sick. The big fields are fine. Ri'zhassa does not believe in a sickness that knows which farmer is rich.
story.skycraft.q.side_els_luck_comes_due: Near Clavicus Vile's shrine I found the urn of Ma'jhad, a Torval merchant whose luck ran out after twenty years. A key in the ashes points to his ruined counting-house.
A burial urn left in the grass, its lid sealed with red wax. Painted on the side: 'Ma'jhad, merchant of Torval. Lucky for twenty years. Not for twenty-one.' Something rattles inside that is not ash.
Ma'jhad bought twenty years of luck from Clavicus Vile and signed for 'his blood' as surety. His daughter Ja'neema sells charms in Torval. She does not know she is the payment.
Take Ma'jhad's luck contract from the strongbox
Burn it. The Collector is gone; let the debt go with him.
Fire, yes. Ja'neema will feel lighter when it is ash. She hopes the Prince is not watching. She suspects he always is.
Keep it. A Daedric contract is a weapon if you know how to read it.
You are braver than Ja'neema, or more foolish. Take it far away from her, then. And take this, from her father's stock. It never worked for him.
Ja'neema always thought her father was simply clever. ...Clever and lucky, and a coward at the end. What do we do with it, walker? Ja'neema is afraid to touch it.
Your father signed you away for his luck. I have the contract.
Ma'jhad of Torval bought twenty years of luck from Clavicus Vile and pledged his daughter as payment. The Collector who came for her is banished.
story.skycraft.q.side_els_old_scar_mothe: Hanzira Spear-Mother of Riverhold asked me to help hunt Old Scar-Mother, a senche-tiger that suddenly turned man-eater after twenty peaceful years.
Search the Tall-Grass Gully for Scar-Mother's tracks
Someone had baited a pit with meat soaked in skooma. Poachers drug a big cat, then sell its pelt whole. Old Scar-Mother had eaten the bait and not died. She had only gone mad.
Drive the wolves away from the baited pit in the gully
Kill Grell Hookhand and his poachers
Track Old Scar-Mother to her den

Skooma in the meat. Hanzira should have guessed; the darts were in her shoulder all along. She will not sell this pelt. She will hang it over the Riverhold gate, with the darts still in it, so every poacher on the road can see what it cost.
Poachers fed her skooma-bait. She was mad, not wicked.
What has teeth this week, Spear-Mother?
Old Scar-Mother turned man-eater because poachers baited her with skooma-soaked meat. The poachers are dead, and so, mercifully, is she.

A senche-tiger. Old Scar-Mother, the herders call her. She has hunted the plains west of Riverhold for twenty years and never touched a Khajiit. This month she has killed four. Something has changed her. Hanzira wants to know what, before she puts a spear in her.
story.skycraft.q.side_els_sand_in_the_cr: Khali the Tally-Keeper of Rimmen hired me to guard Dro'zel's caravan to Riverhold. It has been robbed three times at Broken-Wheel Pass, and the trade-guild has paid each time.
Meet Dro'zel's caravan at the Dry Wells Waystation
Wait while the caravan loads up
The raiders fought badly and died easily. One of them, dying, laughed: 'He said the guard would be a fool.' The crates they were meant to steal were full of sand.
Fight off the raiders at the pass
Dro'zel hired the raiders himself, sold the guild empty crates, and planned to leave a dead guard behind as proof of the robbery. I declined.
Forty crates of sand. Three times paid. Khali knew the numbers were wrong; she did not know they were wrong in such a tidy way. The guild will be very grateful. Khali will make sure of it.
Bring the manifest back to Khali in Rimmen
Do you need a caravan guard?
Dro'zel Two-Ledgers staged his own caravan robberies to cheat the Rimmen trade-guild, and meant to leave me dead as his alibi. The guild has its ledger straight again.

Khali always needs a caravan guard. Dro'zel's caravan to Riverhold has been robbed three times this year at Broken-Wheel Pass, and three times the trade-guild has paid him for the loss. Khali would like it not to be robbed a fourth time. Meet the caravan at the Dry Wells Waystation.
story.skycraft.q.side_els_the_bride_of_w: At the edge of the Pellitine cane-fields I found an empty grave for the groom of Weeping Palms, an estate deep in the jungle.
A small headstone at the edge of the cane, half swallowed by jungle: 'Ri'darhan, groom of Weeping Palms. Kept too long. Let him go.' The grave is empty, and fresh.
Find the Weeping Palms Estate in the jungle
The bride was the vampire, not the victim. She fed on her groom for sixty years in the cellar and buried him only when he finally stopped being useful. The locket shows them both, young.
Destroy Lady Shazira of Weeping Palms
Ri'darhan. Inzirr's grandfather told stories of the wedding that never ended. They were not stories. Inzirr will find him a sand-grave in Torval, under the open moons, far from any cellar.
Bring word to Grave-Tender Inzirr in Torval
The groom of Weeping Palms needs a proper grave.
Good. He scratched it himself, Inzirr thinks, near the end. Let him keep the one face he still wanted to remember: his own, when he was young.
Give the locket to Inzirr to bury with the groom
Bury this with him. Her face is scratched out.
The bride of Weeping Palms was a vampire who kept her groom alive to feed on for sixty years. She is destroyed, and the groom has a grave in Torval under the open moons.
story.skycraft.q.side_els_the_crooked_la: Azirr the Star-Counter of Rimmen believes the Lunar Lattice is being bent near an old stone ring east of the city, confusing the furstock of newborn cubs.
Visit the Ring of Jode's Teeth
Destroy the atronachs set to guard the turned stones
At moonrise the light ran off the turned stones in a thin silver thread, south-east across the plain, to a tower of glass.
Watch which way the bent moonlight runs after dark
Follow the stolen moonlight to the glass tower
The Altmer magister was paid by a noble house to choose the furstock of their unborn heirs. She called it husbandry. The lens she built drank moonlight, and every cub nearby paid for it.

To choose a cub's shape before it is born. To choose. The moons never ask permission, and they never play favourites. That is the whole point of them. Azirr will grind this to dust and scatter it on the Ring. And this, from the old stores, is yours.
Bring the moonglass lens to Azirr
An Altmer was bending the moonlight through this lens.
What is wrong with the count, star-counter?
An Altmer magister was bending the Lunar Lattice through a moonglass lens to choose the furstock of a noble house's heirs. The stones of Jode's Teeth face the right sky again.

The moons are where they should be. The light is not. Three cubs were born in Rimmen this month, and the midwives cannot agree on what furstock any of them will grow into. That does not happen. Something is bending the Lattice near the Ring of Jode's Teeth. Come with Azirr's map and see.
story.skycraft.q.side_els_the_first_claw: Ma'dara the Song-Keeper of Riverhold wants the lost funeral-song of Ja'khizzar, the First Claw, recovered from his tomb in the northern sands of Anequina.
Find the Tomb of the First Claw
The guardian was Nahrisha, who truly held the pass while Ja'khizzar ran. The funeral-song on the tablet tells it plainly. Someone carved it, then buried it with the lie.
Take the funeral-song tablet from the sarcophagus
Sing the true song. Nahrisha has waited long enough.
Then tonight Riverhold hears a new old song, and every child learns a new name. Some will be angry. Good. Angry children remember.
Keep the old song. The clans need their hero.
That is what Nahrisha chose too. Ma'dara will keep the tablet in her chest, and sing the old song a little more quietly.
Ma'dara has sung his name at every wedding in Riverhold for forty years. ...Ah. And yet. A song is a thing you choose, walker. You chose to carry this out of the sand. What would you have her sing?
The First Claw ran. It was Nahrisha who held the pass.
Which of your songs is mostly untrue?
Ja'khizzar the First Claw was a coward, and the hero who held the dune pass was the guardian buried at his door. Ma'dara the Song-Keeper now knows both songs.

Clever. The song of Ja'khizzar, the First Claw, who held the dune pass alone against a thousand. Ma'dara learned it from her mother. But the tomb-scribes left a second song, a funeral-song, and no one has heard it for a thousand years. It is sealed in his tomb, in the north. Ma'dara is too old to rob tombs. You are not.
story.skycraft.q.side_els_the_honest_thi: Lord Ahzir of Rimmen hired me to recover his signet ring, stolen by an Alfiq trickster. He was very clear that I should not ask what the ring seals.
Follow the Alfiq's trail to the old granary north of Rimmen
Pazhi the Alfiq was waiting for me, not running. It left a tithe receipt sealed with Ahzir's lion, for a debt the farmer swears he never owed.
Granary Skeever
Clear the skeevers out of the granary
Follow the Alfiq to Lord Ahzir's summer villa
Velvet Knife
Survive Shazrah the Velvet Knife
The villa was a forger's workshop. Ahzir's signet made false sugar-tithes against half the farms around Rimmen. The Alfiq stole the stamp, and Ahzir sent a knife after whoever followed it.
Take the signet the Alfiq left on the forger's desk
Keep your gold. The magistrate will have the ring.
Then you are a fool with a ring. Go. Lord Ahzir has better lawyers than you have friends.
Say nothing. Let him sweat.
Silence. Lord Ahzir hates silence. ...Go away, walker.
Lord Ahzir does not know what you mean, and would pay a great deal to keep not knowing. Name a number. No? Then get out, and remember that Rimmen's magistrates dine at Lord Ahzir's table.
Confront Lord Ahzir in Rimmen
Your knife missed. Your villa is a forger's workshop.

Pazhi. Ha! That one has brought Shavi-ra evidence for years, through the window, at night, never once through the door. Lord Ahzir dines with magistrates, yes. Not with this one. Pazhi left something for you on Shavi-ra's desk. There is a paw-print on the wrapping.
Give the signet to Magistrate Shavi-ra
This is Lord Ahzir's signet. It sealed forged sugar-tithes. An Alfiq named Pazhi stole it.
You seem short one ring, my lord.
An Alfiq called Pazhi stole Lord Ahzir's signet to expose the forged sugar-tithes it sealed. The magistrate of Rimmen has its evidence, and I have the thief's thanks.

Lord Ahzir's signet was stolen from his own hand. By an Alfiq. A cat, walker, the size of a cat, who sat on his desk and smiled. It is humiliating. Find the beast, bring back the ring, and do not ask what the ring is for. Lord Ahzir pays well for people who do not ask.
The Honest Thief
story.skycraft.q.side_els_the_hungry_dar: Zaba-jo, Torval's lamplighter, says the lamps in the low streets are going dark on their own and people are vanishing, among them his own sister.
Walk the low streets of Torval after dusk
Something small and black was eating the lamp-flames. When I killed them they fled as smoke, south, toward the old cistern outside the city.
Lamp-Eater
Fight off the shadows snuffing out the lamps
Descend into the Lightless Cistern
Child of the Great Dark
Cistern Spider
Kill the Namiira cultists
Mother Nhirra wore a lamplighter's ring on a cord around her neck. Zaba-jo's sister did not run away. She went looking for the dark, and found it, and became it.
Kill Mother Nhirra
She led the cult. She called herself Mother Nhirra.
Nhirra. Their mother's name. So she took it into the dark with her. ...Thank you for the truth. It is heavy, but it is shaped like something, at least.
She was a prisoner there. She died fighting them.
Fighting. Yes, she always fought. Zaba-jo will light a lamp for her on every street. Every one.
Zaba-jo can see it on your face. Tell him. Tell him how she died.
Return to Zaba-jo
I found the cult in the cistern. I found your sister.
It is very heavy for something so empty. Zaba-jo will break it on the temple steps at dawn, where the moons can watch it break.
Give Zaba-jo the black lamp to be smashed
This is what drank your lamps.
Why light the lamps twice?
A cult of Namiira in Torval's old cistern was swallowing the city's lamps and its lost people. Its Mother was the lamplighter's own sister.

Because they go out, walker. Not blown out. Out, as if something drank the flame. Three street-cats are gone from the low quarter, and two beggars, and Zaba-jo's sister has not come home in a month. People whisper Namiira. Zaba-jo would rather whisper nothing at all.
Lamplighter's Hood
The Hungry Dark
story.skycraft.q.side_els_the_keepers_li: In the dead lighthouse on Senchal's south rocks I found the keeper's last log. Twenty years ago he put out the light for a ship with serpent sails.
A rain-swollen logbook on a lectern in the dead lighthouse. The last entry is twenty years old: 'Serpent sails, green lamps. She asked for me by name. I put out the light. Forgive me, Shirra.'
Find the wreck the keeper wrote about
Wait until the green lamps are lit
Put down the drowned Maormer crew

Velethis was a Maormer raider who paid the keeper to douse his light so her ship could slip into Senchal unseen. The keeper doused it, then fled before she could pay him in blades instead. The rocks took her ship either way.

He ran. Shirra waited twenty years for a father who was afraid to come home. ...But he wrote her name in the last line. Shirra will light the south rocks again herself. Someone in this family should keep the light.
Bring the log to Shirra in Senchal
Your father put out his light for a Maormer raider. Then he ran.
The keeper of the South Rocks Lighthouse doused his lamp for a Maormer raider and fled. Captain Velethis and her drowned crew are at rest, and Shirra will keep the light herself.
story.skycraft.q.side_els_the_scaled_man: Jo'zhirr the Old Claw of Riverhold warned me about the Scaled Mane, a dragon-cult remnant digging in the northern dunes of Anequina, where the sand smokes at night.
Find the cult's camp in the northern dunes
The chanters at the camp were only the outer circle. Their maps all pointed north, to a ridge they called the Aerie, where their High Whisker sings over a buried dragon.
Kill High Whisker Zahjarr before the song ends
Zahjarr died with the last verse in his mouth, and it was enough. The bones he had been singing to for a lifetime were not Alkosh's. They belonged to a dragon who woke up hungry and very annoyed.

A real dragon. Jo'zhirr said stupid; he did not say dangerous. He should have. Old Claw is too old. Here: take this from his hoard, and tell no one that Jo'zhirr was wrong. Ha. Tell everyone. It is a good story.
Bring the bone shard to Jo'zhirr in Riverhold
The cult woke something. It was not Alkosh.
The Scaled Mane sang a dragon awake in the northern dunes of Anequina, believing it was Alkosh. Morvunrah the Ash-Wing is dead again, and the cult's song is over.

A cult, walker. Old, stupid, stubborn. They wear dragon scales and say Alkosh was a dragon who learned to be a cat. Fine, says Jo'zhirr, believe what you like. But now they dig in the northern dunes, and the herders say the sand there is warm at night, and smoking.
story.skycraft.q.side_els_the_sweet_tide: The man behind the grey sugar is Dro'sakhar Sweet-Tooth, a skooma lord who runs a pirate fleet out of Senchal. The wharf-warden of Senchal may know where to find him.

In Sugar-Smoke Cove, south along the shore, where the cliffs hide the lanterns. His crews are not sailors, walker. They are farmers who owe him. He takes the field, then he takes the farmer. Remember that when you draw steel.
Speak with Ahnissi, the Wharf-Warden of Senchal
Where does Sweet-Tooth anchor?
Find Sugar-Smoke Cove after dark
Wait for the skooma barges to come in at night
Ahnissi was right. The enforcers fought; the deckhands mostly dropped their clubs and ran into the dark. Sweet-Tooth keeps his skooma in a sea-cave further west.
Sweet-Tooth Enforcer
Debt-Sworn Deckhand
Fight off Sweet-Tooth's enforcers on the beach
Enter Sweet-Tooth's hold in the sea-cliffs
Sugar-Mate
Kill Captain Dro'sakhar Sweet-Tooth
Lose it in the harbor. They were his prisoners, not his crew.
Then the tide takes it. Ahnissi will tell the magistrate the book was very wet. Go well, walker. Senchal is sweeter for you.
Keep it. The worst of them deserve a magistrate.
The worst of them, yes. Ahnissi will read carefully and be fair. That is harder than hanging, but she is paid for hard.
Ahnissi could hang every name in this book on a hook for smuggling. Or she could lose it in the harbor, and Pellitine would have a great many farmers again by spring.
Bring Sweet-Tooth's ledger to Ahnissi
Sweet-Tooth is dead. This ledger lists everyone who owed him.
Dro'sakhar Sweet-Tooth is dead in his sea-cave, and the ledger that bound half of Pellitine's farmers to his skooma barges is in Ahnissi's hands, or in the harbor.
Sweet-Tooth's Hook
The Sweet Tide
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_sand_in_the_shr: I found an opened grave among the caravan burials outside Skaven. Whatever left it walked out on its own.
The grave has been opened, but not by a robber: the dirt was thrown outwards, from below. The shroud lies empty beside it, still tied at the feet.
Then someone is doing the vilest thing a Redguard can do to another. Tu'whacca forgive them, because I will not. Shepherds saw lamps at Faugta's Guard, the old shrine to the south-west. Go.
Tell Qadira, the keeper of the last rites in Skaven
One of the caravan graves outside town is empty. It was opened from the inside.
Go to Faugta's Guard
Risen Caravaneer
Shrouded Bones
Lay the risen caravaneers back down
Bahzir had been raising the dead of the Ninth Caravan massacre one by one, trying to make them name their killers. His own father was among them.
Kill Bahzir the Gravewright
Take Bahzir's ledger
Burn it. Nothing good comes of words like these.
Then the dead keep their secrets, as they should. I'll say the rites over the ashes.
Give it to the town watch. The killers should hang.
Justice bought with necromancy. I don't like it, but I like murderers walking free even less. The watch will have it by nightfall.
Names wrung out of the dead. And some of them, I'd wager, belong to men still drinking in this town. What do you want done with it?
Bring word to Qadira in Skaven
Bahzir is dead. He kept a ledger of what the dead told him.
Bahzir the Gravewright is dead and the caravan's dead lie still again. His ledger answered the question nobody in Skaven wanted to ask.
Tu'whacca's Rest
Sand in the Shroud
