story.skycraft.q.side_hf_small_footprint: At a drowned slipway east of Taneth, a child left a sandal and a scratched message: Tariq was here, and something about a ferry.
A child's sandal is tied to the urn with fishing twine, very neatly, as if left on purpose. Scratched in the clay beneath: TARIQ WAS HERE. THE FERRY.

That's his! I tied that knot myself. He went to the school-ferry eight days ago with the other net-children and never came back. Sabir the ferryman said he ran off. Sabir has rowed our children for twenty years.
Is your boy called Tariq? I found his sandal at the old slipway east of town.
Follow the ferry route south to Brine Hollow
Kill the slavers guarding the pens
The slavers' master was Sabir the ferryman, the man Taneth trusted with its children. He had been selling them a few at a time to galleys out of the southern sea.
Kill the man who sold the children
Oh, my boy, my clever boy. He left you a trail, didn't he? Of course he did. Take this, it was his father's. He'd want it carried by the one who brought our son home.
Here's Tariq. The other children are on their way back with the fishing boats.
Sabir the ferryman is dead and the net-children of Taneth are home. Tariq's sandal did more than any watchman.
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_the_ancestors_j: Jazira at-Kherun of Sentinel asked me to bring her the sword of her ancestor Sahrazad, a Ra Gada warrior buried in a tomb in the Alik'r Desert.
Find the Tomb of Sahrazad in the desert south-west of Sentinel
Someone had been here before me. The burial niches were pried open and the gold was gone, but the guardians were still keeping their oath.
Put down the oathbound guardians of the tomb
Wait in the burial hall until nightfall
The shade of Sahrazad judged me with her sword and then with her tongue. She said Jazira had already sold the tomb's gold, and that the blade was mine, not hers.
Prove yourself against the shade of Sahrazad
Sahrazad spoke to me. She knows you sold her funeral gold, and she gave the sword to me.
She... spoke? No. No, that's a story. Fine. Keep the cursed thing. I'll explain to the Crowns that my ancestor prefers strangers.
The tomb was robbed. The sword's gone with the gold.
Robbed. Of course it was. Well, I suppose the robbers did me the courtesy of not bringing it to my door. Here, for your trouble.
And? You're holding something under that cloak. Is it her sword? Let me see it.
You said your family had a sword-singer at every wedding. What happened?
Sahrazad of the Ra Gada weighed me in her tomb and found me worth her sword. Whatever Jazira believes, the blade that came ashore with the first ships hangs at my side now.

We ran out of weddings and money in that order. Out in the Alik'r lies the tomb of Sahrazad, our foremother, who came ashore with the Ra Gada. Her sword was buried with her. Bring it to me and the at-Kherun will have something to show the Crowns besides debts.
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_the_lantern_cis: Huzayra Quickpurse, a thief of Taneth, hired me to steal an old Hew's Bane scimitar from the merchant Ozan bel-Rihm's cistern vault north-west of the city.
Find the Lantern Cistern north-west of Taneth
Wait until the watch changes after dark
The scimitar in the case was a gilt forgery. The real blade was hidden behind it, with a note from Huzayra: I was meant to take the fake and be caught with it.
Open the display case in the vault
Huzayra's partner Sarrah was waiting at the cistern mouth to make sure I was caught red-handed, or not caught at all.
Survive the ambush on the way out
Sarrah? I... well. Clever boots. Very clever boots. I suppose we'll call this square, and I suppose you'll tell me which blade you're really carrying some other day.
Give Huzayra the scimitar she expects
Here's your scimitar. Sarrah sends her regards. From the bottom of the cistern.
You notice boots. What else do you notice?
Huzayra planned to sell me to the watch along with a forgery. She got the forgery. I kept the real Hew's Bane scimitar.

I notice that Ozan bel-Rihm, the richest fat man in Taneth, keeps an old Hew's Bane scimitar in a cistern vault north-west of the city, and that his watchmen drink. I need quiet boots to walk in at night and walk out with it. Half the fence price is yours.
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_the_last_dispat: A waystone in Bangkorai bears a garrison's old plea for relief, and a bitter answer scratched under it. Thornwatch Garrison lies somewhere to the south-west.
Cut deep under the moss: THORNWATCH HOLDS. SEND RELIEF. Beneath it, in fresher, shallower letters, someone has added: They never did.
Find Thornwatch Garrison
Stay until dark, when the garrison wakes
Unrelieved Sentry
Frozen Picket
Fight past the unrelieved sentries
When Rasheen fell, a sealed dispatch dropped from his belt. It was the request for relief he had sent with a courier. It had never left the garrison.
Lay Captain Rasheen to rest
Thornwatch. My great-grandfather was its courier. The family story says he rode through the snow and the relief came too late. This seal was never broken. He never rode at all, did he?
Carry the dispatch to Commander Veshra in Elinhir
This is from Thornwatch Garrison. It's very late.
Enter it in the garrison rolls. Let the truth stand, even about your family.
Then it goes in the rolls tonight, under my own name. Rasheen's men held their post. The record will say so.
Read their names at the waystone and let the dispatch burn with them.
An old soldier's funeral. I'd like that. I'll ride out with you at dawn.
Either way I can't give them back their lives. But I can give them something.
Decide with Veshra what to do with the dispatch
What will you do with it?
Captain Rasheen and his men waited a century for relief that was never asked for. Their last dispatch has finally been delivered.
Thornwatch Half-Helm
The Last Dispatch of Thornwatch
Lady Nahrin at-Selem of Sentinel fears her son Fahim has fallen in with the Selenu, the old vampire bloodline of the Sentinel coast. She asked me to follow him by night and bring him home.
Fahim was already gone when I arrived. A beggar on the steps said he walked west along the shore, toward the old drowned palace.
Wait for nightfall outside the at-Selem house in Sentinel
Follow Fahim to the Drowned Court on the western shore
Selenu Courtier
Selenu Thrall
Cut through the Selenu courtiers
Ushara fell into the black water of her own stair. Fahim was alive in the inner hall, pale and confused, but not yet turned.
Destroy Ushara the Tide-Pale, matriarch of the Selenu
Bring Fahim home to Sentinel
Fahim deserves to know why they came for him.
Yes. He does. It will be the worst conversation of my life, and I have had some bad ones. Thank you for bringing him back to have it.
The debt died with Ushara. Let it stay buried.
Then I will carry it alone, as I always have. Take this. My husband's, from the Order of the Candle. It was always meant for someone braver than him.
When I was younger than he is now. I was dying of the wasting cough and they offered me years. They wanted my first child in return. I thought, if I never told anyone, it would never come due.
Speak with Lady Nahrin
Fahim is home. The matriarch said you made a bargain with the Selenu once.
Your son keeps late hours?
Ushara the Tide-Pale is ash in her drowned palace, and Fahim at-Selem sleeps at night again. The debt his mother made with the Selenu is settled, if not forgotten.

Fahim leaves at dusk and comes home at dawn, with sea-salt on his boots and no colour in his face. He says the sun shouts at him. I know what that means. Every family in Sentinel knows. Follow him tonight and bring him home.
Candlewake
The Pale Court
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_the_salt_terrac: Ansei Turaz al-Hadi, an old sword-singer of Sentinel, asked me to be his champion in a duel of honour against Khalid of the Nine Cuts on the Salt Terrace east of the city.
Go to the Salt Terrace by daylight, as the duel law demands
Khalid yielded with my blade at his throat. Then he told me Turaz had been paid to lose their first duel, and gave me a bookmaker's slip to prove it.
Defeat Khalid of the Nine Cuts in the ring of blades
Then pay the rest. Go to Khalid and tell him yourself.
Yes. Forty years late, but yes. Take the blade of my school. I am not fit to keep it until I've done this.
This stays between us. Burn the slip.
You are kinder than I deserve. Kinder than Khalid would like, too. Take the blade of my school, and do not let it learn my habits.

Ah. I wondered if he had kept it. I was young, my mother was sick, and a fat man in the market offered more than a year's teaching for one bad afternoon. I have been paying it back in shame ever since.
Confront Ansei Turaz with the wager-slip
Khalid yielded. He also gave me this. It has your name on it.
Forty years of practice. Do you still teach?
I won Turaz's duel and learned why he lost his own. The school's old shehai blade is mine now, given by a man who finally knows what it cost him.

I teach. I do not duel, not any more. Khalid of the Nine Cuts beat me forty years ago and took my student's sword as forfeit, and now he has challenged my school again because he knows my hands shake. The old law lets me name a champion. Stand for me on the Salt Terrace.
A Duel on the Salt Terrace
Ilvane Courtic, a Breton scholar in Elinhir, asked me to retrieve a tonal key-cylinder from the Dwemer ruin of Mzindhal. Her partner Eriq was lost there last season.
Go to the Dwemer ruin of Mzindhal in the Craglorn hills
Mzindhal Spider
Mzindhal Sphere
Destroy the ruin's waking automatons
Hall Ballista
Take the tonal key-cylinder from the inner hall
Behind the Warden I found Eriq Dannel in a humming brass cage. He said Ilvane had shut it on him herself, so she could publish the discovery alone.
Destroy the Warden of Mzindhal
Get Eriq safely back to Elinhir
The key goes to Eriq. The discovery is his as much as yours.
Of course it does. Take what I promised you and go. I'd rather not have a witness here when he comes in.
Pay me double and I'll forget what Eriq said.
You're no better than I am. That's oddly comforting. Double it is.
He... it was the cage or both of us, the Warden was coming, I... No. That's not true and you'd know it. I wanted my name on that door. Just mine.
Confront Ilvane Courtic
I have your key-cylinder. I also have Eriq, alive. He says you locked him in.
A Dwemer ruin that sings in the right key?
The Warden of Mzindhal is scrap and Eriq Dannel walked out of the ruin he was left to die in. The tonal key unlocked more than a Dwemer door.

Mzindhal, in the hills north of Elinhir. My partner Eriq and I opened its outer doors last season. Then the guardians woke, and Eriq didn't come out. I need the tonal key-cylinder from its inner hall, and I need someone who can deal with whatever is guarding it.
Resonant Maul
The Tonal Lock of Mzindhal
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_the_web_of_anke: Bashir the Long-Eyed, a hunter of Skaven, wants help killing a sand serpent in the Singing Dunes and clearing a nest of giant scorpions at the Web of Anker.
Track Old Saltback into the Singing Dunes
Old Saltback came up out of the sand right under my feet. I cut the venom sac out of it, as Bashir asked.
Old Saltback
Kill the sand serpent Old Saltback
Go to the scorpion nest at the Web of Anker
Anker Brood
Clear the young scorpions from the nest
Around the brood-mother's den lay crates of goat meat, nailed shut and stamped with an apothecary's brass tag. Someone had been feeding the nest.
Kill the brood-mother, Anker
Take it to the town watch. People could have died.
People did, last spring, two drovers. I'll walk it over myself. Here's your half of the bounty, and a bow I've no more use for.
Sell Hadir the venom sac and let him know we know.
Hah. You've a merchant's heart. He'll pay double to keep this quiet, and he'll never feed another nest. I'll take my cut.
That's Hadir's mark. The apothecary. He buys scorpion venom by the jar and sells it to the Imperials as medicine. He must have decided wild scorpions were too slow.
Bring the venom sac and the feed-tag to Bashir
Saltback and Anker are both dead. And somebody's been feeding that nest. Here's the tag off their crates.
Seen anything worth hunting out there?
Old Saltback and the brood-mother Anker are dead, and the apothecary who fed the nest has been found out, one way or another.

Worth hunting? Two things. A sand serpent the drovers call Old Saltback has been swallowing goats whole in the Singing Dunes north of here. And scorpions as long as a cart have nested in the Web of Anker to the north-east. They're breeding faster than anything should. Help me with both and I'll split the bounty.
Stingbreaker
The Web of Anker
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_two_flags.desc: Neyra Sail-Mender of Stros M'Kai says pirates pressed her husband Jafar into service. She thinks they shelter at Gullwhistle Cove.
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_two_flags.o0.re: Gullwhistle? Nothing there but gulls. These raiders come from the open sea, and they fly honest flags to get close. I keep my ledger, I warn the captains. What more can one man do?
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_two_flags.o0.te: Ask Harbourmaster Hamid about the pirates
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_two_flags.o0.to: Neyra says pirates took her husband. What do you know about Gullwhistle Cove?
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_two_flags.o3.jo: Ishraq's tide-ledger listed every merchant sailing for a month ahead, copied from the harbour register in Hamid's own neat hand.
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_two_flags.o4.te: Bring Jafar back to Stros M'Kai
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_two_flags.o5.c0: Take the ledger to the town's elders. Let them deal with him.
They'll put him in the stocks and then on a boat, and good riddance. Thank you. Thank you for Jafar.
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_two_flags.o5.c1: Let me have a quiet word with Hamid. He'll pay you back every coin.
Quiet words. Well, the coin would feed us through the winter. Just make sure he knows that we know.
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_two_flags.o5.re: Hamid? Hamid who ate at our table every feast day? Gods, he sold us all. What do we do with him?
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_two_flags.o5.to: Jafar's home. And the pirates' sailing dates were copied from the harbourmaster's ledger.
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_two_flags.outro: Captain Ishraq is dead, Jafar Netmaker is home, and the harbourmaster's neat ledger turned out to be the pirates' best map.
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_two_flags.pitch: Pirates. They took my Jafar off his boat a month ago to row for them, and the harbourmaster says there is nothing to be done. Fishermen saw longboats at Gullwhistle Cove on the far side of the island. Bring him home and I'll mend every sail you ever own.
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_two_flags.title: Two Flags over Gullwhistle
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_two_names_one_w: Imran Bel-Tavir, a Forebear merchant in Rihad, believes the Crown family at-Senna burned his date grove at the Well of Two Names. He wants proof.
Burned? Three nights ago Bel-Tavir men beat my nephew Yusuf half to death on that same road. If we wanted war we would not start it with dates. Go and look, if you must.
Hear Maradh at-Senna's side
Imran Bel-Tavir says your family burned his date grove.
Go to the Well of Two Names west of Rihad
Hired Torch
Drive off the men camped among the burnt palms
Dabir carried two purses knotted together, one stitched with the at-Senna crescent and one with the Bel-Tavir scales. Both families' hotheaded sons had hired him, each to ruin the other.
Kill their leader, Dabir Cinderhand
Bring Maradh here. You two should hear this together.
Together. In the square, where everyone can see. Gods, my father will spin in his tomb. Very well.
Keep the purses. They're a good lever if the at-Senna move again.
A Forebear answer. I'm almost proud of you. Almost.
My Karim? That... I would like to call you a liar. I find I can't. What happens now is a question for old men and old women.
Return to Imran Bel-Tavir in Rihad
Your son paid to have the at-Senna's nephew beaten. Their nephew paid to have your grove burned. Same man did both jobs.
A grudge older than your figs?
The burning of the Bel-Tavir grove was paid for by both families at once. What Rihad does with that truth is up to its elders now.

Older than my grandfather. The at-Senna are Crown, we are Forebear, and we have shared the Well of Two Names since before Rihad had a wall. Last week someone burned my date grove beside it. Old Maradh at-Senna will deny it to your face. Go and look at that well, and tell me who did it.
Well-Warden's Scimitar
Two Names, One Well
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_where_the_star_: Bahrun the Star-Reader of Elinhir says a fallen star in Starfall Hollow is maddening shepherds and drawing living storms. He wants it dealt with before the Elinhir mages get to it.
Go to Starfall Hollow
Walking Storm
Star-Mote
Disperse the storm-things circling the hollow
The thing that came out of the glass called itself Vharzul. When it broke apart, the whole hollow rang like a struck bell.
Destroy Vharzul, the Fallen Light
Take the shard from the heart of the hollow
Drop it down the well. Some doors stay shut.
Good. Come, we'll do it at dawn, when the stars can see us do it. They'll remember you kindly.
Sell it to the mages. Let scholars worry about it.
Scholars. Yes. Scholars always worry about the right things. Go on, then. Don't come to me when it starts talking to them.

Of course it does. It is a splinter of something the stars locked away, and it wants out. The Elinhir mages would pay a fortune for it. My grandmother's grandmother would have dropped it down the deepest well in Craglorn.
Bring the shard back to Bahrun in Elinhir
The storm-thing is dead. The shard still whispers.
The sky is writing back?
Vharzul, the Fallen Light, is gone, and the shard of the fallen star has gone where I chose to send it. Craglorn's sky is quiet again, for now.

Nine nights ago a star fell into the hollow south-east of Elinhir. The shepherds who went to see it came back speaking a language nobody taught them. Storms walk there now on legs. My family has read the sky for a hundred generations, and we have a word for this. The word is 'no'.
Starsplitter
Where the Star Fell
story.skycraft.q.side_hf_witches_of_devi: Grandmother Nisha, an apothecary of Rihad, is one of the Witches of Devilrock. She wants me to break the Mother-Stone of the rival Mountain Witches, which she says has poisoned Devilrock's spring.
Climb to Devilrock in the Dragontail Mountains
Find the Mother-Stone of the Mountain Witches
I made a promise. The stone comes down.
Then my stone-wife will have something to say about that.
Devilrock lied to me. Your stone stays.
Then Devilrock will send someone to finish the job. They always do. Stand with me.
Their spring poisoned itself, child, when they cut it a new channel through our dead. The stone keeps our dead from walking. Cut it, and you will see what Devilrock really wanted.
Speak with the old woman at the Mother-Stone
Devilrock says your stone poisoned their spring.
Whichever coven I crossed, it sent its champion at me before the dust had settled. The Dragontail witches do not leave a debt unpaid for long.
Face the witch who comes for you
So it is. The mountain heard, and the mountain will remember. Here. A witch's thanks is a small thing, but it keeps.
Return to the witch whose side you took
It's done.
What's the something you mentioned?
I chose a side in the old quarrel between the Witches of Devilrock and the Mountain Witches. The Dragontail will be talking about it for a generation.

The something is my sisters' gratitude, and it's worth more than gold in these mountains. We are the Witches of Devilrock. The Mountain Witches have set their Mother-Stone above our spring and turned the water foul. Climb to Devilrock, take what my sisters give you, and cut that stone.
Hagthorn
Thorn and Stone
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_a_favour_for_gl: Goodwife Wenna Thrale, an herbalist of Daggerfall, sent me to the Glenmoril Witches in their grove north of the city. They have a favour to ask.
Find Glenmoril Grove north of Daggerfall
Find the witchfinder's camp east of the grove
Witchfinder's Torchman
Fight off the witchfinder's men
Ser Aldous carried a writ with a list of women he had burned. The last name on it was Isolde Thrale. Thrale, like Wenna.
Kill Ser Aldous Mire
Bring the captive witch back to Glenmoril Grove
Go and see her. She's alive, and she's family.
Yes. Yes, I think I will. Even if the priestess frowns.
Your secret is safe with me.
I hope so. Daggerfall is a small city with a long memory.

My daughter. She ran to the grove at fifteen and I told everyone she'd drowned. I couldn't walk into that camp, not with half of Daggerfall watching me. Thank you. The coven keeps its bargains. So do I.
Tell Wenna in Daggerfall the favour is done
The witch the coven wanted saved was called Isolde Thrale.
Nothing a priestess would frown at. And something she would?
I saved Isolde Thrale from the witchfinder's pyre and returned her to the Glenmoril Witches. The coven owes me a summoning, and her mother owes me the truth she finally told.

You've a sharp ear. There's a grove north of the city where some old women live who know more than herbs. The Glenmoril Witches. They have a favour to ask, and I can't do it myself. Go to them, do what they ask, and I'll owe you more than coin.
Glenmoril Yew
A Favour for Glenmoril
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_cinderwick.desc: Magister Prosper Allard of Evermor says his apprentice Linnet lost control of a flame atronach, which is now burning Brindlecombe Farm in Stormhaven.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_cinderwick.o0.t: Go to Brindlecombe Farm south-west of Evermor
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_cinderwick.o1.t: Put out the lesser fires that have taken shape
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_cinderwick.o3.j: Linnet sent the atronach on purpose, to burn the debt ledgers of Allard's own brother, a moneylender who ruined her family.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_cinderwick.o3.r: I didn't lose hold of it. I sent it here. This farm belongs to the Magister's brother. He lends to farmers and takes their land when the harvest fails. He took ours. I wanted his ledgers to burn. The barn just... came with them.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_cinderwick.o3.t: Cinderwick's gone. You can come out.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_cinderwick.o4.r: Edric's ledgers. Of course. Half these farmers came to me begging, and I sent them away because family is family. Linnet will be punished for the barn. Edric will be punished for the rest, if I have anything to say about it.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_cinderwick.o4.t: Bring what's left of the ledger to Magister Allard
Linnet's safe. She sent the atronach after your brother's debt ledgers. This is what survived.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_cinderwick.offe: Your apprentice set a farm on fire?
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_cinderwick.outr: Cinderwick is banished and Brindlecombe's barn is ash. So are most of the debts that ruined half of Stormhaven's farms, and Magister Allard has decided he can live with that.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_cinderwick.pitc: Not personally. She summoned a flame atronach in my workroom, lost hold of it, and it walked out of the door and down the road to Brindlecombe Farm, south-west of here. It's still there, burning. Linnet ran after it. Please bring her back, and preferably not the atronach.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_on_viles_day.de: The Glenmoril Witches are paying their debt. Mother Brannagh will summon the Daedric Prince Clavicus Vile for me on his summoning day, at his shrine east of Camlorn.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_on_viles_day.o0: Meet Mother Brannagh at the shrine of Clavicus Vile east of Camlorn
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_on_viles_day.o1: Clavicus Vile came to the coven's call, as cheerful as a moneylender. His price: the death of a man named Marrowgate, who had made a wish of him and somehow cheated him.
Wait for the summoning hour at nightfall
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_on_viles_day.o2: Find Marrowgate at the Gallowmoor crossroads north of Camlorn
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_on_viles_day.o3: Marrowgate had wished never to die. Vile granted it and let him rot instead. He thanked me when it was over.
Give Hollis Marrowgate the death he wished away
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_on_viles_day.o4: Return to the shrine with Marrowgate's contract
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_on_viles_day.o5: I'll keep it. A gift is a gift.
So said Marrowgate. Mind how you go.
Give it to the coven. I don't want his favour.
Wise. We'll bury it under the oak where he can't hear it. Here, take this instead, from us.
Then it is, dear, and it's yours. The coven's debt is paid. Now, a word from an old woman: whatever he gave you, don't ever ask it for anything.
Vile says my reward is already in my pack.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_on_viles_day.ou: Clavicus Vile got his account settled and I got a Daedric Prince's gift. Mother Brannagh says the trick with Vile is not in the asking. It's in never asking twice.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_the_bell_ringer: Priestess Aline of Daggerfall asked me to find out whether Odo the Bell-Ringer, whose prophecies of fire keep coming true, is a true prophet or a fraud.
Odo swears he only dreams the fires. His latest dream was of an orchard, and a woman with his mother's eyes holding a tinderbox.
They do. I dream them. I don't want to. Last night I dreamed something new.
Speak with Odo the Bell-Ringer
The priestess says your fires always come true.
Search the ruins of Gaersmith Orchard east of the city
Fire-Ward Peddler
Deal with the fire-setters
Mabry Crowe was Odo's sister. She set the fires and sold the wards. But she swore with her last breath that she only ever burned the houses Odo had already dreamed.
Stop Mabry Crowe
Take him into the temple. Let someone help him with his dreams.
Kynareth's house has room for a man who hears too much. I'll see to it.
Let him keep warning people. Without Mabry, his warnings might save a house or two.
A prophet with no one to make his prophecies come true. That may be the best kind. Very well.
Then he's both. A fraud's pawn and a true dreamer. Gods, what a burden. What do we do with a man like that?
Tell Priestess Aline what you found
Odo's sister set the fires and sold the wards. But she said she only burned what he dreamed first.
Who is the Bell-Ringer?
Odo the Bell-Ringer dreamed of fires, and his sister made sure they came true. Mabry Crowe is dead, and Daggerfall has one less arsonist and one sadder prophet.

Odo. He rang the bells at Kynareth's temple until his dreams started. Now he stands at the well and names the next house to burn, and it burns. Half the city thinks he's a prophet and buys his painted fire-wards. Weigh him for me. Is he touched by the gods, or by something else?
Ash-Warden
The Bell-Ringer's Fires
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_the_dark_lamp.d: On the strand west of Daggerfall I found a dead man holding the key to Hawkston Tower, the old lighthouse to the north. The light has been dark for months.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_the_dark_lamp.f: A skeleton in a fisherman's smock lies above the tide line, one hand still closed around an iron key on a loop of tarred rope. The rope is stamped HAWKSTON.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_the_dark_lamp.o: Burn out the spiders nesting in the tower
In the Weaver's web hung the lighthouse keeper, Gerrold Hawke, wrapped tight but alive.
Kill the Weaver of Hawkston in the lamp-room
You'll answer to the magistrate in Daggerfall.
Aye. I suppose I've been waiting for someone to say it. Give me the key. I'll light the lamp one more time before I go.
Keep the light burning every night from now on, and I'll forget I heard this.
Every night. I swear it on every drowned sailor I owe. You won't find this tower dark again.

Gerrold Hawke. I'd thank you, but you'll find out soon enough and then you'll wish you hadn't bothered. The spiders didn't put the lamp out. I did. Every dark night for two years, for the wreckers on the strand. Their man came to pay me and the spiders got him on the way back.
You're the keeper? Hold still. I'll cut you down.
The Weaver of Hawkston is dead and the lighthouse burns again. Its keeper had been dousing it for wreckers, and now I am the only one besides him who knows.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_the_ferrygate_r: Warden Lucan Davette of Evermor wants a smuggling ring on the Bjoulsae broken. His men found their landing upriver.
Go to Reedwater Landing upriver from Evermor
River Tough
Drive off the river toughs at the landing
The manifest listed no crates at all. It listed families: Orc refugees from the Wrothgar clan wars, Reachfolk, others. And it pointed downriver to Ferrygate Cellars.
Search the landing for the smugglers' manifest
Follow the river south to Ferrygate Cellars

They're nobody's cargo. They're families that the Warden's toll would turn back at the border. I take a little coin to feed them and move them on to Wayrest. Hargrave runs the boats for me. Now, what will you do?
Speak with Mother Odile
These people are your cargo?
Hargrave had been selling Odile's ring to the Warden and Odile's passengers to slavers in Daggerfall, and taking money from both.
Hargrave's Oarsman
Stop Hargrave the Eel
Let her keep her boats. Better she moves them than the slavers do.
I never heard you say that and I never saw any boats. Here is the Crown's reward, for the slaver.
The law's the law. Arrest her, and see the families settled properly.
Properly. That'll take a clerk and a year. But it'll be done. You have my word, and the Crown's reward.
Refugees. And my own informant was the slaver. That's a fine thing to put in a report to the King. What do you want me to do with the old woman?
Report to Warden Davette in Evermor
The ring's broken. Their boatman was a slaver. The rest of them are refugees and an old woman feeding them.
What's floating past without paying?
The Ferrygate ring turned out to be a refugee road, and its boatman a slaver. Hargrave the Eel is dead, and the Bjoulsae is a little cleaner.

Boats, at night, without lamps. Somebody's running cargo down the Bjoulsae past Evermor and paying nobody. My men found a landing upriver where they put in. Find out who's behind it and break it up, and the Crown's reward is yours.
Ferrywoman's Knife
The Ferrygate Ring
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_the_held_door.d: A Direnni carving on a cairn in northern Rivenspire points west to Ennhalwe Spire, where an elven sorcerer is said to keep something.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_the_held_door.f: Elven letters, still sharp after three thousand years, run around the stone in a spiral. Someone has scratched a Breton gloss beneath in charcoal: 'Ennhalwe, west. The Direnni sorcerer keeps it. Do not wake him.'
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_the_held_door.o: Find Ennhalwe Spire to the west
Climb to the top of the spire
Saerendil Direnni was not hoarding treasure. He had made himself a lich to hold a door shut, and I had just killed him.
Kynval Ashmaw had waited three thousand years for Saerendil to let go. He had a few minutes of freedom. I made sure of that.
Kill the dremora that climbed out of the floor

Let me see. Violet ink, very old Direnni hand. 'I will hold, though my house falls and the Bretons forget us.' He held it for three thousand years, alone. And you killed the dremora that came through? Then perhaps it ends well. Here, this was in the spire's inventory, according to his own list. It's yours by right.
Take Saerendil's journal to Magister Corwen in Shornhelm
I found this at Ennhalwe Spire. The Direnni there was holding a gate shut. He isn't any more.
Saerendil Direnni held a Daedric door shut for three thousand years. I ended him, then ended what came through. His warhammer is mine now, and his journal is in Magister Corwen's keeping.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_the_heron_and_t: Dame Orlaith Vane, last Knight-Warden of the Order of the Heron, asked me to keep vigil at the order's ruined chapterhouse in Stormhaven and find Chrysamere, the blade her grandfather stole.
Go to the ruined Heronmere Chapterhouse in Stormhaven
At the end of my vigil a voice spoke from the empty altar. It named itself Sir Malcor Vane and told me to seek him at Castle Copperston.
Keep vigil before the stone heron
Relic-Hunter
Relic-Hunter Archer
Drive off the relic-hunters drawn by the voice
Go to the crypts of Castle Copperston to the south-east
Oathbound Heron
Put down the knights who followed Malcor into the dark
Sir Malcor took Chrysamere because the order meant to sell it to pay its debts. He died guarding it and was still guarding it when I came.
Face Sir Malcor Vane
I'll kneel. Let the Heron fly again.
Rise, Knight of the Heron. You are the whole order now. Try to do better than the last lot.
Let the order rest. Malcor earned that much.
Perhaps you're right. Then carry the blade as he would have: for no one's coin. Keep the seal. Someone should.
So the shame was ours, not his. All these years. He gave you the blade, you say? Then the Heron has chosen. Kneel, if you would. It's the last thing I can give.
Return to Dame Orlaith in Wayrest
Your grandfather didn't steal Chrysamere for himself. He took it to stop the order selling it.
The Order of the Heron? I've never heard of it.
Chrysamere, the Paladin's Blade, has come out of Castle Copperston in my hands. Sir Malcor Vane's name is clear, and the Order of the Heron has had its last word.

Few have, now. We were a small order, like the Owls of Glenpoint or the Ravens of Dwynnen. Our grandmaster carried Chrysamere, the Paladin's Blade, until my grandfather Sir Malcor vanished with it and the order died of shame. I'm too old to find it. Keep vigil at our chapterhouse in Stormhaven, and see if the Heron still answers.
The Heron and the Blade
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_the_lady_on_the: Bertrand Lorne of Shornhelm has inherited Lornhallow Manor and the ghost of his great-aunt Ysmay. He wants the house cleared so he can sell it.
Go to Lornhallow Manor north of Shornhelm
Ysmay was not haunting the stair. She was guarding the cellar door, against whatever her husband left down there.
Wait on the stair until midnight
Go down into the cellar and put down the restless servants
Lord Garamond murdered his wife and walled the servants who knew into the cellar. Ysmay held the stair against him for sixty years.
Destroy the ghost of Lord Garamond Lorne

Gods. And the family has toasted Great-Uncle Garamond every Saturalia for sixty years. Well, no more. The sword is yours. It was his, and I'd rather it went to someone who's done something decent with a blade.
Bring Ysmay's ring to Bertrand in Shornhelm
Your great-aunt is at rest. Her husband killed her. She was keeping him in the cellar.
A ghost? What sort of ghost?
Lady Ysmay Lorne has left the stair at Lornhallow, and her murderer has left the cellar. The Lorne family sword has finally gone to someone the family can be proud of.

My great-aunt Ysmay. Murdered by persons unknown, the family history says, sixty years ago. She stands on the stair of Lornhallow Manor, north of Shornhelm, every night at midnight, and no buyer will come within a mile. Make her go away and the family sword is yours. I'm no swordsman anyway.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_the_red_wool_be: A totem in the Wrothgarian Mountains bears the red wool of the Daughters of Wroth and a plea: the Lyrezi vampires have taken Castle Mastercroft.

A skull wound in red wool hangs from the totem with a clapperless bell. A strip of bark is tied beneath it: 'The Lyrezi have Mastercroft. Whoever reads this, come to the Hearth. West, then north. - M.'
Find the Hearth of the Daughters in the north-west of Wrothgar

Mastercroft was ours for two hundred years, until an elder of the Lyrezi walked in one winter and made it a feasting hall. Turn her out of it, and the Daughters will brew you something kings would kill for. That is a coven's bargain. It is a good one.
Speak with Sister Morwen of the Daughters of Wroth
I found your totem. The Lyrezi took Mastercroft?
Go to Castle Mastercroft
Lyrezi Guest
Lyrezi Hound
Cut through the Lyrezi feast-guests
Countess Ilsabet was once a Daughter of Wroth, Morwen's own elder sister. She still wore the coven bell around her wrist, with the clapper torn out.
Destroy Countess Ilsabet of the Lyrezi
Take the bell. Hang it at the Hearth where she started.
Then she comes home, after a fashion. Here is the Daughters' brew, as promised. Drink it in a dire hour and not before.
I'll bury it at Mastercroft, where she chose to be.
Where she chose. Yes. That's fair, and it's cruel, and it's right. The Daughters' brew is yours.

She was. She left to live forever and came back to eat the women who raised her. I sent a stranger because I couldn't lift a hand to her myself. Give me her bell, or keep it. I find I don't know which I'd rather.
Return to Sister Morwen
Ilsabet is dead. She said you were her sister.
Countess Ilsabet of the Lyrezi is destroyed and Castle Mastercroft belongs to the Daughters of Wroth again. Two sisters' quarrel ended with a stranger's blade.
Mastercroft Bell-Breaker
The Red Wool Bell
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_the_vraseth_sup: Brother Tobias of Camlorn fears that the noble Morvayne family of Dunmoor Hall have been taken by the Vraseth, the vampire bloodline of Glenumbra.
Go to Dunmoor Hall west of Camlorn
Wait for the household to wake at nightfall

Grandfather. He died before I was born. I found his letters in the crypt and they were so kind, and the door wasn't even locked. He said he only wanted to see the family again. Now Mother and Father don't eat, and he sends me to bed early.
Speak with the young Lady Morvayne
Your parents aren't sleeping, are they? Who's coming up the stairs?
Lord and Lady Morvayne
Vraseth Servant
Fight past the turned household
Follow Aubert Morvayne to the family crypt
Aubert Morvayne is ash. His granddaughter let him in out of loneliness, and the rest of the family paid for it.
Crypt Thrall
Destroy Aubert Morvayne, eldest of the Vraseth

A child who missed a grandfather she never met. Stendarr have mercy, it's always love that opens the door. I'll go to her myself and see what can be saved. Take this for your trouble. It was blessed for a better day than this.
Bring the Morvayne signet to Brother Tobias in Camlorn
The Morvaynes are gone, all but the youngest. Their grandfather came back from the crypt. She let him in.
Camlorn could use more mercy?
Aubert Morvayne of the Vraseth is destroyed and Dunmoor Hall stands empty. Celestine Morvayne will grow up knowing what her loneliness cost.

Dunmoor Hall, west of the city. The Morvaynes were faithful to Stendarr for three generations. This year they stopped coming. Their cook left without her wages. Their stable-boy didn't leave at all; we found him in a ditch with no blood in him. I fear the Vraseth, and I am too old to go and look.
Stendarr's Late Mercy
Supper at Dunmoor Hall
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_thunderheels_gr: Stonewright Gashna gra-Ulfim of Orsinium says a giant called Thunder-Heel is attacking the haulers who take stone from an old cairn south of the city for Orsinium's walls.
Go to the Cairn of Thunder-Heel south of Orsinium
Thunder-Heel would not be calmed. When he fell, the stone he had been cradling rolled out of his lap. It was carved with an orc's hand beside a giant's foot.
Take the carved stone from the cairn

In the old orc records carved over the gate of Old Orsinium I found it: King Gortwog paid the giants of the cairn for passage through their valley, and swore that no orc would move a stone of their dead.
Search the ruins of Old Orsinium for a record of the pact

An oath of Gortwog's, broken by my own crews. Malacath's teeth. Thunder-Heel was guarding his dead, and we called him a beast for it. The stones go back, every one, if I have to carry them myself. And this, which the King kept in the vault with Gortwog's pact-papers, you've earned more than any of us.
Bring the pact-stone to Gashna in Orsinium
That cairn was a giants' grave. Gortwog swore the orcs would never touch it. This stone was his oath.
Grommoth Thunder-Heel died guarding his people's graves against a broken orcish oath. Gashna is taking the stones back, and King Gortwog's hammer has come out of the vault to me.

The wall needs stone. South of the city there is an old giants' cairn, beautiful dressed stone, nobody using it. So we used it. Now a giant called Thunder-Heel smashes our carts and has killed two haulers. The King wants him dead. I want to know why a giant cares about a pile of rocks.
story.skycraft.q.side_hr_very_good_handw: Master Tobin Vauclair, a wool merchant of Wayrest, says his son Remy was kidnapped for ransom. He thinks the gang hides in the old Hawkford ruins north of the city.
Go to the Ruins of the Old Hawkford Hovel north of Wayrest
Kill Cutwater Jessamy, the gang's leader
The kidnapping was Remy's own plan, written in his own good hand. His hired kidnapper had simply decided to make it real.

No. Embarrassed. I wrote the ransom note. I needed the money to marry Aveline, and Father would never allow it. I hired Jessamy to play the kidnapper. Then she decided she liked the idea of the money and of keeping me.
Your father sent me. Are you hurt?
That's... that's Remy's hand. The little fool. He could have asked me. No. No, he couldn't, could he. I'd have said no. Well. I suppose I had better meet this Aveline.
Return Remy and the ransom note to his father
Here's your son. And here's the note. Look closely at the handwriting.
Do I have children? Is something wrong?
Remy Vauclair's kidnapping was his own idea until his hired kidnapper improved on it. He is home, and his father has agreed to meet the girl he nearly died for.

My son Remy. Taken from the street outside our warehouse four nights ago. The note wants five thousand drakes. I'll pay it, gods help me, but I don't trust them to give him back. The watch says the gang uses the old Hawkford ruins north of the city. Bring my boy home.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_ash_on_the_wind: Meralyn Hlervu of Ald'ruhn lost a silt strider, its caller and her strongbox to an ash storm on the Falasmaryon track. She thinks the strider was steered wrong on purpose.
Find the stranded strider on the Falasmaryon track
Drive off the beasts circling the strider

Our guide, a woman with a burned hand, made me leave the track when the storm came. Shelter, she said. Then she cut loose the pack-guar with the strongbox and walked into the ash. Raiders came at dusk. They went east, toward Mausur.
Speak with Galos the caller
Galos? Meralyn sent me. What happened out here?
Follow the raiders to Mausur Caverns
Ash-Hand Raider
Fight through the raiders
The raider chief's right hand was burned to the wrist. Meralyn's guide and the Ash-Hand were the same woman.
Ash-Hand Raider
Defeat the raider chief
Recover Meralyn's strongbox
Still locked. Good Hlervu work. Galos sent word the strider is walking again, slowly. I'll be hiring my own guides from now on, from people I've known since they were eggs.
Return the strongbox to Meralyn in Ald'ruhn
Your strongbox. And your guide won't be hiring on again.
Which strider didn't come home?
Galos brought the strider home on foot, singing to it the whole way. Meralyn says it now refuses to leave the track for anyone.
The one with my caller Galos on it, and my strongbox, and eight passengers. An ash storm caught them on the Falasmaryon track three days ago. Striders don't get lost, sera. Somebody steered it wrong.
Caller's Ash-Coat
Ash on the Wind
Cassia Ventrilla of the Balmora excise office wants a Khajiit sugar-runner named J'darr stopped at the Bitter Coast cave of Shal, and she does not want him brought back alive.
J'darr is a bondsman of the sugar-factor Fendryn Llaro, and he gave me Llaro's ledger. Cassia Ventrilla's name is in it every month.
Find J'darr at the cave of Shal
Sugar-Guard
Drive off the guards sent to silence the runner
Track Llaro to his cookhouse in Yasamsi
Skooma Cook
Sugar-Guard
Put out the skooma fires
Fendryn Llaro is dead among his own pots. J'darr's debt died with him.
Deal with Fendryn Llaro
It goes to the Legion at Ebonheart.
Then I hope they pay you as well as Llaro paid me.
Your purse is a good start.
Here. Burn it where I can watch.
Ah. Well. A soldier's pay doesn't stretch far in Balmora. What will it take to make that book disappear?
Settle things with Cassia Ventrilla
I found J'darr. I also found Llaro's ledger, with your name in it.
Any work for someone who doesn't mind mud?
J'darr sent word from Hla Oad that he has bought a fishing boat. He named it after me, which is either a kindness or a warning.

A Khajiit runner named J'darr carries moon-sugar up from the Bitter Coast. He makes his drop at a cave called Shal. Catch him there and see he doesn't run again, if you take my meaning. The Empire pays for results, not for prisoners.
J'darr's Thanks
Sugar and Salt
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_the_bloom_of_te: Faldrys Uvel, steward to the Telvanni wizard Uvren Falavel, says an experiment escaped the growth-vats at Tel Ravani. He wants it found and quietly destroyed.
Search Uvren Falavel's tower, Tel Ravani
The day-book belonged to Velsa Taren, Falavel's apprentice. She volunteered for 'a small graft'. The entries grow shorter, then stop.
Vat-Room Warden
Search the vat-room for notes
The specimen is Velsa. She did not escape; Falavel threw her out. She begged me to report her dead.
Follow the spore-trail to the grove
Falavel's Leash
Falavel's Leash
Fight off the hunters Falavel sent after her
The hunters were only a signal. The binding-rune Falavel carved into her finished the job they started. There was nothing left of Velsa to save but a seed.
Grove Sprout
Free Velsa from the binding
Take Velsa's heartseed
Plant it in the grove where she wanted to stay.
I'll do it myself. And I'll keep my master's books more carefully, for anyone who asks. Take this from his vault. He won't miss it; he never understood it.
Put it on Falavel's desk with her day-book.
He'll have me flayed. Good. I'd like to see his face first. Here, from his vault, before he locks it.
Velsa. I sent her her post every week. He told me she'd gone home to Tear. Give me the seed. What do I do with it?
Report to Faldrys Uvel in Sadrith Mora
Your master's specimen was his own apprentice. He threw her out and then sent atronachs to finish her.
Your master must keep you busy.
A Telvanni master tried to grow something new and made a victim instead. Tel Ravani's vats are dry now, and the grove by the sea is quietly, slowly thinking.

Master Uvren Falavel keeps me busy, and today he keeps me worried. While he sits at council, something has broken out of his growing-vats at Tel Ravani. He says a 'specimen'. He says it quietly. Find it, destroy it, and nobody in Sadrith Mora need ever ask what it was.
The Bloom of Tel Ravani
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_the_boy_and_the: Near Ald'ruhn I found a child's note: a boy named N. had gone after a guar called Scuttle. The tracks lead west into the Ashlands.
Chalked on a flat stone in a child's careful letters: 'Gone to bring Scuttle home. Back by supper. Don't tell Mama. N.' Small footprints and a guar's three-toed tracks lead off toward the west.
Inside the cave I heard a guar bleating and a boy shushing it. I also heard something much larger breathing.
Follow the tracks to the cave called Milk
Kill the young kagouti in the outer cave
Kill the Tusk-Mother before she finds the boy
I'm Nilvyn. Scuttle was my papa's guar. Papa's gone, and Scuttle ran off, and Mama said we'd have to sell him anyway. I wasn't going to let a kagouti eat him first.
You must be N. Your mother's looking for you.
Bring Nilvyn and Scuttle home to Ald'ruhn
Nilvyn! You foolish, wonderful... I'll not sell Scuttle. His father would haunt me. Take this, sera. It was my husband's, and he would want it used.
Nilvyn's home. So is the guar, limping a bit.
Nilvyn now walks Scuttle around Ald'ruhn on a rope twice as long as it needs to be.
The Boy Who Followed the Guar
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_the_brass_tithe: Brucius Allene, a salvager in Balmora, says a Dwemer machine from Arkngthand is carrying his salvage back into the ruin. He wants it broken.
Follow the drag-marks to Arkngthand
Arkngthand Spider
Arkngthand Sentry
Clear the ruin's waking sentries
The tally-plate lists everything Brucius's crew took. The machine has struck each item off as it brought it home. Only one remains: a regulator coil.
Take the brass tally-plate from the sorting hall
The Steam-Warden was not raiding anyone. It was taking back what was stolen, and it died one coil short.
Bring down the Steam-Warden
Then you'll seal what's left of the ruin and leave it be.
Fine. Fine! There are other ruins. Probably with fewer opinions.
Your business. Pay me and we're done.
A practical sort. I like you. Here, the best of the haul.
Sold, last month, to a Telvanni buyer who didn't haggle. Don't look at me like that. It was a machine guarding an empty house.
Confront Brucius with the tally-plate
Your 'abandoned scrap' was a working warden's inventory. Where's the coil?
Your crew looks like it's been chased by something.
Somewhere in Telvanni country a stolen Dwemer coil is humming in someone else's machine. I suspect I'll hear of it again.

Chased is the word. Something big and brass walked out of Arkngthand, flattened my wagons and carried my salvage back in. The Dwemer are gone, so it's a machine with no master, and machines can be broken. Break it, and I'll pay what the scrap's worth.
The Warden's Due
The Brass Tithe
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_the_gray_lanter: On a reef in Sheogorad I found a drowned sailor who wrote that the light he followed was wrong. A gray lantern burns in an old tower to the north.
A sailor's bones on the rocks, still clutching a broken spyglass. Scratched on the brass: 'Followed the light. The light was wrong.' Out to the north, an old tower burns with a gray flame.
Reach the tower of the Gray Lantern
Fight off the cliff racers nesting on the tower
Lantern-Wrecker
Salvage Boss
Clear out the wreckers
Lantern-Wrecker
Defeat the lantern-keeper
Twenty years of wrecks, kept in a fisherman's tidy hand. The first page is signed: Bolvyn, son of Hjal, of Dagon Fel.
Take the keeper's ledger
Tell her the truth.
So I've been mourning the man who drowned the others. Give me the book. Every family in Dagon Fel deserves to read their page.
Tell her he died a keeper, trying to save ships.
A keeper. That's like him. Thank you, outlander. Here, it isn't much.
Had. He drowned twenty years back, the night the north boats went down. Why have you got his writing?
Bring the ledger to Hjolfrid Salt-Eye in Dagon Fel
Did you have a brother named Bolvyn?
The Gray Lantern is dark now. Ships out of Dagon Fel are steering by the stars again, which is how it should have been all along.
Wrecker's Reckoning
The Gray Lantern
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_the_last_sleepe: Near Sharapli under Red Mountain I found an ash-statue offering and a letter from someone named F. to an Aldam. The Sixth House is gone, but somebody is still dreaming its dreams.

A small ash-statue with a face pressed into it, set on a stone and ringed with burnt-out candles. Tucked beneath it is a letter: 'Aldam, the dreams have stopped being dreams. Don't look for me. F.' The ash-statue's eyes are wet.
Enter Sharapli
Ash Ghoul
Dreaming Sleeper
Break the sleepers' circle
The journal belongs to Fenas Rothri, brother of the Balmora apothecary Aldam Rothri. He came to Red Mountain to cure his dreams and found a cult willing to finish them.
Take the journal from the sleepers' shrine
I sold him draughts for the dreams for a year. I thought they were working. Maran-Adon, the last pages say. Bring him home. Whatever's left of him, bring it home.
Bring Fenas's journal to Aldam Rothri in Balmora
Your brother Fenas. He's with what's left of the Sixth House.
Go to Maran-Adon on the slopes of Red Mountain
Ash Ghoul
Ash Slave
Cut through the Ash-Kin's guard
Dagoth Thelvas was Fenas Rothri. The cult did not take a captive. It made a new kinsman out of a man who couldn't sleep.
Destroy Dagoth Thelvas
He said your name at the very end.
Then I'll stop selling dream-draughts. They never worked anyway. Take this. He'd want it used against them.
The cult is broken. Others may still be dreaming.
Then I'll watch my customers' eyes. Take this, and go armed.
He said my name? Then some of him was still there. Some of him was still mine.
Tell Aldam how his brother ended
I found Fenas. I'm sorry. There wasn't enough of him left to bring home.
The Mountain's heart is long gone, but its dreams outlived it. One of them had my friend's brother's face.
The Last Sleeper
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_the_oath_under_: Outside Ebonheart I found a Pact memorial with one Nord name gouged out. Frost clings to the gap. Something about it pointed me west, to the old Pact Cairn.

A weathered memorial stone with the three-headed seal of the old Ebonheart Pact. Three columns of names were carved here. One Nord name has been chiseled out so hard the stone is cracked. Fresh frost rimes the gap, though the day is warm.
Visit the Pact Cairn in the Stonefalls
Follow the frozen bootprints to the old barrow
Fight through the barrow's oath-sworn dead
The ring bears a Dunmer captain's mark as well as Hjorvald's. Someone of the Pact took his oath, then took his name.
Carve Hjorvald's name back into the stone.
I'll do it myself, and put the captain's beside it with the truth. History should be uncomfortable.
Leave the stone as it is. The dead are quiet now.
Quiet isn't the same as right. But I'll keep the ring, and the story.
That captain's mark... he was the hero of the Stonefalls muster, by the histories. The histories may need correcting.
Bring the oath-ring to Ungrid Ash-Born in Ebonheart
This belonged to a Nord whose name was cut off the Pact stone. I think he was wronged.
A Nord who kept his word was cut from the stone by a Dunmer who didn't. Three peoples swore that oath; it took a stranger to finish it.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_the_quiet_cup.d: Saryne Dalvilu, a palace scribe in Mournhold, believes a royal food-taster was poisoned through wine from the old Deshaan cellars, and that the steward is covering it up.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_the_quiet_cup.o: A weak heart. It happens. The palace does not need strangers stirring up talk of poison. Good day.
Question the palace steward, Dethan Raloth
About the taster who died last week.
Search the old Deshaan wine cellars
Cellar Thug
Cellar Watcher
Deal with the cellar's new tenants
The orders are written in a palace cipher, in a fine scribe's hand. They name a safehouse: Villa Dralor.
Find the poisoner's orders
Vireth the Quiet Cup is dead. With her last breath she told me to ask the scribe who writes her orders. Saryne sent me to tidy up her own loose end.
Find the poisoner at Villa Dralor
Now the steward reads your orders.
Raloth will bury it to save face. But you're welcome to try.
Now you pay me twice what you paid her.
Done. I do admire practical people.
Because Vireth was getting greedy, and you were available. The taster was a mistake; the cup was meant for someone who deserves it. So. What now?
Confront Saryne Dalvilu
Your cipher. Your hand. Your poisoner. Why send me?
You look like someone with a secret.
In Mournhold, the scribes write the history and occasionally the obituaries. I know which one I nearly ended up in.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_the_quiet_cup.p: Everyone in the palace has one. Mine is that a food-taster died last week, and the steward has ruled it a weak heart. It wasn't. The wine came from the old Deshaan cellars. I can't be seen asking. You can.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_the_razor_that_: I found a Daedric altar near the ruin of Ald Kharvenu in Molag Amur, still wet with something. The ruin belongs to Mehrunes Dagon, and it was waiting for me.

A black altar set alone in the scrub, its candles burning without wax. A thin groove runs across the stone, the exact shape of a razor's edge, and it is wet. Beyond it, the ruin of Ald Kharvenu seems to lean toward you.
Return at night, when the ruin wakes
The shard cut me through the cloth of my pack. The cut won't close. The Daedra-hunters of Necrom will know what to do with it.
Take the razor-shard from the altar
Brave, or foolish. Here's your share. Don't come crying when the Telvanni buyer turns up headless.
A piece of Dagon's Razor, or something that badly wants to be. I can break it on a Temple anvil, or I can sell it to a Telvanni who wants to bleed slowly. Your shard. Your choice.
Take the shard to Tarvyn Faleran in Necrom
This came from Ald Kharvenu. It's cursed, and it's cutting me.
Ald Kharvenu is quiet now. In Necrom, Tarvyn swears the anvil he broke the shard on still bleeds on Sundas mornings.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_the_unquiet_fer: Hlavora Selvani, a priest of Necrom's dead, says corpses are walking out of the lower ossuaries. All the coffins come through Mourners' Landing.
The 'dead' are not dead. A man woke in his coffin, drugged with embalming tea. The seal on his coffin belongs to the Necrom embalmers.
Inspect the coffins at Mourners' Landing
Ferry Warden
Fight off the ferry's wardens
Master Varyn's seal. He embalms half of Necrom. If he is sealing the living into the ossuaries, he is doing it for someone who wants them pliant. Go below, and be careful of what you find awake.
Show Hlavora the embalmer's seal
Your walking dead are living pilgrims, drugged and coffined. This seal was on the lid.
Descend into the lower ossuaries
Hollow Mourner
Get past the hollow mourners
Varyn was making thralls of the pilgrims he coffined. The ones who woke early were the ones whose tea he'd watered down to save coin.
Stop Master Embalmer Aldos Varyn
As what he was. Put his name on the gate.
Every embalmer in Necrom will read it on the way to work. Good.
Quietly. The city needs to trust its dead.
A kind lie. Necrom is full of them already. Take this, for your silence.
Then we wake the ones we can and bury the rest honestly. How shall Necrom remember him?
Tell Hlavora what Varyn was doing
Varyn is dead. The ossuaries are full of half-made thralls.
What troubles the City of the Dead?
In the City of the Dead, it turned out the danger was a man who couldn't wait for people to die.

The dead have begun walking out of the lower ossuaries at night, and none of my rites will keep them in. They come up the steps blinking, sera, as if confused. The coffins all pass through Mourners' Landing first. Start there.
Embalmer's Hook
The Unquiet Ferry
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_two_herds.desc: Drulvos Hleth, a netch herder in the Grazelands, is feuding with the Mavrin family over a shared spring. Each blames the other for netch going mad.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_two_herds.o0.re: Then why does my bull come back from the spring frothing? Why did Old Thundergut stave in my barn? The Hleths want the whole spring. Go and look at it yourself.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_two_herds.o0.to: Drulvos Hleth says he didn't touch your herd.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_two_herds.o1.jo: Someone has been tipping gall-root into the spring. It drives netch mad. Neither family would poison its own water.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_two_herds.o4.jo: The gall-root came from the Setus mine. Its overseer wants the spring for a new kwama shaft, and two feuding families make for easy buyers of a cheap pasture.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_two_herds.o4.te: Search the Setus Egg Mine for the poisoner's supplies
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_two_herds.o5.c0: Share it, like your grandfathers did.
Orvesa will hate that. So will I. We'll manage.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_two_herds.o5.c1: The Hleths. You asked for help first.
Ha! I'll send her a fair price. Probably.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_two_herds.o5.c2: The Mavrins. They lost a barn.
You're a hard judge. She did lose a barn. Fine.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_two_herds.o5.re: The mine. Forty years of shouting at the wrong family. Well, someone has to have the spring now. Who?
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_two_herds.o5.te: Tell Drulvos Hleth who poisoned the spring
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_two_herds.o5.to: It wasn't the Mavrins. The Setus mine poisoned the spring to drive you both off.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_two_herds.outro: Two netch-herding families, one spring and a kwama mine that thought they'd be easy. They weren't, in the end.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_two_herds.pitch: Trouble with Mavrins, which is worse. Since spring their bull netch have gone mad and wrecked my fences, and Orvesa Mavrin swears my family did it. My grandfather and hers shared the spring between us for forty years. Go and talk sense to her. She won't hear it from a Hleth.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_two_herds.title: Two Herds, One Spring
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_wax_and_shell.d: Bralsa Teleri, a wax merchant in Sadrith Mora, lost six harvesters at the dreugh cove of Nallit on Azura's Coast.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_wax_and_shell.o: Go to the cove at Nallit
Dreugh eggs, six of them, packed for market. The harvesters weren't scraping wax. They were robbing a nest, and the mother followed.
Shell-Mother Kharr is dead. The cave held what was left of the harvesters, and nothing else.
Face the Shell-Mother in her cave
Sell them, and pay your harvesters' families out of it.
That is... fair. Expensive, but fair.
Nothing. I'm taking them back to the sea.
Then I've lost six harvesters and a fortune. Go on, then. The sea's welcome to them.
Dreugh eggs fetch ten times what wax does at a Telvanni table. Of course I knew. What do I do with them now?
Bring the crate of eggs to Bralsa
Your harvesters died robbing a dreugh nest. Did you know?
Bralsa still sells dreugh wax. She has stopped asking her harvesters where it comes from, and they have stopped telling her.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_wax_and_shell.p: Six of them went down to the cove at Nallit on Azura's Coast to scrape dreugh wax. None came back. Dreugh are nasty but they are stupid, and my people know their work. Find out what went wrong, and bring back whatever wax you can.
story.skycraft.q.side_mw_what_the_dead_s: Ervyn Sandas of Vivec is haunted in his dreams by his grandsire Dravil, who claims he was murdered. Ervyn asked me to visit the Sandas Ancestral Tomb.
Dravil's shade says his brother Ulvon poisoned him. He wants Ulvon's bones taken from the Othrelas tomb and scattered in the ash.
Enter the Sandas Ancestral Tomb
Sandas Bonewalker
Calm the restless Sandas guardians
Go to the Othrelas Ancestral Tomb
The widow's letter tells it plainly. Dravil poisoned his brother's wife for her dowry, and Ulvon killed him for it. Dravil wants Ulvon's bones gone because they are what keeps him shut in.
Othrelas Guardian
Open Ulvon's urn
Return to the Sandas tomb after dark
Dravil came at me with every lie he had left. When he broke, the tomb went quiet in a way it had not been for sixty years.
Sandas Bonewalker
Put Dravil's shade down for good
Read him the widow's letter.
So the murderer was the one asking for justice. Ulvon gets a lamp at our shrine from now on, and Dravil gets none.
Tell him Dravil found peace, and burn the letter.
Peace. Good. Then I can mourn him properly. Thank you, sera.
Tell me. I have been afraid of him for a month. I would rather know why.
Tell Ervyn what his grandsire was
Your grandsire won't visit again. But you should know what he wanted.
Your grandsire visits? Isn't he dead?
Two brothers, one tomb's worth of grudges. The Sandas house sleeps now, and Ervyn with it.

Very. Dravil Sandas, dead these sixty years. He comes in my sleep and tells me he was murdered, and that I must set it right before he can rest. I am a clerk, sera, not a hero. Would you go to our tomb and hear him out?
What the Dead Say
story.skycraft.q.side_pya_the_serpents_h: Gwaelin Saltbelly of Woodhearth says a sea serpent ridden by a Maormer herald has sunk seven fishing boats this season.
Sail south to the herald's coast on Pyandonea
Survive Vorrhaal the Old Coil
Woodhearth sawdust in the empty nests. Someone in my own harbor has been stealing serpent eggs, and the herald came to take them back.
Find the serpent rookery in the cove
Coil-Guard
Fight the herald's guard
Kill Iriel Wave-Rider
Take the egg Iriel recovered from Woodhearth
Hang the harbor master's name in the market and send the egg home.
Both. Today. Let the sea see we can be honest too.
Raise it. Woodhearth could use a guardian of its own.
A serpent of our own... The elders will howl. I like it.
The harbor master's crates. He swore they were Elsweyr melons. By the Pact, we'd have eaten a serpent egg if we'd known. Hungry or not, a stolen egg is a stolen child.
Bring the egg back to Gwaelin
This egg came from Woodhearth's harbor. Your people stole them first.
The sea is eating your boats?
The boats of Woodhearth fish again, and nobody in the harbor will touch a crate of 'melons'.

A serpent the length of the harbor wall, with a Maormer riding on its neck like a stable-boy on a pony. Seven boats this season. Our hunters say kill the rider and the beast goes home. Our hunters are very hungry. So are we. Sail south and kill the rider.
Old Coil's Scale
Wave-Rider's Harness
The Serpent's Herald
story.skycraft.q.side_pya_through_the_mi: Lieutenant Calaenor of Alinor wants the Maormer mist-lantern, which lets ships pass through the fog that hides Pyandonea.
Sail through the mist wall to Pyandonea
Fight the Maormer raiders on the beach
Take the mist-lantern from its coral post
Here. Do what you will with it.
Adequate work. The fleet sails within the season. You may go.
I broke it on the way back. The mist stays.
You... broke it. How regrettable. Take your fee and leave my sight before I find a law you've broken.
Ancient history, embellished by pirates. The lantern, please.
Return to Lieutenant Calaenor in Alinor
I have the lantern. The Tide-Singer told me why the mist exists.
I have seen the hidden coast of Pyandonea, and whether anyone else will depends on what I did with a blue glass lantern.

The Maormer hide their isles behind a wall of mist that no Altmer navigator has pierced in an age. Our agents report the Tide-Singers keep a lantern that parts it. Bring it to me, and the Sea Vipers will never again strike our coast from hiding. You will be paid as befits a minor instrument of Alinor's will.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_ashes_on_the_i: Ilvesi Dravyne of Winterhold asked me to recover her grandmother's ash-urn from the wreck of the Velothi Promise in Pilgrim's Trench.
Go to the wreck in Pilgrim's Trench
Drowned Pilgrim
Lay the drowned passengers to rest
Find the Dravyne urn in the hold
Captain Dren barred the hold from outside and took the only boat. The ice took him a few strokes from the wreck. He didn't stay at the wheel; he left everyone to die.
Take the ship's log from the captain's cabin
Silence Captain Dren's ghost
Ancestors be thanked. I will make her a shrine by the hearth. Did you learn how the ship was lost? The survivors never spoke of it.
Bring the urn to Ilvesi Dravyne
Your grandmother, Ilvesi.
He locked the hold and fled in the only boat.
Then the families of Winterhold will hear it, and his name will be cursed at every ash-shrine in Skyrim. That is justice of a kind.
The ice took them all. No one could have saved them.
Then it was the will of the sea. I can live with that. Perhaps it is better.
Tell me plainly.
Tell Ilvesi what the log says
The captain's log tells the story.
You seem troubled, serjo.
Ilmeni Dravyne's urn sits by her granddaughter's hearth in Winterhold. The Velothi Promise is sinking back under the ice.

Forty years ago the Velothi Promise ran aground in the trench below the ice, full of refugees from Morrowind. My grandmother's ashes were aboard, in the hold with the living. The ice shifted this winter, and the wreck shows again. I would have her back, and in a proper shrine.
Ashen Wake
Ashes on the Ice
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_coldveins_merc: In the snow outside Windhelm I found a frozen beggar, bled by a vampire and then carefully tended. The blanket came from the Grey Quarter's healer.

A man lies frozen under a thin drift, wrapped in a Grey Quarter blanket. Two small wounds on his throat have been neatly cleaned and bandaged. Whoever fed on him tended him afterward, and folded his hands.

He was dying already. Lung-rot. The Lady gave him a warm bed and a gentle end, which is more than this city ever gave him. You would rather he coughed his last in an alley? Go and see her, then. The old prison in the marshes south-west of here, past Mixwater Mill.
Ask the Grey Quarter healer about the blanket
This blanket is yours. The man wrapped in it was drained by a vampire.
Find the Lady's rest at the abandoned prison
Beside each name in Coldvein's book, the healer had written a diagnosis. Half of them were dockworkers, hale and strong. Nerasa had been sending her the healthy ones too.
Coldvein Thrall
Read the guest book by the door
Kill Lady Vigdis Coldvein
The Grey Quarter will judge you. I'll give them the book.
Then I'll stand there and let them. It's fair.
Burn the book. Spend the rest of your life healing for free.
Every day. Every patient. I swear it on my mother's ashes.
She said the strong ones lasted longer. That she could make them comfortable for weeks instead of days. She promised me... it doesn't matter what she promised. What will you do with me?
Confront Nerasa with the guest book
You sent her healthy men. It's in her book, in your hand.
The old prison is cold and empty again. In the Grey Quarter, nobody speaks of the Lady's rest.
Coldvein's Last Kiss
Coldvein's Mercy
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_salt_between_h: Ingrith Arnleif of Dragon Bridge says the Kolfinn family burned her timber, the latest blow in a twenty-year feud. She wants proof.
We didn't. But I'll not weep for it. Twenty winters ago their boys threw my Torvar off this bridge, and the river never gave him back. Ask them about that.
Ask Old Kolfinn about the fire
Did your family burn the Arnleif timber?
Search the riverbank below the burned woodpile
Follow the pitch-stained tracks to Pinemoon Cave
Saltcutter Smuggler
Fight off the smugglers in Pinemoon Cave
With Eldra dead, her lieutenant surrendered. He was Torvar Kolfinn, the boy who drowned twenty years ago. He burned the timber to keep the feud alive.
Kill Eldra Saltcutter
Both families should hear it. Today.
Aye. Let them all hear it. Maybe we can stop being fools together.
It's your family. You decide who hears it.
Then I'll go up to that cave myself. After that, we'll see.
Alive. And he let me spit at the Arnleifs every day for twenty years, so nobody would look at the water. My boy.
Tell Old Kolfinn his son is alive
Torvar is alive. He's been running smugglers past this bridge for twenty years.
Then who... No. Torvar? I was twelve. I cried for him. Gods, I cried for that boy.
Report to Ingrith Arnleif
The Kolfinns didn't burn your timber.
What happened to your woodpile?
Dragon Bridge has gone quiet, the way a house does after a long shouting match. The smugglers' boats no longer pass at night.
Somebody burned our seasoned timber, a whole winter's work. Everybody on this bridge knows it was the Kolfinns. Twenty years they've hated us. Find me proof, and the Jarl's reeve can deal with them.
Feudbreaker
Salt Between Houses
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_custodians: Corvin Vale, a Breton tinkerer at Nightgate Inn, woke a Dwemer centurion in Raldbthar. It walked out of the ruin and is crossing the Pale.
Find the centurion's trail near Loreius Farm
Destroy the machines trailing behind it
Ah. Well. There was a small brass key in a niche by its pedestal. I took it as a keepsake. You don't think it wants...? Oh. Oh dear. Please take it. Take it far away from me.
Ask Corvin why the machine is walking toward him
It isn't going to the farm, Corvin. It's coming for you.
Carry the key back to Raldbthar
The Custodian didn't want its key back. It wanted the thief, and to its mind anyone carrying the key was the thief.
Return the key to its niche beside the empty pedestal
I will never touch a Dwemer niche again. Probably. Here, take this. I made it from a centurion's spare knuckle. It seemed appropriate.
Your keepsake nearly flattened a farm. The key's back where it belongs.
The Custodian of Raldbthar lies in pieces at its post. Corvin swears he has given up Dwemer ruins for the study of moss.

I woke a Dwemer centurion in Raldbthar. Only for a moment! It was meant to recite its maintenance logs. Instead it walked out of the ruin, and now it is walking, very slowly, toward Loreius Farm, flattening whatever is in its path. I would very much like it to stop.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_false_beac: A watch-log near the Solitude lighthouse recorded a lantern burning where no lantern should be, on the headland above Broken Oar Grotto.

A lighthouse watch-log lies open on a rock, its pages flapping. The last three entries read the same: 'Lantern seen burning on the Broken Oar headland. No light should burn there. Reported to O.' The ink smells fresh.

That's my log! My boy Hakon keeps the night watch. Lights on Broken Oar, three nights? He never said a word to me. Two ships have gone on those rocks this season. Gods. Go and look, will you? I can't leave the oil.
Ask the lighthouse keeper about the log
Someone's been logging a false light on the Broken Oar headland.
Above Broken Oar Grotto a wrecker's lantern swung like a harbor light. The man holding it called himself Hakon.
Watch the Broken Oar headland after dark
Wrecker
Fight the wreckers in Broken Oar Grotto
Gunnhild's crew lured ships onto the rocks and sold the salvage to the smugglers of Haafingar. Hakon ran when she fell.
Kill Gunnhild Falsebeacon
Take the wrecker's lantern
He ran. If he comes back, it's for you to judge him.
Then I'll leave the door unbarred. And the lighthouse lit. He'll know which light is mine.
The Solitude guard should know his face.
...Aye. Two ships. Men drowned. I'll tell them myself.
Hakon's mark. I taught him to scratch it on his tools. He kept my lamp burning with one hand and that one with the other. Where is he?
Show Olfrid the lantern
This is the false beacon. There's an H scratched in the brass.
Only one light burns on the Haafingar coast at night now, and it is Olfrid's.
Lampwarden's Bow
The False Beacon
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_fellhammer: Sigrun of Winterhold says the dead garrison of Fort Fellhammer answers a roll call every night, and her father Asgeir's name is always called and never answered.
Be at Fort Fellhammer when night falls
Fellhammer Revenant
Put down the revenants of the garrison
The last real entry in the roll, in Hafgrim's hand: 'Six deserters sealed in the lower mine. Charges set. Let the mountain judge them.' Asgeir was the first name.
Take the garrison roll book from the commander's table
Behind the rubble I found six skeletons huddled together, and a Legion badge with Asgeir's name. They hadn't deserted. Their letters home were tucked in their boots, asking for leave that never came.
Search the collapsed mine behind the fort
Destroy Commander Hafgrim's shade
Strike his name from the roll. He's off duty now.
Struck. Let him rest. Let all six of them rest.
Write 'present' beside his name.
Present. He was always where he said he'd be. Thank you.
Sealed in. By his own commander. And for twenty years Hafgrim's ghost kept calling him absent, as if that made it his fault.
Bring Sigrun the garrison roll
Your father didn't answer because he wasn't on duty. He was in the mine.
Why avoid Fellhammer?
Nobody answers roll call at Fort Fellhammer any longer. The shepherds say the wind there sounds like ordinary wind now.

Every night the dead garrison of Fort Fellhammer answers roll call. Shepherds hear it on the wind. My father Asgeir served there before the mine fell in, and every night they call his name and he doesn't answer. I want to know why he can't rest when the others can't stop.
Roll-Caller
The Fellhammer Roll
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_grey_maw.d: Ulfgar Lean-Bow, a Falkreath hunter, thinks a werewolf is killing woodcutters and robbing the town's graves. He asked me to help him hunt it.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_grey_maw.o: Search for tracks around Half-Moon Mill
At the Lady Stone I found Ulfgar's brother Eirik, a werewolf by his own admission. He swore another wolf, Runa the gravekeeper, was the killer.
Follow the footprints to the Lady Stone after nightfall
...I knew. I think I knew when he stopped coming to supper. If he's still himself, even a little, I won't put silver in him. Find the one who made him.
Tell Ulfgar what you saw at the Lady Stone
Your brother Eirik is one of them.
Find the pack's den at Moss Mother Cavern
Greymantle Wolf
Kill the wolves of Runa's pack
Runa Greymantle had kept Falkreath's graveyard for twenty years, and fed her pack from it for the last one.
Kill Runa Greymantle
Send him north, into the empty country, far from anyone he could hurt.
North. Aye. He always liked the snow better than I did.
That's your choice to make, not mine.
Then I'll make it at the stone, where he can see the lake. Thank you for leaving it to me.
He's waiting at the stone. He said whatever I decide, he'll accept. That's worse, somehow.
Tell Ulfgar that Runa is dead
Runa is dead. What about Eirik?
What are you hunting?
The graves of Falkreath lie quiet again. Ulfgar doesn't talk about his brother, and I don't ask.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_grey_maw.p: Two woodcutters dead by Half-Moon Mill this month, and the graveyard dug up besides. Jarl says sabre cat. No cat I ever tracked opens a coffin. Come hunt with me, and bring something silver if you've got it.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_knock_belo: Hela Corundum-Hand of Darkwater Crossing says her night shift vanished in the new Veinhollow shaft after weeks of knocking from below.
Go down the Veinhollow shaft
Falmer Skulker
Kill the Falmer in the galleries
Someone had hammered a Dwemer resonance rod into the deepest gallery. The 'knocking' was the rod, ringing down into the dark. It called them up.
Pull the humming brass rod out of the gallery floor
That's the foreman's sounding rod. Bought it off a Markarth trader to find ore veins. He's been down there every night 'listening.' He went down with the night shift. Gods help him.
Show Hela the rod
Someone drove this into your floor. It's been ringing like a dinner bell.
Follow the Falmer tunnel to where it opens at Kagrenzel
The Gloomseer had been answering the rod's call for weeks, each night a little closer to the miners. Two of the night shift were alive in its larder.
Kill the Gloomseer who leads the raiders
Break it, and fill in the bottom gallery.
Rock and mortar, as deep as we can pour it. No more listening.
Keep it. If you hear it ring on its own, run.
Hmph. An alarm bell that answers back. I'll hang it over the shaft.
Two is more than I hoped. What do we do with that cursed rod?
Report to Hela at Darkwater Crossing
Two of your miners are coming home. The rest aren't.
Why is the new shaft closed?
The Veinhollow shaft is quiet now. Hela says the miners sing while they work, loudly, to drown out anything they might hear below.

We opened a new seam north of the crossing. Good corundum. Then the knocking started, from under the deepest gallery, steady as a heartbeat. Two nights ago it stopped, and the night shift didn't come up. Something else did.
Seam-Splitter
The Knock Below
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_lantern_sh: Three children have vanished from Rorikstead, the last of them Svana's daughter Hroa. The village blames the Khajiit caravan camped by the road.

Ri'shadi has heard what Rorikstead says. Rorikstead does not say that Ri'shadi saw a lantern of bone cross the fields at midnight, three nights running, going west. Small feet followed it. Ri'shadi did not follow. Ri'shadi is not brave.
Question the Khajiit trader Ri'shadi
Rorikstead says your caravan took their children.
Follow the lantern's path west to the Moldering Ruins
